items.name: Corollary (3.17): γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜)
items.statement: Standing notation (Chap. I §3, restated p. 233): K imaginary quadratic, discriminant D, 𝒪 = 𝒪_K, (D, N) = 1, D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), D ≡ square (mod 4N) (all p | N split in K); H = Hilbert class field, Cl_K ≅ Gal(H/K); u = #𝒪^×/2; t = number of prime factors of D; s = number of prime factors of N; Γ = Γ₀(N) ⊂ PSL₂(ℤ); 𝔥 = upper half-plane; R_N = (ℤ ℤ; Nℤ ℤ); m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; √D = i√|D|. For m ≥ 1, (m, N) = 1, r_𝒜(m) = 0, s > 1: γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) = −2u² Σ_{n≥1} δ(n) R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)), where R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) is the number of integral ideals of norm n in the genus {𝒜𝔫}.
items.note: No library; not planned for X₀(N) (nearest GZ.7, general; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/90). Consumed in §4 (Proposition (4.2)). Coefficients checked numerically (SCR/t_314.py, '(3.17) coefficient mismatches: 0'). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) versus R(n); genus-character form
items.statement: R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) is either R(n) or 0, where R(n) = Σ_{𝒜 ∈ Cl_K} r_𝒜(n) = Σ_{d|n} (D/d) is the number of integral ideals of norm n. If (n, D) = 1 then R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) may be replaced by R(n) in (3.17) (r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) ≠ 0 ⇒ (A(nN + m|D|)/p) = 1 ∀p | D ⇒ (AN·n/p) = 1 ∀p | D ⇒ R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) = R(n), A any integer prime to D that is a norm from the genus {𝒜}); in general δ(n)R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n)r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) may be replaced by ∏_{p|(n,D)} (1 + ε̂_p((nN + m|D|)/(nN))) · R(n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|), where ε̂_p is the character of the group of norms of fractional ideals with ε̂_p(N𝔞) = 1 for 𝔞 principal and ε̂_p(n) = (n/p) for n ∈ ℤ, p ∤ n.
items.note: Nearest: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:49 `NumberField.dedekindZeta (s : ℂ) := LSeries (fun n ↦ Nat.card {I : Ideal (𝓞 K) // absNorm I = n}) s` (R(n) as its coefficient, but no factorisation ζ_K = ζ·L(χ_D), i.e. no R(n) = Σ_{d|n}(D/d)); Tau Ceti GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:212 `genusCharFun (s : Finset ℤ) (n : ℤ) : ℤ` (genus characters on integers/norms). No stage plans R(n) = Σ(D/d) (ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 1 plans only norm-fibre coefficients). The replacement argument was checked by hand. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Hyperbolic distance on 𝔥 (quoted)
items.statement: The quantity 1 + |z − z′|²/(2yy′) is the hyperbolic cosine of the hyperbolic distance d(z, z′); |z − z′|/|z̄ − z′| = tanh(d/2); PSL₂(ℝ) acts by isometries, so a function of z, z′ satisfies a′) iff it is a function of d(z, z′).
items.note: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/Metric.lean:67 `UpperHalfPlane.cosh_dist (z w : ℍ) : cosh (dist z w) = 1 + dist (z : ℂ) w ^ 2 / (2 * z.im * w.im)` and :58 `UpperHalfPlane.tanh_half_dist (z w : ℍ) : tanh (dist z w / 2) = dist (z : ℂ) w / dist (z : ℂ) (conj ↑w)`; the instance `IsIsometricSMul SL(2, ℝ) ℍ` at :328 (unnamed instance). Same statements; the 'iff' (point-pair invariants are functions of d) is the standard transitivity of SL₂(ℝ) on pairs at fixed distance, not stated in Mathlib.

items.name: Archimedean part ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ of the height pairing
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Assume r_A(m) = 0, so that c and T_m d^σ have disjoint support. Define ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ := Σ_{v|∞} ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v, the sum over the h complex places of H of Néron's archimedean local symbols. Since Gal(H/K) ≅ Cl_K permutes these places simply transitively, ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ = Σ_{A₁, A₂ ∈ Cl_K, A₁A₂⁻¹ = A} ⟨(τ_{A₁,𝔫}) − (∞), T_m((τ_{A₂,𝔫}) − (0))⟩_ℂ, where τ_{A,𝔫} ∈ 𝔥 are the points of Chap. II §1 (roots of aτ² + bτ + c = 0 of discriminant D with N | a) attached to the class A and the ideal 𝔫.
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, first two displays, p. 248
items.note: Planned: GZ.2 'For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a number field, construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions … Prove the Faltings–Hriljac comparison for degree-zero divisors with the canonical Jacobian pairing … Export local height decomposition'. That plans the decomposition into local symbols in general; the rewriting over the h conjugate Heegner points is GZ-specific. Library: no local heights in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep localHeight/LocalHeight: none; 'Néron' in Tau Ceti occurs only in the elliptic-curve canonical-height files AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean and MordellWeil/*); library-coverage audit of GZ.2 (AUDIT-25): arithmetic intersection pairing 'absent'.

items.name: (4.1) Eisenstein series of Γ₀(N) summed over Heegner points
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let E(z, s) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\SL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s be the weight-0 Eisenstein series of SL₂(ℤ) (Γ_∞ = ±(1 *; 0 1); this normalization is the one forced by κ_N in (2.13) and by the identity 2^s ζ(2s) E(τ_A, s) = u|D|^{s/2} ζ_K(A, s) used on pp. 248, 252), E_N(z, s) the Eisenstein series (2.14) of Γ₀(N) at ∞, w_N z = −1/(Nz), Re s > 1. Then Σ_{A∈Cl_K} E_N(w_N τ_{A,𝔫}, s) = Σ_{A∈Cl_K} E_N(τ_{A,𝔫}, s) = N^{−s} Π_{p|N}(1 − p^{−2s})^{−1} Σ_{d|N} (μ(d)/d^s) Σ_{A∈Cl_K} E((N/d) τ_{A,𝔫}, s). For each d | N the points (N/d)τ_{A,𝔫} again satisfy quadratic equations over ℤ of discriminant D, and the inner sum is independent of d and equals Σ_{A} E(τ_A, s), where τ_A ∈ 𝔥 is any root of a primitive form of discriminant D in the class A. Hence Σ_A E_N(τ_{A,𝔫}, s) = N^{−s} Π_{p|N}(1 + p^{−s})^{−1} Σ_A E(τ_A, s) (the combination used in the display at the top of p. 249).
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, (4.1) and the paragraph after it, p. 248
items.note: Checked: if aτ² + bτ + c = 0 with a = Na₁ and τ′ = (N/d)τ, then a₁dτ′² + bτ′ + (cN/d) = 0, of discriminant b² − 4ac = D; the first equality is (2.16) applied termwise; Σ_{d|N} μ(d)d^{−s} = Π_{p|N}(1 − p^{−s}) gives the last form. Searched: Mathlib/Tau Ceti have only holomorphic Eisenstein series (Mathlib `eisensteinSeries`, NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/Defs.lean:205, weight k level N); no non-holomorphic E(z, s). Atlas: AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.1 plans general Eisenstein-series convergence on reductive groups ('Prove absolute convergence of the Eisenstein sum over P(F)\G(F) …'), not this CM-point identity; no stage mentions E(z, s) at Heegner points. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Partial zeta function ζ_K(A, s) of an ideal class
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic, A ∈ Cl_K and Re s > 1: ζ_K(A, s) = Σ_{𝔞 ⊆ O integral, [𝔞] = A} N(𝔞)^{−s}. One has Σ_{A∈Cl_K} ζ_K(A, s) = ζ_K(s), the Dedekind zeta function of K.
items.note: Library: Mathlib has only the full Dedekind zeta `NumberField.dedekindZeta` (NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:49: `LSeries (fun n ↦ Nat.card {I : Ideal (𝓞 K) // absNorm I = n}) s`), not the class-restricted series; grep partialZeta/classZeta in both libraries: none. Atlas: no stage plans ideal-class partial zeta functions (AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 plans Hecke/Dedekind interfaces generically; Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields Layer 3 plans ray-class ideal counting with error term, not the zeta function). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Eisenstein series at a CM point equals a partial zeta function
items.statement: Let τ_A ∈ 𝔥 be a root of a primitive positive-definite binary quadratic form of discriminant D (K = ℚ(√D), u = #O_K^×/2) in the class A, and E(z, s) as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/94. For Re s > 1: E(τ_A, s) = 2^{−s} |D|^{s/2} u ζ(2s)^{−1} ζ_K(A, s); equivalently 2^s ζ(2s) E(τ_A, s) = u |D|^{s/2} ζ_K(A, s).
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, p. 248 ('As is well-known (and elementary)'); restated p. 252
items.note: Quoted as classical. Checked: ζ(2s)E(τ, s) = ½ Σ′_{(m,n)} y^s |mτ + n|^{−2s}; with a|mτ + n|² = Q(m, n) of discriminant D and y = √|D|/(2a) this is ½ (√|D|/2)^s Σ′ Q(m,n)^{−s}, and Σ′ Q(m,n)^{−s} = w ζ_K(A^{±1}, s) = 2u ζ_K(A, s) (ζ_K(A) = ζ_K(A⁻¹) by conjugation). Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (no non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, no partial zeta); no atlas stage plans it. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Factorization ζ_K(s) = ζ(s) L(s, ε)
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D and ε(n) = (D/n) (an odd primitive character of conductor |D|): ζ_K(s) = ζ(s) L(s, ε); near s = 1, ζ_K(s) = (1/(s − 1) + γ + O(s − 1))(L(1, ε) + L′(1, ε)(s − 1) + O((s − 1)²)), γ Euler's constant.
items.note: Planned only generically: AN.4 'Connect number-field ideal counting, Hecke characters and completed L-functions to the analytic class-number formula and Chebotarev'. No stage states the quadratic factorization explicitly. Library: absent — grep for products of riemannZeta with an L-function equal to dedekindZeta found nothing (the only hit, Mathlib NumberTheory/LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean:144, is an auxiliary function for Dirichlet characters); Tau Ceti has `dedekindZeta_eq_LSeries_normCoeff_one` (ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Trivial.lean:100), an L-series rewriting only.

items.name: Class number formula L(1, ε) = πh/(u√|D|)
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, class number h and u = #O_K^×/2: L(1, ε) = π h / (u √|D|) (= 2πh/(w√|D|)).
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, p. 249 ('and the formula L(1, ε) = πh_K/u√|D|')
items.note: Planned: AN.4 '… to the analytic class-number formula'. Library (partial, not the statement): Mathlib `NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT` (NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:77) proves (s − 1)ζ_K(s) → dedekindZeta_residue K = 2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂} R h/(w√|disc K|) (definition at line 56), which for imaginary quadratic K is 2πh/(w√|D|) = πh/(u√|D|); with the (absent) factorization PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/97 this gives the stated L(1, ε).

items.name: Proposition (4.2): archimedean contribution when r_A(m) = 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let x ∈ X₀(N) be a Heegner point for the full ring of integers of K, c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0), σ ∈ Gal(H/K), m ∈ ℕ prime to N, and A ∈ Cl_K the ideal class corresponding to σ under the Artin isomorphism. Suppose m is not the norm of an integral ideal in A. Then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ = lim_{s→1} [γ^m_{N,s}(A) − h σ₁(m) κ_N/(s − 1)] + h κ_N [σ₁(m)(log(N/|D|) + 2 Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1) + 2 + 2(ζ′/ζ)(2) − 2(L′/L)(1, ε)) + Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²)], where γ^m_{N,s}(A) is the invariant (3.3) (evaluated in Corollary (3.17)), κ_N = −12/[SL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)] = −12 N^{−1} Π_{p|N}(1 + 1/p)^{−1} (2.13), and L(s, ε) is the L-function of K.
items.note: Checked the derivation from Prop. (2.23), (4.1), PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/96–PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/98: the Eisenstein terms equal F(s) = 2^{2−s}|D|^{s/2}πu (σ₁(m) + m^s σ_{1−2s}(m)) ζ_K(s) / (N^s Π_{p|N}(1 + p^{−s}) ζ(2s)), whose polar part is −2hσ₁(m)κ_N/(s − 1) (residue 24hσ₁(m)/(NΠ(1+1/p))); its constant term together with −hσ₁(m)λ_N + 2hσ₁(m)κ_N and (2.21) gives exactly the printed bracket, the Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²) coming from (d/ds) log(σ₁(m) + m^s σ_{1−2s}(m)) at s = 1. Planned only as a method: GZ.7 'Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization'; GZ.8 'Specialize to X₀(N)' (of YZZ's formula). GZ's explicit evaluation through Kronecker/partial zeta functions (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/94–PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/98) is not itself planned. Library: none.

items.name: (5.1) Local symbol for divisors with a common point (tangent-vector symbol)
items.statement: Let X be a curve over the number field H, v a place of H, and a, b divisors of degree 0 on X whose supports meet exactly in the point x. Let g be a uniformizing parameter at x (a function on X with ord_x(g) = 1). Define ⟨a, b⟩_v := lim_{y→x} {⟨a_y, b⟩_v − ord_x(a) ord_x(b) log|g(y)|_v}, where a_y is the divisor obtained from a by replacing every occurrence of x by a nearby point y not in the support of b, and ⟨·,·⟩_v on the right is Néron's local symbol of relatively prime divisors. The limit exists by the standard properties of local heights ([14] = Gross, 'Local heights on curves').
items.note: Quoted from Gross [14]. Planned only in a different form: GZ.2 'Handle rational degree-one Hodge classes and self-intersections by a genuine regularization/intersection construction'; GZ.7 'Handle self-intersection terms and the normalized Hodge divisor'. YZZ regularise via the Hodge class, not via a tangent vector; Conrad (in the roadmap's source contract, Conrad §§2–10) re-derives (5.1) as Theorem 8.3 (conrad.txt p. 31). Library: none.

items.name: (5.2) Change of uniformizer; the sum of local symbols is the global pairing
items.statement: In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100: if g′ is another uniformizing parameter at x and g/g′ has the value α at x, then ⟨a, b⟩′_v = ⟨a, b⟩_v + ord_x(a) ord_x(b) log|α|_v. Consequently ⟨a, b⟩_v depends only on the non-zero tangent vector ∂/∂t at x determined by ∂g/∂t = 1, is unchanged if ∂/∂t is multiplied by a root of unity (|α|_v = 1 for all v), and — g being a single global function — Σ_v ⟨a, b⟩_v is independent of g and (product formula) equals the global height pairing of the classes of a and b [14].
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, (5.2) and the following paragraph, p. 250
items.note: Sign checked: with g′ = g/α + …, log|g′(y)|_v = log|g(y)|_v − log|α|_v. Agrees with Conrad (8.2) (conrad.txt p. 31), 'since our α is the reciprocal of that in [GZ]'. Planned as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100 (GZ.2 local height decomposition and regularized self-intersections). Library: none.

items.name: Dedekind eta function
items.note: Mathlib NumberTheory/ModularForms/DedekindEta.lean:60 `noncomputable def eta (z : ℂ) := 𝕢 24 z * ∏' n, (1 - eta_q n z)` with 𝕢 = Periodic.qParam (𝕢 24 z = e^{2πiz/24}) and `eta_q n z = (𝕢 1 z) ^ (n + 1)` (line 44): the same function.

items.name: (5.4) The differential ω = η⁴ dq/q and the normalized tangent vector at x
items.statement: ω := η⁴(z) dq/q = 2πi η⁴(z) dz (5.4). It is well defined on X₀(N) only up to a 6th root of unity (η⁴ has a multiplier of order 6), which by PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/101 does not affect the local symbols. If x is not an elliptic point of X₀(N) (u = 1), ω is non-zero at x, the tangent vector ∂/∂t is taken dual to ω, and the uniformizing parameter g satisfies ω = (g + a₂g² + a₃g³ + …) dg/g near x. In general ω has order 1/u − 1 at x and g is normalized so that ω = (1/u)(g^{1/u} + higher degree terms) dg/g near x, i.e. ω = d(g^{1/u})·(1 + …) [corrected; the printed display omits the factor 1/u — see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12].
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, (5.4) and the two paragraphs after it, p. 250
items.note: Corrected per PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12 (the corrected form is the one used in (5.5) and in Ch. III (8.3)). No atlas stage plans a tangent-vector normalization at Heegner points; Conrad §9 (conrad.txt pp. 34–35) replaces η⁴ dq/q, which lives only on a degree-6 cover, by the ℚ-rational 6-tensor Δ(q)(dq/q)^{⊗6} = ((2πi)η⁴(z) dz)^{⊗6}; this is in the GZ roadmap's source contract but not in any stage description. Library: only η (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/102). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (5.3) The local symbol ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v when r_A(m) ≠ 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. When r_A(m) ≠ 0 the point x occurs with multiplicity r_A(m) in T_m(x^σ) (Ch. III (4.3)), so c and T_m d^σ are not relatively prime; ord_x(c) = 1 and ord_x(T_m d^σ) = r_A(m). For every place v of H set ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v := lim_{y→x} {⟨c_y, T_m d^σ⟩_v − r_A(m) log|g(y)|_v}, c_y = (y) − (∞), with g the normalized uniformizing parameter at x of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103. By PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/101, Σ_v ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩.
items.note: Special case of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100 with the global g of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103. Planned only in YZZ's Hodge-class form, as for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100. Library: none.

items.name: (5.5) The normalized uniformizer at a complex place
items.statement: Let v be a complex place of H (|·|_v = |·|² on ℂ), g as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103 (corrected normalization). Then log|g(y)|_v − u log|2πi η⁴(z)(w − z)|_v → 0 as y → x, where z, w ∈ 𝔥 map to x, y on X₀(N)(ℂ).
items.note: Checked: the local parameter of X₀(N) at x is (w − z)^u·(unit); with ω = 2πiη⁴(w)dw and ω = (1/u)(g^{1/u} + …)dg/g one gets g = (2πiη⁴(z)(w − z))^u (1 + o(1)), which is (5.5); with the printed normalization one would get g = (2πiη⁴(z)(w − z)/u)^u and a spurious −u log|u|_v (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12). Conrad Theorem 9.6 (conrad.txt p. 42) takes g_{z_v}(z′) = 2πiη⁴(z_v)(z′ − z_v) and says this is 'exactly the archimedean height contribution which is computed in [GZ, Ch II, (5.3), (5.5)]'. Not planned; no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (5.6) Archimedean local symbol when r_A(m) ≠ 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let v be a complex place of H and z, z′ ∈ 𝔥 points mapping to x, x^σ. With R_N = {(a b; c d) ∈ M₂(ℤ) : N | c}, g_s(z, z′) = −2Q_{s−1}(1 + |z − z′|²/(2 Im z Im z′)) (2.9), κ_N, λ_N as in (2.13), (2.21): ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = lim_{s→1} [Σ_{γ ∈ R_N/±1, det γ = m, γz′ ≠ z} g_s(z, γz′) + 4πσ₁(m) E_N(w_N z, s) + u r_A(m) lim_{w→z} {g_s(z, w) − log|2πi η⁴(z)(w − z)|_v} + 4π m^s σ_{1−2s}(m) E_N(z′, s) + σ₁(m)κ_N/(s − 1)] − σ₁(m)(λ_N − 2κ_N) [printed '−σ₁(m)(λ_N + 2κ_N)'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E10]. The number of γ ∈ R_N/±1 of determinant m with γz′ = z is u r_A(m).
items.note: Obtained from Prop. (2.23), (5.3) and (5.5); the terms with γz′ ≠ z and E_N(w_N w, s) are continuous at w = z. Checked a = u r_A(m): each coset Γ₀(N)γ with γz′ ∈ Γ₀(N)z contains exactly u elements (mod ±1) with γz′ = z, and there are r_A(m) such cosets (Ch. III (4.3)). Planned as a method only (GZ.7 archimedean Green-function identity; GZ.7 'Handle self-intersection terms'). No library.

items.name: (5.7) Extension of G^m_{N,s}(z, z′) to all z, z′
items.statement: For all z, z′ ∈ 𝔥 (previously defined only for z ∉ T_m z′): G^m_{N,s}(z, z′) := Σ_{γ ∈ R_N/±1, det γ = m, γz′ ≠ z} g_s(z, γz′) + Σ_{γ ∈ R_N/±1, det γ = m, γz′ = z} lim_{w→z} (g_s(z, w) − log|2πi η(z)⁴ (z − w)|²). With this definition (5.6) is literally the formula of Proposition (2.23); the second sum equals a·g_s(z), a = #{γ ∈ R_N/±1 : det γ = m, γz′ = z} (= u r_A(m) for z, z′ over x, x^σ), g_s(z) the renormalized value PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/109.
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, (5.7) and the paragraph after it, p. 251
items.note: GZ-specific renormalization; the terms with γz′ ≠ z reproduce §3 and give the n > 0 part of the sum in Prop. (3.11). Not planned; no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Asymptotics of the Legendre function Q_{s−1}(t) as t ↘ 1
items.statement: For the Legendre function of the second kind Q_{s−1} (s > 1, s near 1) as t ↘ 1: Q_{s−1}(t) = ½ log((t + 1)/(t − 1)) − (Γ′/Γ(s) − Γ′/Γ(1)) + o(1) [printed '+ O(1)'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E11].
items.note: Classical: Q_ν(t) = ½ log((t+1)/(t−1)) − γ − ψ(ν + 1) + O((t − 1) log(t − 1)), and −γ − ψ(s) = ψ(1) − ψ(s). Library: Mathlib has the digamma function `Complex.digamma` = logDeriv Gamma (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Digamma.lean:48) with `Complex.digamma_one` = −γ (line 56), but no Legendre functions (grep legendreQ/LegendreQ in both libraries: none); atlas: no stage mentions Legendre functions of the second kind. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Renormalized self-value g_s(z)
items.statement: g_s(z) := lim_{w→z} (g_s(z, w) − log|2πi η(z)⁴ (z − w)|²) = −log|2π (z − z̄) η(z)⁴|² + 2 Γ′/Γ(s) − 2 Γ′/Γ(1).
items.note: Checked from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/108 with t = 1 + |z − w|²/(2y²): ½ log((t+1)/(t−1)) = log(2y/|z − w|) + o(1) and |z − z̄| = 2y. Not planned; no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Kronecker's first limit formula (as used for g_s(z))
items.statement: For z ∈ 𝔥 and E(z, σ) the weight-0 Eisenstein series of SL₂(ℤ) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/94): g_s(z) = −2 log 2π + 2 Γ′/Γ(s) + 2 Γ′/Γ(1) + (2/π) lim_{σ→1} [2^σ ζ(2σ) E(z, σ) − π/(σ − 1)]; equivalently (Kronecker's first limit formula) lim_{σ→1} [2^σ ζ(2σ) E(z, σ) − π/(σ − 1)] = 2πγ − π log(2 Im z · |η(z)|⁴).
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, p. 251 (last display; 'By Kronecker's first limit formula')
items.note: Quoted classical result. Checked the printed consequence against PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/109 using Σ′ y^σ|mz + n|^{−2σ} = π/(σ − 1) + 2π(γ − log 2 − log(√y |η(z)|²)) + O(σ − 1) and ζ(2σ)E(z, σ) = ½ Σ′ y^σ|mz + n|^{−2σ}. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep kronecker/LimitFormula: only matrix Kronecker products and Mathlib's Gamma/Beta 'LimitFormula' for Γ); atlas: EllipticRegulators:ER.3/ER.5 plan Kronecker–Eisenstein series in Bloch's setting, no stage plans the first limit formula. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Sum of renormalized self-values over the Heegner points
items.note: Checked from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/110, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/96 (2^σζ(2σ)E(τ_A, σ) = u|D|^{σ/2}ζ_K(A, σ)), PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/97 and PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/98: u|D|^{σ/2}ζ_K(σ) = πh/(σ − 1) + πh(½ log|D| + γ + (L′/L)(1, ε)) + O(σ − 1), and Γ′/Γ(1) = −γ. Not planned; no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Proposition (5.8): Proposition (4.2) when r_A(m) ≠ 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Proposition (4.2) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/99) remains true when m is the norm of an ideal in A, provided that the local symbols ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v (v | ∞) in the definition of ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ are defined by (5.3) with the normalized uniformizer g of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103, and γ^m_{N,s}(A) is defined by (3.3) with G^m_{N,s} as in (5.7). This invariant is then γ^m_{N,s}(A) = (expression in Corollary (3.17)) + 2h u r_A(m) (Γ′/Γ(s) − log 2π + (L′/L)(1, ε) + ½ log|D|).
items.note: Checked: total contribution of the γz′ = z terms is a·Σ_A g_s(τ_A) with a = u r_A(m) (g_s(z) is SL₂(ℤ)-invariant since Im z·|η(z)|⁴ is). As for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/99, planned only as a method (GZ.7 archimedean Green-function identity and self-intersection terms; GZ.8 specialization to X₀(N)); Conrad Theorem 9.6 (conrad.txt p. 42) confirms that this archimedean term, paired with his non-archimedean terms, recovers the global height. Validity at elliptic points (D = −3) depends on the corrected normalization of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12).

items.name: (0.1) Néron's local symbol as an arithmetic intersection number
items.statement: Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Let 𝒳 be a regular model of the curve X over A_v, a, b relatively prime divisors of degree 0 on X over H_v, and A, B divisors on 𝒳 restricting to a, b on the general fibre. If A has zero intersection with every fibre component of 𝒳, then ⟨a, b⟩_v = −(A · B) log q.
items.note: Quoted from Gross [14]. Planned: GZ.2 'construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions. Include regular models, vertical correction divisors, intersection matrices and their kernel … Prove the Faltings–Hriljac comparison for degree-zero divisors with the canonical Jacobian pairing … Export local height decomposition'. Library: none (coverage audit AUDIT-25 for GZ.2: intersection pairing 'absent', regular models 'partial' — Tau Ceti has flat finitely presented models over a DVR but no regularity predicate).

items.name: Announced p-inert formula for Σ_{v|p}⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v (case r_A(m) = 0)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let p be a prime inert in K and assume r_A(m) = 0. Then Σ_{v|p} ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = −u² log p Σ_{0 < n < m|D|/N, n ≡ 0 (mod p)} ord_p(pn) r_A(m|D| − nN) δ(n) R_{{A𝔮𝔫}}(n/p), where 𝔮 is an ideal of O with (N𝔮/l) = (−p/l) for all primes l | D, δ(n) = 2^{#{primes l | (n, D)}} (3.15), and R_{{B}}(k) is the number of integral ideals of norm k in the genus of B.
items.locator: Chapter III, introduction, p. 253 (proved as the r_A(m) = 0 case of Proposition (9.7), p. 266)
items.note: Announcement; agrees with the second term of Prop. (9.7) (the first term −r_A(m) h u ord_p(m) log p vanishes when r_A(m) = 0). Planned only as YZZ's analogue: GZ.7 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction'; GZ.8 'Specialize to X₀(N)'. The explicit quaternionic evaluation (GZ III §9, Conrad §10 and Mann's appendix, in the source contract) is not named in any stage. Library: none.

items.name: (0.4) The case m = 1 at a prime p ∤ ND
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Let m = 1, v | p with p ∤ ND, and r_A(1) = 0 (σ ≠ 1, so x ≠ x^σ over H). Then ⟨(x) − (∞), (x^σ) − (0)⟩_v = ⟨c, d^σ⟩_v = −½ Σ_{n≥1} Card(Isom_{W/π^n}(x^σ, x)) log q_v. The sum is zero unless x and x^σ meet mod π; by Deuring's theory it is zero if p splits in K; otherwise p is inert (as p ∤ D) and log q_v = 2 log p.
items.locator: Chapter III, introduction, (0.4) and following paragraph, p. 253
items.note: Special case m = 1 of Prop. (3.3) + Prop. (4.4) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/132, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/135); degree-1 homomorphisms are isomorphisms. q_v = p² because p inert in K splits completely in H/K ((p) is principal). Planned as for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/137 (GZ.7 deformation-length calculations). Library: none.

items.name: Supersingular reduction of a Heegner diagram: Eichler order and Hom ≅ R𝔞
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Let p be inert in K and p ∤ N (in the paper's illustration p ∤ ND, m = 1). The endomorphism ring R = End_{W/π}(x mod π) of the (supersingular) reduction of the Heegner diagram is an Eichler order of index (level) N in the definite quaternion algebra B over ℚ of discriminant p (ramified exactly at p and ∞), and Hom_{W/π}(x^σ, x) is isomorphic to the left R-module R𝔞 (𝔞 an ideal in the class A). The points x and x^σ meet mod π if and only if R𝔞 is principal; then Card(Isom_{W/π}(x^σ, x)) is the number of generators of R𝔞.
items.note: Stated without proof in the illustration (made precise in §§7, 9). Searched: 'Eichler' in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: none; atlas 'Eichler order': no stage. Nearest plans: GZ.7 ('supersingular and superspecial reduction'), HE.1 ('For quaternionic curves construct optimal embeddings of the specified orders'), HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3 (definite quaternionic forms on finite double cosets); none states the Eichler-order description of End of a supersingular Γ₀(N)-diagram. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 plans only that End of an ordinary curve over 𝔽_q is an order in ℚ(π_q). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (0.5) Explicit model of B and of the order R, and R𝔞
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let p be inert in K (p ∤ ND) and q a prime with q ≡ −p (mod D); then (q) = 𝔮𝔮̄ splits in K and B = K + Kj with jα = ᾱj (α ∈ K) and j² = −pq is the definite quaternion algebra of discriminant p. For some place v | p the order R = End_{W/π}(x mod π) is R = {α + βj ∈ B : α ∈ 𝔡⁻¹, β ∈ 𝔡⁻¹𝔮⁻¹𝔫, α − β integral at all primes dividing 𝔡}, 𝔡 = (√D) the different of K and 𝔫 the primitive ideal of norm N attached to x. For 𝔞 an ideal in the class A: Hom_{W/π}(x^σ, x) ≅ R𝔞 = {α + βj : α ∈ 𝔡⁻¹𝔞, β ∈ 𝔡⁻¹𝔮⁻¹𝔫𝔞̄, α − β integral at 𝔡}.
items.locator: Chapter III, introduction, (0.5), p. 253 (general version (9.2)–(9.3), p. 265)
items.note: Checked: ε(q) = ε(−1)ε(p) = (−1)(−1) = 1, so q splits; the Hilbert symbol (D, −pq) is −1 exactly at p and ∞ (at l | D, −pq ≡ p² mod l is a square); the reduced norm is N(α + βj) = Nα + pqNβ, and the lattice R has reduced discriminant pN (Gram determinant (pN)² after the index-|D| congruence condition), consistent with an Eichler order of level N in B_{p,∞}. (α + βj)𝔞 = α𝔞 + β𝔞̄ j gives the form of R𝔞. Library: Mathlib has the carrier `QuaternionAlgebra` (Algebra/Quaternion.lean:65) and Tau Ceti splitting criteria (Algebra/Quaternion/Split.lean), but no orders; no atlas stage plans this model (Tau Ceti QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 2 plans quaternion algebras over fields only). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (0.6)–(0.7) Generators of R𝔞 and solutions of l + nN = |D|
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/117, R𝔞 is principal iff it contains b = α + βj with reduced norm Nb = Nα + pqNβ = N𝔞. If b is a generator, the ideals 𝔠 = (α)𝔡𝔞⁻¹ and 𝔠′ = (β)𝔡𝔮𝔫⁻¹𝔞̄⁻¹ are integral (0.6) and satisfy N𝔠 + pN·N𝔠′ = |D| (0.7). Putting n = pN𝔠′ and l = N𝔠 gives a solution of l + nN = |D| with n ≡ 0 (mod p) and r_A(l) ≠ 0; conversely such solutions yield generators of R𝔞 and contribute to the height in (0.4).
items.note: Checked: N𝔠 = Nα·|D|/N𝔞 and N𝔠′ = Nβ·|D|q/(N·N𝔞), so N𝔠 + pN·N𝔠′ = |D|(Nα + pqNβ)/N𝔞 = |D|; 𝔠 lies in A⁻¹ and r_{A⁻¹} = r_A. The 'conversely' is asserted without proof here (proved in §9). Not planned (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/117); no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (1.1)–(1.2) The moduli stack 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} of cyclic N-isogenies of generalized elliptic curves
items.statement: For a base scheme S, 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)}(S) is the groupoid of cyclic isogenies φ: E → E′ of degree N between generalized elliptic curves over S (1.1) such that the group scheme A = ker φ meets every irreducible component of each geometric fibre. 'Cyclic of degree N' means that locally on S there is a point P with A = Σ_{a=1}^{N} [aP] as Cartier divisors on E (1.2). When N is invertible on S this is equivalent to A being locally isomorphic to ℤ/Nℤ; when N is squarefree it is equivalent to A being locally free of rank N.
items.note: Planned: R13.2 'Construct compactified full and Γ₁ level problems, and the correct Γ₀(n) problem at general n. Follow Česnavičius' refined description when the naive cyclic-subgroup formulation fails; include the extra boundary data'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves 8D (KM 6.6.1, [Γ₀(N)] over Ell, elliptic curves only, 'Identify this locus with [Γ₀(N)]'); 3B 'Define a cyclic subgroup of order N …' (Drinfeld/KM cyclicity). Note: for N not squarefree this naive stack does not give X₀(N) at the cusps (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E13); R13.2 plans the corrected (Česnavičius) stack instead. Library: none (grep generalizedElliptic/cyclicIsogen/coarseModuli in both libraries: none).

items.name: The model X of X₀(N) over ℤ (coarse moduli scheme)
items.statement: X := the coarse moduli scheme of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} ([7] Deligne–Rapoport pp. 234–243; [21] Katz–Mazur pp. 407 ff.), a model of X₀(N) over ℤ. X ⊗ ℤ[1/N] is smooth and proper over ℤ[1/N]; for a prime p | N, X ⊗ ℤ/pℤ is singular and reducible over ℤ/pℤ.
items.note: Planned: R13.4a 'Construct coarse compactified curves from R13.2's actual stack presentations, with the necessary finite-inertia quotient, normalization and existence arguments. Treat full, fixed-pairing, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ level separately … Prove properness, normality and the allowed base-change statements'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves 9D (coarse moduli M(𝒫) of affine KM problems) and Layer 10 (compactified curves over ℤ[1/N], prime N ≥ 5 only). Coverage audit (AUDIT-10): R13.4a 'not built'. For N not squarefree the coarse space of the naive stack PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/119 is not X₀(N) near some cusps (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E13); the intended object is the normalization model (DR/KM).

items.name: Structure of the fibre X ⊗ 𝔽_p for p | N
items.statement: Let p | N, N = pⁿM with (p, M) = 1. Then X ⊗ ℤ/pℤ has n + 1 irreducible components 𝓕_{a,b}, indexed by pairs of non-negative integers with a + b = n; 𝓕_{a,b} is isomorphic to X₀(M) ⊗ ℤ/pℤ and occurs with multiplicity φ(p^c), c = min(a, b). All the 𝓕_{a,b} meet at each supersingular point of X (the points x = (φ: E → E′) with E, E′ supersingular). The non-supersingular points of 𝓕_{a,b} correspond to diagrams whose kernel A = ker φ is locally isomorphic to μ_{p^a} × ℤ/p^bℤ × ℤ/Mℤ.
items.note: Katz–Mazur ch. 13 ('crossings'). Planned only partially: R13.5 'Compute the local models and supersingular intersections required by the proof … Begin with the prime-to-p level and one p-factor cases used by level lowering, then treat every higher p-power/composite-level case actually invoked by the Serre weight-and-level argument' (scope tied to level lowering, so general pⁿ is not guaranteed); Tau Ceti ModularCurves 8A 'for an ordinary p-power fibre, identify E[pⁿ] ≅ μ_{pⁿ} × (ℤ/pⁿℤ) and prove that the rank-pⁿ subgroups are exactly μ_{p^a} × p^{n−b}(ℤ/pⁿℤ) with a+b=n' (the pointwise part). Coverage audit (AUDIT-10): R13.5 'not built'. Checked the component count against Kronecker's congruence PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/122 (degrees p² + p for n = 2, M = 1).

items.name: Kronecker's congruence for the modular polynomial
items.statement: For N = pⁿM with (p, M) = 1 and Φ_N(j, j′) the classical modular polynomial of level N: Φ_N(j, j′) ≡ Π_{a+b=n, c=min(a,b)} Φ_M(j^{p^{a−c}}, j′^{p^{b−c}})^{φ(p^c)} (mod p).
items.note: Quoted classical result illustrating PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/121. Checked n = 1, M = 1: Φ_p(j, j′) ≡ (j^p − j′)(j − j′^p) (mod p), the classical Kronecker congruence; for n = 2, M = 1 the j-degrees p² + (p − 1) + 1 = p² + p = ψ(p²) agree. Searched: modularPolynomial/ModularPolynomial in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: none; atlas: no stage mentions modular polynomials or Kronecker's congruence. Routed (source) to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.3.

items.name: (1.3) Aut_k(x) for a geometric point of X
items.statement: For a geometric point x = (φ: E → E′) of X over an algebraically closed field k, Aut_k(x) is the group of pairs of isomorphisms (f: E → E, f′: E′ → E′) with f′ ∘ φ = φ ∘ f (diagram (1.3)). It is finite, contains ⟨±1⟩, and equals the automorphism group of the pair (E, A), A = ker φ.
items.note: Planned implicitly with the stack: R13.4a 'Treat full, fixed-pairing, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ level separately, with their bases and stabilizers'. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 plans Aut(E, O) (units of the geometric endomorphism ring) but not automorphisms of level structures. Library: none.

items.name: Strict henselization of X at x ([7, p. 172])
items.statement: The strict henselization of X at a geometric point x is isomorphic to the quotient of the strict henselization of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} at the corresponding point by the group Aut_k(x)/⟨±1⟩.
items.note: Quoted from Deligne–Rapoport. Conrad Lemma 4.2 (conrad.txt p. 11) proves the complete-local version: the complete local ring of X at y₀ is the ring of Aut(y₀)-invariants in the universal deformation ring, on which −1 acts trivially. Planned: Tau Ceti ModularCurves 9D (M(𝒫) = 𝕄(𝒫, δ)/G, invariant quotients) and 9C ('at a supersingular point the completed local ring of the quotient is A^H', for the listed quotient problems); R13.4a (finite-inertia quotients). Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (1.4): regularity of X over ℤ
items.statement: X is regular over ℤ, except at the supersingular points x in characteristics p | N where Aut_k(x) ≠ ⟨±1⟩.
items.note: Quoted as a consequence of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/124, Drinfeld [9] and Katz–Mazur [21, p. 166]. Not independently verified here at ordinary points with extra automorphisms lying on components 𝓕_{a,b} of multiplicity φ(p^{min(a,b)}) > 1 (possible only when p² | N, j = 0 or 1728); this does not affect the paper, since Heegner points reduce to the multiplicity-one components 𝓕_{n,0}, 𝓕_{0,n} (Prop. 3.1). Nearest plans: Tau Ceti ModularCurves 8D ('prove the Notes Added in Proof descent theorem which passes regularity to [Γ₀(N)]' — the stack, not the coarse space) and 9C ('No assertion is made that an arbitrary finite quotient of a regular moduli problem is regular'); R13.5 (regular models only at the levels used by level lowering). Conrad avoids the statement (Remark 2.3: X_v 'is usually not regular'; only the relative smooth locus is used). Library: none. Routed (source) to ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5.

items.name: Cusps of X and their reductions
items.statement: The subscheme Cusps of X is finite over ℤ, with one irreducible component Cusp(d) for each positive divisor d of N; Cusp(d) has φ(f) geometric points, f = gcd(d, N/d), and Cusp(d) ≅ Spec ℤ[μ_f]. [Printed: 'Cusp(d) corresponds to diagrams of Néron polygons where A = ker φ is isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ' — correct only when gcd(d, N/d) = 1; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E13.] The section ∞ of X is Cusp(N) (A ≅ μ_N) and the section 0 is Cusp(1) (A ≅ ℤ/Nℤ); in characteristic p | N they reduce to the components 𝓕_{n,0} and 𝓕_{0,n} respectively, and in general Cusp(d) (mod p) lies on 𝓕_{a,b} with a = ord_p(d) [21, Chap. 10].
items.note: Planned: R12.3 'Construct the local parameter at each cusp, compare its width with the Tate parameter … identify the scheme-theoretic cusp locus. … do not … assert that the coarse cusp fibre is always reduced'; R13.3 'classify boundary level data and compute completed local rings, cusp widths … The finite-flat cusp fibre, its reduced locus, and its Cartier structure are distinct assertions'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 10 treats only prime N ≥ 5 over ℤ[1/N]. The count φ(gcd(d, N/d)) and field ℚ(μ_f) are the classical cusp data of X₀(N). Only Cusp(N) and Cusp(1) (gcd = 1) are used later. Library: none (Tau Ceti has analytic cusps of congruence subgroups in NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps, not the integral cusp scheme).

items.name: (2.1) Hom_S(y, x) between Γ₀(N)-diagrams, its degree
items.statement: Let S be a complete local ring with algebraically closed residue field k, and x = (φ: E → E′), y = (ψ: F → F′) two S-valued points of X with non-cuspidal reduction, represented by diagrams of cyclic N-isogenies over S. Hom_S(y, x) is the set of pairs of homomorphisms (f: F → E, f′: F′ → E′) over S with f′ ∘ ψ = φ ∘ f (diagram (2.1)); addition uses the group laws of E and E′. It is a left module over End_S(x) = Hom_S(x, x) and a right module over End_S(y) (multiplication = composition). The degree of a non-zero (f, f′) is the positive integer deg f = deg f′; for each m ≥ 1 the set Hom_S(y, x)_{deg m} is finite and carries a faithful action of the finite group Aut_S(x). [GZ add: 'one can check that the definition of Hom_S(y, x) is independent of the diagrams chosen to represent the points x and y' — false in general for artinian S at points with extra automorphisms; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E14.]
items.note: deg f = deg f′ because deg φ = deg ψ = N. Planned as the object of the deformation-length method: GZ.7 'Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models'; A6 'Extend the field Hom/End API … with finite generation and torsion freeness … degree formulas for polarized isogenies' (abelian schemes, not diagrams). Library: none for diagrams (Tau Ceti has field-level isogenies of Weierstrass curves, AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/*).

items.name: Deuring: End_S(x) is ℤ, an imaginary quadratic order, or a quaternion order
items.statement: In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/127, the ring End_S(x) is either ℤ, an order in an imaginary quadratic field, or an order in a definite quaternion algebra of prime discriminant over ℚ [8].
items.note: Quoted from Deuring (1941). Searched: no endomorphism-ring classification in Mathlib or Tau Ceti ('supersingular' occurs once in Tau Ceti, in a comment of AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/QuadraticTwist.lean). Nearest plan: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 ('The assertion that the endomorphism ring of an ordinary curve over 𝔽_q is an order in ℚ(π_q) is a substantial theorem … a named milestone'; also `GeometricEnd`, `HasGeometricCM`); the quaternion (supersingular) case and the characteristic-0 classification are not planned. Routed (source) to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5.

items.name: Reduction of Heegner sections (Deuring; potentially good reduction)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Since N is prime to D^h = disc(H/ℚ), X ⊗ A_v has the shape of §1. CM elliptic curves have potentially good reduction, so the sections x and x^σ do not meet the divisor Cusps in the special fibre. They reduce to supersingular points if and only if p is not split in K [29]. If p | N then p splits in K and x, x^σ have ordinary reduction.
items.note: Deuring's reduction criterion, quoted from Serre [29]. Nearest plans: GZ.7 'Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction' (names the case division, not the criterion); ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5 'Instantiate the Shimura–Taniyama formula for reductions … Supersingular reduction cannot be treated as ordinary'. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layers 3–4 plan the ordinary/supersingular dichotomy and HasGoodSupersingularReduction as definitions only. Library: none. Conrad Lemma 2.4 / Theorem 2.5 (conrad.txt pp. 4–6) supply the good models over W. Routed (source) to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5.

items.name: Proposition (3.1): component of the reduction when p | N
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Suppose p | N (so p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits and v divides exactly one of 𝔫, 𝔫̄, where O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/Nℤ is the annihilator of ker φ). Then the sections x and x^σ reduce to ordinary points in the component 𝓕_{0,n} if v | 𝔫̄, and 𝓕_{n,0} if v | 𝔫 (n = ord_p N).
items.note: Proof: if v | 𝔫̄, ker φ is étale over A_v, ≅ ℤ/Nℤ over 𝔽, so the reduction lies on 𝓕_{0,n} ∋ Cusp(1) = 0; if v | 𝔫, ker φ ≅ μ_{pⁿ} × ℤ/Mℤ over 𝔽, so it lies on 𝓕_{n,0} ∋ Cusp(N) = ∞; x^σ has kernel also annihilated by 𝔫 (σ fixes K). Checked against PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/121, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/126. Used by Conrad Lemma 2.2 and Corollary 2.7. Planned only via GZ.7 'horizontal intersections and vertical corrections' (the vertical correction at p | N vanishes by PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/131). Library: none.

items.name: Corollary (3.2): one of c, d is orthogonal to all fibre components
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. One of the divisors c = (x) − (∞), d = (x^σ) − (0) has zero intersection with every fibral component 𝓕_{a,b} of X ⊗ A_v: c if v | 𝔫, d if v | 𝔫̄ (and v divides 𝔫𝔫̄ = N).
items.locator: Chapter III, (3.2) Corollary and proof, pp. 256–257
items.note: For p ∤ N the fibre is irreducible and the statement is trivial. Planned as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/130. Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (3.3) = (0.2): local symbol as intersection number
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Assume m ≥ 1 is prime to N and r_A(m) = 0. Then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = −(x · T_m x^σ) log q.
items.locator: Chapter III, (3.3) Proposition, p. 257 (announced as (0.2), p. 252)
items.note: Proof checked: resolve the quotient singularities at supersingular points to get X^reg (Heegner sections and cusps unaffected); by PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/131 and Hecke-invariance of fibral components (m prime to N), PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/113 applies to c and T_m d; expand (c·T_m d^σ) = (x·T_m x^σ) − (x·T_m 0) − (∞·T_m x^σ) + (∞·T_m 0), where the middle terms vanish (potentially good reduction) and (∞·T_m 0) = σ₁(m)(∞·0) = 0 since N > 1. Regularity after base change to A_v holds: if p | D then p ∤ N and X is smooth over ℤ_p; if p | N then H_v/ℚ_p is unramified (cf. Conrad Remark 2.3, conrad.txt p. 4, which cites this proposition). Planned: GZ.2 (local height decomposition via regular models) and GZ.7 ('Assemble local formulas … including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes'). Library: none.

items.name: (4.1)–(4.2) Endomorphisms and homomorphisms of Heegner diagrams over W
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. End_W(x) = End_W(x^σ) = O (4.1), and Hom_W(x^σ, x) ≅ 𝔞 as a left O-module (4.2), where 𝔞 is an ideal in the class A corresponding to σ under the Artin isomorphism. If g_α ∈ Hom_W(x^σ, x) corresponds to α ∈ 𝔞, then deg g_α = Nα/N𝔞.
items.locator: Chapter III, §4, (4.1)–(4.2) and following paragraph, p. 257
items.note: Quoted: proved analytically via lattices [23] (Lang), algebraically by Serre [29] (x^σ = (Hom(𝔞, E) → Hom(𝔞, E′))). Checked analytically: E = ℂ/L, E^σ = ℂ/𝔞⁻¹L, Hom(ℂ/𝔞⁻¹L, ℂ/L) = 𝔞, deg = [L : α𝔞⁻¹L] = N(α)/N(𝔞). Planned: CM.1 'Construct the elliptic curve associated to a complex ideal lattice and its order action … Compute the action of an invertible prime ideal and its isogeny degree; compare analytic and algebraic endomorphisms'; HE.1 'prove descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication'. The passage to W (good models; Conrad Theorems 2.5–2.6) is not named in these stages. Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (4.3): multiplicity of x in T_m x^σ
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Assume m is prime to N. The multiplicity of the point x in the divisor T_m x^σ is r_A(m).
items.note: Proof: by (2.3) of Ch. I the multiplicity is the number of degree-m isogenies g_α ∈ 𝔞 ≅ Hom_W(x^σ, x) = Hom_{H̄}(x^σ, x) modulo O^× ≅ Aut_W(x), i.e. the number of integral ideals 𝔟 = (α)/𝔞 of norm m in A⁻¹, equivalently r_A(m) (conjugation). Refines Prop. (9.1) of Ch. I. Used by Conrad §4 (conrad.txt p. 10). Planned: HE.2 'Compute Hecke correspondences on CM points by classifying the local cyclic subgroups/optimal embeddings'. Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (4.4) = (0.3): intersection number as a sum of Hom counts
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Assume m is prime to N and r_A(m) = 0. Then (x · T_m x^σ) = ½ Σ_{n≥1} Card(Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x^σ, x)_{deg m}).
items.locator: Chapter III, (4.4) Proposition, p. 258 (announced as (0.3), p. 252; proved in §§5–6)
items.note: (0.3) is printed with Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x, x^σ); duality f ↦ f̂ (compatible with the diagrams, Hom groups being torsion-free) gives a degree-preserving bijection, so the two counts agree — not a mistake. Same statement as Conrad Theorem 5.1 (conrad.txt p. 13, with W_n = W/π^{n+1}, n ≥ 0). Planned: GZ.7 'Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models'; A4 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves 7F (ST-1: the Serre–Tate equivalence). Coverage audit (AUDIT-25) for GZ.7: deformation-length calculations 'absent'. Library: none.

items.name: (4.5) Reduction of homomorphisms is injective; Hom_W = ∩ Hom_{W/πⁿ}
items.statement: Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. For S-valued diagrams y, x as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/127 over W: Hom_{W/π^{n+1}}(x^σ, x) ↪ Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x^σ, x) for n ≥ 1, and Hom_W(x^σ, x) = ∩_{n≥1} Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x^σ, x) [15, 30]. Hence, when r_A(m) = 0, the terms of the sum in (4.4) vanish for n sufficiently large.
items.note: Injectivity is rigidity (Conrad Theorem 2.1(2), Lemma 3.1); the intersection is Grothendieck's existence theorem (Conrad Theorem 3.4 and the display after it, conrad.txt p. 9); vanishing for large n follows since Hom_W(x^σ, x)_{deg m} = ∅ when r_A(m) = 0 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/133–PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/134) and the finite sets decrease. Planned: A1 'Prove rigidity for pointed maps … Include the nonreduced-base argument'; SF.4 'formal schemes, algebraization'. Library: none.

items.name: The integer h_n(y, x)_{deg m}

items.name: h_n(y,x)_{deg m} and 'new' homomorphisms
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). For non-cuspidal W-sections y, x of X and n ≥ 1: h_n(y,x)_{deg m} := ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}. The reduction maps Hom_{W/π^{n+1}}(y,x) ↪ Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x) are injective and Hom_W(y,x) = ∩_n Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x) (4.5). Hom^{new}_{W/π^n}(y,x) := Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x) ∖ (image of Hom_W(y,x)), and likewise Aut^{new}_{W/π^n}(x).

items.name: (5.1) Hom counts over T_m x^σ for m prime to p
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume p ∤ m. Every point y of the divisor T_m x^σ is a Heegner point over H in the sense of Gross [13], with End_H(y) = O_y an order in K of conductor dividing m. Each y is rational over W ⊗ ℚ_p and is the canonical lifting of its reduction. For every n ≥ 1, h_n(x^σ,x)_{deg m} = Σ_{y ∈ T_m x^σ} h_n(y,x)_{deg 1}. Reason: a degree-m isogeny f: x^σ → x over W/π^n is determined by its kernel, which lifts uniquely to an étale subgroup C of order m of x^σ over W, and f induces an isomorphism x^σ_C ≅ x over W/π^n.

Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.' The roadmap's primary source contracts include 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' and 'Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, §§2–10' (README l.127), and Conrad §§4–10 re-prove exactly this chapter. items.name: (5.2) Decomposition of T_{p^t}z into quasi-canonical liftings (Gross [15], Prop. 5.3)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Let m = p^t·r with t ≥ 1 and (r,p) = 1, and let z ∈ T_r x^σ (rational over W ⊗ ℚ_p). The points y of T_{p^t}z are rational over ramified extensions of W ⊗ ℚ_p. The corresponding sections over the ring-class extensions W_y are quasi-canonical liftings of level p^s (0 ≤ s ≤ t) of their reductions ([15], Prop. 5.3). Let y(s) denote the W-divisor formed by a point of level s together with all its W-conjugates. Then: p split in K: T_{p^t}z = Σ_{0≤s≤t} Σ_{j=1}^{t−s+1} y(s)_j with deg y(s)_j = p^s − p^{s−1} (s ≥ 1); p inert in K: T_{p^t}z = Σ_{0≤s≤t, s≡t (mod 2)} y(s) with deg y(s) = p^s + p^{s−1} (s ≥ 1); p ramified in K: T_{p^t}z = Σ_{0≤s≤t} y(s) with deg y(s) = p^s (s ≥ 0). Level-0 components have degree 1.
items.note: Checked: the degrees add up to σ₁(p^t) = 1+p+…+p^t in each case (split: Σ_s (t−s+1)(p^s−p^{s−1}) + (t+1) telescopes; inert and ramified directly). The degrees equal [O_p^× : O_{s,p}^×] for O_s = ℤ + p^sO. Partial plan: HE.0 'Compute the kernels of Pic(O_cℓ)→Pic(O_c) and extension degrees with the exceptional unit indices retained; ℓ+1 is only the inert, prime-to-conductor, ordinary-unit case' (the global orbit sizes). HE.2 'Compute Hecke correspondences on CM points by classifying the local cyclic subgroups/optimal embeddings ... for split or ramified primes and repeated conductor primes prove the full recurrence' (the conductor decomposition). GZ.7 plans deformation-length calculations in general. No stage names Gross's quasi-canonical liftings: 'quasi-canonical' and 'canonical lift' do not occur in any atlas stage description (the only hit is BelyiMaps layer 12, unrelated). Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti either.

items.name: (5.3) Eichler's congruence T_{p^t} ≡ Σ F^{t−i}F′^i (mod p) (quoted, Eichler [11])
items.statement: For a prime p ∤ N and t ≥ 1, on the special fibre X ⊗ F_p: T_{p^t} ≡ F^t + F^{t−1}F′ + F^{t−2}F′² + … + F′^t (mod p). Here F is the Frobenius correspondence and F′ its transpose. Consequence used (with (5.2)): every point y of y(s) is congruent mod π_y to a canonical lifting y₀ of level zero over W.
items.note: Checked for t = 2 from T_p ≡ F + F′, FF′ = F′F = p·Δ and T_p² = T_{p²} + pΔ. R14.6: 'Supply the special-fibre Eichler–Shimura relation'. HE.2: 'Establish the Eichler–Shimura relation used in the proof in the appropriate geometric category'. The p^t form also needs the Hecke recursion as correspondences, planned by R14.1 ('Prove composition, double-coset and adjoint formulas'). Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti: rg for 'Eichler' finds nothing, and Tau Ceti's Frobenius isogenies are for a single curve over a field.

items.name: (5.4) Fundamental negative congruence (Gross [15])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). In the setting of (5.2): if y is a point of y(s) with s ≥ 1 and y₀ is the level-0 canonical lifting with y ≡ y₀ (mod π_y) (π_y a uniformiser of W_y), then y ≢ y₀ (mod π_y²). If x̄ is a non-cuspidal point of the special fibre with Aut_{W/π}(x) = ⟨±1⟩ (and p ∤ N, or x̄ regular), the completion of the local ring of X ⊗ W at x̄ pro-represents deformations of the diagram (φ: E → E′). Hence (y·x) = k exactly when y ≅ x over W/π^k but not over W/π^{k+1}. In general the strict henselisation of X at x̄ is the quotient of that of the stack 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} by Aut(x̄)/⟨±1⟩ (§1, [7]). One may instead pull back to a modular cover Y (full level M ≥ 3, (M,Np) = 1), where the objects are rigid.
items.note: 7D (quoted in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/143) plans the universal deformation and its 'comparison with the completed local ring of a representing moduli scheme'. 9D plans coarse moduli M(𝒫) = 𝕄(𝒫,δ)/G via a finite étale rigidifier, as used for Y → X. 7F ST-4 plans pro-representability with level structure for [Γ(p^n)], [Γ₁(p^n)] only. For p ∤ N the Γ₀(N)-structure deforms uniquely, so 7D suffices there. The p | N case (Katz–Mazur [Γ₀(p^n)]) is not planned at the deformation-ring level. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Deuring lifting for ordinary CM reduction (quoted, Deuring [8])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p splits in K, then x and x^σ have ordinary reduction and reduction induces isomorphisms Hom_W(x^σ,x) ≅ Hom_{W/π^n}(x^σ,x) for all n ≥ 1. In particular Aut_{W/π^n}(x) = Aut_W(x). Two canonical liftings with the same reduction mod π coincide.

items.name: (7.1) Vanishing at split primes when r_𝒜(m) = 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p splits in K and r_𝒜(m) = 0, then (x·T_m x^σ) = 0 at every place v | p (v ∤ N or v | N alike). Proof: Hom_{W/π^n}(x^σ,x) = Hom_W(x^σ,x) for all n ≥ 1, and this group has no element of degree m since r_𝒜(m) = 0.

items.name: Deuring: structure of R = End_{W/π}(x) at a non-split prime (quoted)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume p has a unique prime factor 𝔭 in K (p inert or ramified; then p ∤ N). Then x and x^σ have supersingular reduction mod π. R = End_{W/π}(x) is an order in the definite quaternion algebra B over ℚ ramified exactly at ∞ and p. The reduced discriminant of R is Np. R ⊗ ℤ_p is the maximal order of B ⊗ ℚ_p. For every l ≠ p, R ⊗ ℤ_l is conjugate to the Eichler order {(a b; c d) ∈ M₂(ℤ_l): c ≡ 0 (mod N)} in B ⊗ ℚ_l ≅ M₂(ℚ_l).
