items.name: (7.2) Decomposition B = K + Kj and additivity of the reduced norm
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). With p non-split and R, B as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/147: the reduction map O = End_W(x) → R = End_{W/π}(x) extends to a ℚ-linear embedding K → B. This gives B = B₊ ⊕ B₋ = K ⊕ Kj, where j lies in the non-trivial coset of N_{B^×}(K^×)/K^× (so jα = ᾱj for α ∈ K). Writing b = b₊ + b₋, the reduced norm satisfies N(b) = N(b₊) + N(b₋).
items.note: Partial library coverage, for the explicit symbol algebra only: Tau Ceti QuaternionAlgebra.normForm_apply_coordinates (TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/NormForm.lean:82) states normForm c₁ c₂ c₃ x = x.re² + c₂·x.re·x.imI − c₁·x.imI² − c₃·x.imJ² − c₂c₃·x.imJ·x.imK + c₁c₃·x.imK². With c₂ = 0 this is N(α+βj) = N_K(α) − c₃N_K(β) for α = re + imI·i, β = imJ + imK·i. So it covers the norm identity once B is presented as ℍ[ℚ, D, 0, c₃] (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/165), not the abstract decomposition for an arbitrary embedding K ↪ B. Tau Ceti's TauCeti.skolemNoether (CentralSimple/SkolemNoether.lean:107) needs the source algebra central simple, so it does not give j for a quadratic subfield K. QuadraticFormInvariants layer 2 plans the norm form of ℍ[K,a,b] ('prove Nrd ≅ ⟨1, −a, −b, ab⟩'), not the decomposition relative to a given subfield. No stage plans the decomposition. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Endomorphisms of the canonical formal group mod π^n (quoted, Gross [15])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). p non-split with prime 𝔭 | p in K. Let x̂ = (φ̂: Ê → Ê′) be the diagram of p-divisible groups of x over W. Ê and Ê′ are formal groups of dimension 1 and height 2, φ̂ is an isomorphism (p ∤ N), and End_{W/π^n}(x̂) = End_{W/π^n}(Ê). End_{W/π}(x̂) = R_p = R ⊗ ℤ_p is the maximal order of B_p = B ⊗ ℚ_p, and for n ≥ 1: End_{W/π^n}(x̂) = {b ∈ R_p : D·N(b₋) ≡ 0 mod p·(N𝔭)^{n−1}}.
items.note: Checked against Gross's End_{W/π^n}(F) = O_p + π^{n−1}·End(F₀). Inert: R_p = O_p ⊕ O_pΠ, and βΠ ∈ p^{n−1}R_p ⟺ ord_p N(b₋) ≥ 2n−1 = ord_p(p·(p²)^{n−1}). Ramified: β ∈ 𝔭^{n−1} ⟺ ord_p(D·N b₋) ≥ n. GZ.7 (Local arithmetic identities and boundary contributions): 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction, horizontal intersections and vertical corrections. Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.' The roadmap's primary source contracts include 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' and 'Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, §§2–10' (README l.127), and Conrad §§4–10 re-prove exactly this chapter. The stage text is written in YZZ's generality (Shimura curves). No stage names the X₀(N)-specific statement, and GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)' specialises the global formula, not these local identities. This is a method-level plan. GZ.7 plans supersingular deformation-length calculations; Gross's theorem is not named in any stage. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Serre–Tate: End_{W/π^n}(x) = End_{W/π}(x) ∩ End_{W/π^n}(x̂) (quoted [31, 40])
items.statement: For a Γ₀(N)-diagram x over W with p ∤ N and n ≥ 1, an endomorphism of x mod π lifts to W/π^n exactly when its action on the p-divisible group diagram x̂ lifts: End_{W/π^n}(x) = End_{W/π}(x) ∩ End_{W/π^n}(x̂) inside End_{W/π}(x̂).
items.note: A4: 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures; identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration.' ModularCurves 7F ST-1: 'For R artinian local ... the functor E/R ↦ E[p^∞] is an equivalence from the groupoid of deformations of E₀ over R to the groupoid of deformations of E₀[p^∞] over R'. 7F is stated for groupoids (isomorphisms). The Hom/End-lifting form needed here is the full Serre–Tate theorem of A4. rg 'serre.?tate' in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: 0 hits.

items.name: (7.3)(1) End_{W/π^n}(x) as a quaternionic congruence order
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). items.name: (7.3)(2) Hom_{W/π^n}(x^σ,x) ≅ End_{W/π^n}(x)·𝔞 and the degree formula
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If the isogeny ϕ: x^σ → x corresponds to b ∈ B, then deg ϕ = N(b)/N(𝔞). It rests on Serre's construction x^σ ≅ Hom_O(𝔞, x).

items.name: (7.4)(1) Inert primes: (x·T_m x^σ) as a sum over R𝔞
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume r_𝒜(m) = 0, p inert in K, v | p (so v ∤ N), and 𝔞 ∈ 𝒜 prime to p (implicit; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E21). items.name: (8.1) Self-intersection via the tangent vector ∂/∂t
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Suppose r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0, so c and T_m d^σ share the point x and ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v is defined by Ch. II (5.1)/(5.3) using the tangent vector ∂/∂t at x. Here ∂/∂t is dual to ω = η⁴(q)dq/q when u = 1, is defined in general through the normalisation ω = (g^{1/u} + …)dg/g of Ch. II §5, and is defined up to a 6th root of unity. Define (x·x) := ord_v(α), where α ∈ H_v^× is given (corrected reading) by ∂/∂t = α·(a basis of the free W-module T_x X). Printed: 'where α∂/∂t is a basis'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E16. With this convention the intersection formula (0.2), ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = −(x·T_m x^σ) log q_v, continues to hold.
items.note: GZ.2: 'Handle rational degree-one Hodge classes and self-intersections by a genuine regularization/intersection construction ... Export local height decomposition'. Conrad's Theorem 8.4 is the rigorous version (cotangent vector ω_x, (x.x)_{v,ω} = ord_v(α_x) with α_xω_x a basis, ⟨D,D′⟩_{v,ω} = −(D.D′)_{v,ω} log q_v). items.name: (8.2) Lemma: ord_v(α) counts new automorphisms
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Let x be any W-section of X reducing to a non-cuspidal point of the special fibre (not necessarily a Heegner point), and let v ∤ N. With α as in (8.1): ord_v(α) = ½ Σ_{n≥1} (#Aut_{W/π^n}(x) − #Aut_W(x)) = ½ Σ_{n≥1} #Aut^{new}_{W/π^n}(x). In particular ∂/∂t generates T_x X if and only if Aut_{W/π^n}(x) = Aut_W(x).
items.note: Proof sketch: ω = η⁴dq/q is a Néron differential on the degree-6 cyclic cover Y′ of Y = X₀(1) (the commutator subgroup of PSL₂(ℤ)). X′ = X ×_Y Y′ → X is analysed by ramification over the section, exactly as in (6.1). The sketch is valid for v ∤ 6N; the case v | 6 is omitted (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E25). Correct only with the corrected (8.1) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E16). Conrad Theorem 9.2 with (9.9) and Definition 9.5 proves ord = ½Σ(#Aut_{W_n} − #Aut_W) at non-elliptic points for v ∤ N, all residue characteristics. Plans as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/155.

items.name: (8.3) Explicit α on X₀(1)
items.statement: Let N = 1, so X = Y = X₀(1) and X′ = Y′. For a point x as in (8.2), modulo μ₆ (printed 'mod μ₀', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E17): α ≡ j(x)^{2/3}(j(x) − 1728)^{1/2} if j(x) ≠ 0, 1728; α ≡ 2⁶·3⁴ if j(x) = 1728; α ≡ 2⁹·3^{3/2} if j(x) = 0.
items.note: Exponents read on the 600-dpi scan (gz-wstein.pdf, decoded CCITT image). The GDZ PNG is too coarse for them. Verified: from j = E₄³/Δ and q dj/dq = −E₆E₄²/Δ, ω = η⁴dq/q = −j^{−2/3}(j−1728)^{−1/2} dj. So ∂/∂t = −j^{2/3}(j−1728)^{1/2}∂/∂j, i.e. α = j^{2/3}(j−1728)^{1/2} under the corrected (8.1). At j = 1728 (u = 2) and j = 0 (u = 3) the normalisation ω = (g^{1/u}+…)dg/g gives α = (2³·3²)² and (2³·3^{1/2})³ up to roots of unity, matching 2⁶·3⁴ and 2⁹·3^{3/2}. Libraries: Mathlib has WeierstrassCurve.j and the Dedekind eta function but no modular j-function relation of this kind. ModularCurves 9E plans the coarse j-line M([Γ(1)]) = Spec R[j], but no stage plans this differential computation. It is used by the paper only as a check, for v | 6. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume v | N (so p | N, p splits in K, p ∤ m). Then (x·T_m x^σ) = 0 if v | 𝔫, and (x·T_m x^σ) = −u·r_𝒜(m)·ord_p(N) if v | 𝔫̄. The ingredients: Lemma (8.2) remains true when x reduces to the component of the cusp ∞, which happens when v | 𝔫. When v | 𝔫̄ (x on the component of 0), ∂/∂t spans N^{−u}·T_x X (printed '(N)^u T_x X'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E18).
items.note: The component assignment agrees with Ch. III Prop. (3.1), p. 256: v|𝔫 ⇒ ker φ ≅ μ_{p^n} × ℤ/M, component F_{n,0} ∋ ∞; v|𝔫̄ ⇒ étale kernel, component F_{0,n} ∋ 0. The stated values agree with Conrad Theorem 10.4 (his (x.T_m x^σ)^{GZ} − r_𝒜(m)·ord_{v,x}(Δ)/(r_x+k)) and Lemma 10.1. GZ.7 plans 'local terms supported at conductor ... primes' (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/138).

items.name: (9.1) The p-part ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). For a rational prime p: ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p := Σ_{v | p} ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v, the sum over the places v of H above p, with local symbols as in (0.2) and (8.1).
items.note: GZ.2 plans the 'local height decomposition'. GZ.7 plans to 'Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison'.

items.name: (9.2) Split primes: ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p splits in K, then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p = −u·r_𝒜(m)·h·ord_p(m/N)·log p. Proof: by (8.5) and (8.6), ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = −u·r_𝒜(m)·j_𝔭·log q_v with j_𝔭 + j_𝔭̄ = ord_p(m/N), and Σ_{v|𝔭} log q_v = h·log p.
items.note: Checked both branches. p | N (so ord_p m = 0): only v | 𝔫̄ contributes, +u r ord_p(N) log q_v, summing to u r h ord_p(N) log p. p ∤ N: k_𝔭 + k_𝔭̄ = ord_p(m). Mann Theorem A.1 reproduces it (for even D too). GZ.7 (Local arithmetic identities and boundary contributions): 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction, horizontal intersections and vertical corrections. Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.' The roadmap's primary source contracts include 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' and 'Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, §§2–10' (README l.127), and Conrad §§4–10 re-prove exactly this chapter. The stage text is written in YZZ's generality (Shimura curves). No stage names the X₀(N)-specific statement, and GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)' specialises the global formula, not these local identities. This is a method-level plan.

items.name: Auxiliary prime q and the model B = (D, −pq) = K + Kj (inert case)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Let p be inert in K and v | p. Fix a prime q with (q/l) = (−p/l) for every prime l | D. Such q exist by Dirichlet's theorem. For §9's order S one must in fact also impose −pq ≡ 1 (mod D) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19). Then q splits in K, (q) = 𝔮𝔮̄. The quaternion algebra B with Hilbert symbol (D, −pq) is ramified only at ∞ and p, and B = K + Kj with j² = −pq and jα = ᾱj. For b = α + βj: N(b) = N(α) + pq·N(β) and N(b₋) = pq·N(β).
items.locator: Chapter III, §9, p. 265 (paragraph after (9.2); the norm identity is the first line of (9.4))
items.note: Status 'planned' because the ramification computation is not in any library; two ingredients are. (1) Mathlib Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_zmodEq (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean, namespace Nat): '(n : ℕ) {q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : IsCoprime a q) : ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [ZMOD q]'. By CRT this gives the congruence conditions on q modulo the primes l | D. (2) Tau Ceti QuaternionAlgebra.normForm_apply_coordinates (TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/NormForm.lean:82) on ℍ[ℚ, D, 0, −pq] gives normForm = re² − D·imI² + pq·imJ² − Dpq·imK² = N_K(α) + pq·N_K(β). The Hilbert-symbol ramification computation ((D,−pq)_l = 1 at l | D, at 2 since D ≡ 1 mod 4, and at q; = −1 at p and ∞) is planned in QuadraticFormInvariants 6C ('hilbertSymbol a b : ℤˣ ... Bimultiplicativity ... the frozen hilbertSymbol_productFormula'). No Hilbert symbol exists in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (rg 'hilbert ?symbol': 0 hits). Layer 2 plans the norm form and splitting criterion. Checked: ε(q) = Π_{l|D}(q/l) = ε(−p) = ε(−1)ε(p) = (−1)(−1) = 1, so q splits.

items.name: Eichler-order model S and Eichler's connecting-ideal theorem (quoted, Eichler [10, p. 118])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/165 (with −pq ≡ 1 mod D), let S = {α + βj : α ∈ 𝔡^{−1}, β ∈ 𝔡^{−1}𝔮^{−1}𝔫, α ≡ β mod O_𝔣 for every prime 𝔣 of O dividing 𝔡}. S is an order of B with reduced discriminant Np that is locally an Eichler order at every finite l ≠ p, like R = End_{W/π}(x). Eichler: there is an ideal 𝔟 of O with R𝔟 = 𝔟S inside B. The class 𝔅 of 𝔟 depends on v: if v′ = v^{σ_𝔠} then 𝔟′ = 𝔟𝔠, so 𝔅′ = 𝔅𝒞, and Gal(H/K) permutes the classes that arise simply transitively.
items.note: Two defects: S is an order only if −pq ≡ 1 (mod D) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19, lead Mann); and the relation R𝔟 = 𝔟S versus (9.3) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E20). Mann's appendix proves the connecting-ideal statement as Theorem A.15 / Corollary A.16 (Eichler orders with the same reduced discriminant and S ∩ E = S′ ∩ E = O_E are conjugate by an O_E-ideal). Searched the atlas for 'Eichler order', 'optimal embed', 'quaternion order', 'maximal order': no stage plans Eichler orders or this theorem. Nearest: HE.1 ('For quaternionic curves construct optimal embeddings of the specified orders'). Libraries: nothing (rg 'Eichler|QuaternionOrder|maximalOrder': 0 hits in Mathlib and Tau Ceti). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (9.3) Explicit R𝔞 at an inert prime
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). p inert, v | p, 𝔟 as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/166, 𝔞 ∈ 𝒜 (prime to p and to 𝔡). Then R𝔞 = {α + βj : α ∈ 𝔡^{−1}𝔞, β ∈ 𝔡^{−1}𝔮^{−1}𝔫𝔟̄𝔟^{−1}𝔞̄, α ≡ (−1)^{ord_𝔣(𝔟)}β mod O_𝔣 for 𝔣 | 𝔡}. As printed this holds for 𝔟R = S𝔟; with R𝔟 = 𝔟S replace 𝔟̄𝔟^{−1} by 𝔟𝔟̄^{−1} (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E20).
items.note: Mann's (A.8) is the corrected and generalised version (even D; congruence α − X_{𝔞𝔟}β ∈ O_𝔡). Not planned: this is an internal step of GZ's explicit quaternionic method, which no stage names (GZ.7 plans the local identities by YZZ's method; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/169). items.name: (9.4)–(9.6) Ideals 𝔠, 𝔠′ attached to b = α + βj ∈ R𝔞 (inert case)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). p inert. For b = α + βj ∈ R𝔞 with (9.4) N(b) = N(α) + pq·N(β) = m·N(𝔞) and N(b₋) = pq·N(β) ≠ 0, define the integral ideals (9.5) 𝔠 = (α)𝔡𝔞^{−1} and 𝔠′ = (β)𝔡𝔮𝔫^{−1}𝔟̄^{−1}𝔟𝔞̄^{−1}. Then 𝔠 ∈ 𝒜^{−1} and 𝔠′ ∈ 𝒜𝔅²[𝔮𝔫^{−1}], and (9.6) N𝔠 + N·p·N𝔠′ = m|D|. The integer n = p·N𝔠′ is non-zero and ord_p(n) = ord_p(N b₋) (using p ∤ N𝔞). δ(n) = Π_{l | (n,D)} 2 as in Ch. II (3.15).
items.note: Checked (9.6): N𝔠 = N(α)|D|/N𝔞 and N𝔠′ = N(β)|D|q/(N·N𝔞), so N𝔠 + NpN𝔠′ = |D|(Nα + pqNβ)/N𝔞 = m|D|. Class bookkeeping is consistent with the printed (9.3). Not planned (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/167). Mann (A.9)–(A.10). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (9.7) Inert primes: explicit ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p is inert in K (r_𝒜(m) arbitrary), then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p = −r_𝒜(m)·h·u·ord_p(m)·log p − u²·log p·Σ_{0 < n < m|D|/N, n ≡ 0 (mod p)} ord_p(pn)·r_𝒜(m|D| − nN)·δ(n)·R_{{𝒜𝔮𝔫}}(n/p). Here δ(n) = 2^{#{primes l | (n,D)}}, R_{{𝒞}}(k) is the number of integral ideals of norm k in the genus of 𝒞 (Ch. II (3.17)), and 𝔮 | q is the auxiliary prime of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/165. The value does not depend on the choice of q, of 𝔮 | q, or of 𝔫 versus 𝔫̄.

The proof has three defects: the count '2·u²·δ(n)' should be u²·δ(n) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E22); the order S needs −pq ≡ 1 mod D (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19); and 𝔞 must be prime to pD (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E21).
