items.name: (9.8)–(9.10) Ramified-case model: q, B = (D, −q), R𝔞 and the ideals 𝔠, 𝔠′
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). p ramified in K with prime 𝔭; f = order of [𝔭] in Cl_K. There are h/f places v | 𝔭 in H, each with q_v = p^f (printed 'residual degree p^f', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E23). Choose a prime q with (q/p′) = (−1/p′) for all primes p′ ≠ p dividing D and (−q/p) = −1; for the order model one must also impose −q ≡ 1 (mod D/p) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19). Then q = 𝔮𝔮̄ splits in K, B has Hilbert symbol (D, −q), and B = K + Kj with j² = −q. (9.8) R𝔞 = {α + βj : α ∈ 𝔭𝔡^{−1}𝔞, β ∈ 𝔭𝔡^{−1}𝔮^{−1}𝔫𝔟̄𝔟^{−1}𝔞̄, α ≡ (−1)^{ord_𝔣(𝔟)}β mod O_𝔣 for 𝔣 | 𝔡} (β missing in print, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E24). The class of 𝔟 is well defined in Cl_K/[𝔭] by v. For b = α + βj ∈ R𝔞 with N(b) = m·N(𝔞) and N(b₋) ≠ 0, (9.9) 𝔠 = (α)𝔡𝔞^{−1} ∈ 𝒜^{−1} and 𝔠′ = (β)𝔡𝔮𝔫^{−1}𝔟̄^{−1}𝔟𝔞̄^{−1} ∈ 𝒜[𝔮𝔫^{−1}]𝔅² are integral and both divisible by 𝔭, and (9.10) N𝔠 + N·N𝔠′ = m|D|. The integer n = N𝔠′ is non-zero, with ord_p(n) = ord_p(D·N(b₋)).
items.note: Status 'missing' because the explicit order and ideal construction (the substance of the item) is planned nowhere; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/166 and PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/167. Partial support: Dirichlet (Mathlib) for q; the norm identity N(α+βj) = Nα + qNβ in ℍ[ℚ, D, 0, −q] (Tau Ceti normForm_apply_coordinates); the Hilbert-symbol checks (planned, QuadraticFormInvariants 6C). Checked the Hilbert symbols: (D,−q)_{p′} = (−q/p′) = 1 for p′ ≠ p; (D,−q)_p = (−q/p) = −1; trivial at 2 since D ≡ 1 mod 4. Checked (9.10): N𝔠 + N·N𝔠′ = |D|(Nα + qNβ)/N𝔞. Mann (A.6). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (9.11) Ramified primes: explicit ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p is ramified in K with prime 𝔭 (r_𝒜(m) arbitrary), then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p = −r_𝒜(m)·h·u·ord_p(m)·log p − u²·log p·Σ_{0 < n < m|D|/N, n ≡ 0 (mod p)} ord_p(n)·r_𝒜(m|D| − nN)·δ(n)·R_{{𝒜𝔮𝔭𝔫}}(n/p), with δ and R as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/169 and 𝔮 the auxiliary prime of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/170.
items.note: Proof 'arguing as in (9.7)'. Mann, Theorem A.20, re-proves the same formula for all D. He explains that the factor 2 which p contributes to δ(n) is compensated by the missing order-2 action at p and by the h/f versus h counting of places. Plan: method-level GZ.7, as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/169.

items.name: Genus characters of Cl_K and the factorization of their L-series
items.statement: Standing data of Chap. IV (p. 267): K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, ε = ε_D = (D/·), Cl_K its class group; N ≥ 1 prime to D; f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) with Fourier coefficients a(n); L_𝒜(f,s) as in (0.1). A genus character is a character χ: Cl_K → {±1}. Such characters correspond to the decompositions D = D₁·D₂ of D into two fundamental discriminants (one positive, one negative); the character χ_{D₁·D₂} is characterized by χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞) for integral ideals 𝔞 prime to D, where ε_{D_i} is the Dirichlet character of ℚ(√D_i). Its L-series factors: L_K(s, χ_{D₁·D₂}) = L(s, ε_{D₁})·L(s, ε_{D₂}).
items.locator: Chapter IV, introduction, p. 268 (after (0.3); quoted as known)
items.note: Quoted classical fact, used to explain (0.1)–(0.2) and to specialise the main formula. Library: genus theory for imaginary quadratic fields is in Tau Ceti (see the Chapter II and IV genus-theory items: the 2-rank t−1 of Cl_K and the principal genus theorem), but neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti defines the genus character χ_{D₁·D₂} or the L-series of a class-group character, so the factorization is absent. No atlas stage names genus characters (search of stage descriptions for 'genus character': no hit). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (0.4) Factorization of L_K(f, χ_{D₁·D₂}, s) into twisted Hecke L-series
items.statement: Standing data of Chap. IV (p. 267): K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, ε = ε_D = (D/·), Cl_K its class group; N ≥ 1 prime to D; f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) with Fourier coefficients a(n); L_𝒜(f,s) as in (0.1). For χ: Cl_K → ℂ^× put L_K(f,χ,s) = Σ_{𝒜∈Cl_K} χ(𝒜)L_𝒜(f,s) (0.3). If f is a Hecke eigenform, L(f,s) = ∏_p (1−α_p p^{−s})^{−1}(1−β_p p^{−s})^{−1} with α_p+β_p = a(p), α_pβ_p = p^{2k−1} (p∤N), 0 (p|N), and χ = χ_{D₁·D₂} is a genus character, then the convolution of L(f,s) with L_K(s,χ) equals L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε)^{−1}·L(f,ε_{D₁},s)·L(f,ε_{D₂},s), where L(f,ε_{D_i},s) = Σ ε_{D_i}(n)a(n)n^{−s}; hence (0.4) L_K(f, χ_{D₁·D₂}, s) = L(f,ε_{D₁},s)·L(f,ε_{D₂},s). (The printed text writes L^{(N)}(2s+2k−1, ε) here; see the source issue.)
items.note: The weight-2 definition (0.3)/(5.4) is item 'The L-function L(f, χ, s)' of Chapter I. The factorization is planned only in the special case χ = 1, weight 2, rational coefficients: RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 ('construct the existing quadratic twist ... then the factorization L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^K,s)'). No stage plans the genus-character case or weight 2k; the Euler-factor computation behind it is the 'simple calculation' the paper leaves to the reader. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Functional equation of the twisted Hecke L-series L(f, ε_{D_i}, s)
items.statement: Standing data of Chap. IV (p. 267): K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, ε = ε_D = (D/·), Cl_K its class group; N ≥ 1 prime to D; f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) with Fourier coefficients a(n); L_𝒜(f,s) as in (0.1). Let f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) be a newform with Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue w = ±1 under W_N: f(z) ↦ N^{−k}z^{−2k}f(−1/(Nz)), and let D_i be a fundamental discriminant prime to N. Then L(f, ε_{D_i}, s) = Σ ε_{D_i}(n)a(n)n^{−s} has analytic continuation and a functional equation with gamma factor (2π)^{−s}N^{s/2}|D_i|^s Γ(s) and sign (−1)^k ε_{D_i}(−N) w. Consequently, multiplying the two, L_K(f, χ_{D₁·D₂}, s) satisfies a functional equation with the gamma factor and sign of (0.2), independent of w and of the genus character; if ε(N) = 1 exactly one of the two twisted L-series has sign −1, and the main result specialises to a formula for L′(f,ε_{D₁},k)·L(f,ε_{D₂},k) (p. 269).
items.note: Tau Ceti's ModularForms roadmap plans Hecke's functional equation for the completed L-function of a newform (Layer 7: 'The completed L-function and Hecke's functional equation — in AINTLIB's proved form (Modularforms/LFunctionFEqN.lean)') and the twist f ⊗ ψ by a Dirichlet character with its modularity (Layer 9: 'the twist f ⊗ ψ of a q-expansion by a Dirichlet character ψ'), and Layer 6 pins the sign convention i^k·ε_N. The explicit root number (−1)^k ε_{D}(−N) w of a quadratic twist of conductor prime to N is not named in either layer, so the plan covers the functional equation but not the stated sign; the elliptic-curve case of the parity is RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 ('Prove the root-number parity relation').

items.name: Moderate-growth spaces M̃_k(Γ₀(N), χ) and the weight-k slash operator
items.statement: For f: ℌ → ℂ, k ∈ ℤ and γ = (a b; c d) with ad−bc > 0, (f|_kγ)(z) = (ad−bc)^{k/2}(cz+d)^{−k} f((az+b)/(cz+d)). For N ∈ ℕ and a Dirichlet character χ mod N, M̃_k(Γ₀(N), χ) is the space of functions f: ℌ → ℂ, not necessarily holomorphic, such that f|_kγ = χ(d)f for all γ = (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(N), and which have at most polynomial growth at the cusps: for every γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ) there is C > 0 with (f|_kγ)(z) = O(y^C) as y → ∞. The character is omitted when it is trivial.
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for a space of non-holomorphic functions with a Nebentypus transformation law and moderate growth, and found none. Nearest in the libraries: mathlib:SlashInvariantForm (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/SlashInvariantForms.lean:34) has invariance under a subgroup of GL(2,ℝ) but no character and no growth condition. Mathlib's slash (SlashActions.lean:92) is σ(γ)(f(γz))·|det γ|^{k−1}·(cz+d)^{−k}; it agrees with GZ's (ad−bc)^{k/2} normalisation on SL₂ only. tauceti:modFormCharSpace is holomorphic only (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/176). Nearest plans, neither of which is this classical space: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.0 ('Define height functions … and independence of the moderate-growth condition', adelic) and QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3 (harmonic Maass forms with 'growth conditions, holomorphic/nonholomorphic Fourier parts'). The slash formula and the space are stated on p. 270, the page where this chunk starts; the chunk that covers §0 may list them too. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Holomorphic spaces M_k(Γ₀(N), χ) and S_k(Γ₀(N), χ)
items.statement: M_k(Γ₀(N), χ) and S_k(Γ₀(N), χ) are the subspaces of M̃_k(Γ₀(N), χ) consisting of holomorphic modular forms and holomorphic cusp forms. Used here with (k, N, χ) = (1, |D|, ε) for θ_𝒜, and (2k, N, trivial) for f.
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/DiamondOperators.lean:315 defines `modFormCharSpace (k : ℤ) (χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ) : Submodule ℂ (ModularForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k)` as the joint χ-eigenspace of the diamond operators. :279 defines `cuspFormCharSpace` in the same way. :344 `mem_modFormCharSpace_iff_nebentypus` proves that membership is equivalent to `∀ g : Γ₀(N), f ∣[k] g = χ((Gamma0Map N).toHomUnits g) • f`, the classical Nebentypus law. Mathlib's `ModularForm`/`CuspForm` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Basic.lean:74, 82) with `CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0` (CongruenceSubgroups.lean:79) cover the trivial-character case. This is the same notion; Tau Ceti puts the character on Γ₁(N)-forms rather than defining a separate type.

items.name: Theta series θ_𝒜 of an ideal class (1.1)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. θ_𝒜(z) = Σ_{n≥0} r_𝒜(n) qⁿ = (1/w) Σ_{λ∈𝔞} q^{N(λ)/A}, where 𝔞 is any ideal in the class 𝒜 and A = N(𝔞).
items.note: No theta series of a lattice or quadratic form in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Searched for 'theta series', 'thetaSeries' and `def .*[tT]heta`. Mathlib has only the one-variable Jacobi theta functions (JacobiTheta/OneVariable.lean, TwoVariable.lean). GN.3 plans the carrier: 'Construct reduction domains and arithmetic quotients, local representation densities, mass formulas and theta-series interfaces.' Partial coverage: GN.3 does not plan the specialisation to the norm form of an ideal class, or the identity with the ideal-counting function r_𝒜. MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5 ('For a rational quadratic/symplectic datum define the theta series by summing the transformed Schwartz function over rational vectors') is the adelic version.

items.name: θ_𝒜 is a weight-one modular form of level |D| with character ε (quoted)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. θ_𝒜 ∈ M₁(Γ₀(|D|), ε), i.e. θ_𝒜 is holomorphic on ℌ and at the cusps, and θ_𝒜((az+b)/(cz+d)) = ε(d)(cz+d)θ_𝒜(z) for all (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(|D|). The paper cites this as known ('It is known that θ_𝒜 belongs to M₁(Γ₀(D), ε)'); Lemma (2.3) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/194) re-proves the transformation under all of SL₂(ℤ) when D is odd.
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for modularity of theta series of binary quadratic forms or ideal classes, and for weight-one forms with quadratic character, and found none. The nearest library results are mathlib:jacobiTheta_S_smul (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/JacobiTheta/OneVariable.lean:43) and jacobiTheta₂_functional_equation (TwoVariable.lean:465), which cover one-variable theta only. Nearest plan: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5 ('Prove … transformation under rational points, moderate growth and the specified central character using Poisson summation'). That is the adelic theta kernel; the comparison with the classical level-|D| weight-1 form with Nebentypus ε is not planned (MP.7 compares with classical forms only for half-integral weight). Classical source: Hecke; Schoeneberg, Elliptic modular functions, Ch. IX. Routed (source) to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.3.

items.name: Non-holomorphic Eisenstein series E_s = E_{M,ε,2k−1,s} of level M = N|D|
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. With M = N|D|: E_s(z) = E_{M,ε,2k−1,s}(z) = L^{(N)}(2s+2k−1, ε) Σ_{±(∗ ∗; c d) ∈ Γ_∞\Γ₀(M)} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s |cz+d|^{−2s} = ½ Σ_{c,d∈ℤ, c≡0 (mod M), (d,M)=1} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s |cz+d|^{−2s}, for Re(s) large. Here L^{(N)}(s, ε) = Σ_{(n,N)=1} ε(n)n^{−s} and Γ_∞ = {±(1 n; 0 1)}. E_s ∈ M̃_{2k−1}(Γ₀(M), ε). (The two expressions agree: pull out g = gcd(c,d), which is prime to M, and pair ±(c,d) using ε(−1)(−1)^{2k−1} = 1.)
items.note: Mathlib's `eisensteinSeries` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/Defs.lean:205) is holomorphic, of level Γ(N), indexed by a congruence class a, with no y^s factor and no Dirichlet character, so it is not this series. Nothing in Tau Ceti: searched 'Eisenstein', 'eisensteinSeries', 'nonHolomorphic', 'realAnalytic'. The nearest plan is the packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series (stage EllipticRegulators:ER.7): 'E_x(z, s) = Σ′ y^s / |mz + n|^{2s} … (m, n) ≡ (u, v) mod N'. That is weight 0 with no odd character, a different series. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.1–AS.2 plan adelic Eisenstein series and their continuation, not this classical one. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Petersson scalar product on Γ₀(M)
items.statement: For f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(M)) and g ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(M)): (f, g)_{Γ₀(M)} = ∬_𝓕 f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dxdy/y², where 𝓕 is a fundamental domain for Γ₀(M). The integral is unnormalised: no division by the volume.
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/Basic.lean:107: `def peterssonInner (k : ℤ) (D : Set ℍ) (f g : ℍ → ℂ) : ℂ := ∫ τ in D, petersson k f g τ`. Its integrand is Mathlib's `UpperHalfPlane.petersson k f f' τ = conj (f τ) * f' τ * τ.im ^ k` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson.lean:31). Convention: Tau Ceti is conjugate-linear in the first argument, so GZ's (f, g)_{Γ₀(M)} = peterssonInner (2k) 𝓕 g f with 𝓕 a Γ₀(M)-fundamental domain. :163 `peterssonInner_eq_of_isFundamentalDomain` proves independence of the domain for any slash-invariant F, F′, so holomorphy is not required. That covers the (cusp form, non-holomorphic form) pairing used here, but integrability of such a pairing is not proved in the library. The bundled `CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets` (Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:94) is for two cusp forms only. ModularForms Layer 3 (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-3-the-petersson-inner-product-adjoints-oldforms-and-newforms) is the owner.

items.name: Rankin unfolding: L_𝒜(f, s+2k−1) as a Petersson product with θ_𝒜 E_s̄ on Γ₀(M)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Let f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (any cusp form) and M = N|D|. For Re(s) large, Γ(s+2k−1)(4π)^{−s−2k+1} L_𝒜(f, s+2k−1) = ∬_𝓕 f(z) \overline{θ_𝒜(z) E_s̄(z)} y^{2k} dxdy/y² = (f, θ_𝒜 E_s̄)_{Γ₀(M)}, with E_s as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/179 and 𝓕 a fundamental domain for Γ₀(M). Proof as printed: Γ(s+2k−1)(4π)^{−s−2k+1} Σ a(n)r_𝒜(n)n^{−s−2k+1} = ∬_{Γ_∞\ℌ} f \overline{θ_𝒜} y^{s+2k} dxdy/y². Then write Γ_∞\ℌ = ∪_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\Γ₀(M)} γ𝓕, use the transformation laws of f and θ_𝒜 under Γ₀(M), and interchange sum and integral.
items.note: No Rankin–Selberg unfolding for classical modular forms in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Searched 'Rankin'; the only Tau Ceti hit is an unrelated ideal count in EffectiveBounds/IdealCount. Nearest plans: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3 ('Prove unramified calculations and the global unfolding for cuspidal data') is adelic GL_n×GL_m with cuspidal data, whereas θ_𝒜 is not cuspidal and the Eisenstein kernel is not planned. The packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/rankin-selberg-integral unfolds a weight-2 form against a weight-0 real-analytic Eisenstein series: 'Unfold to ∫_{Γ∞\H} and use the constant term'. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans the adelic YZZ analytic kernel ('Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels'), not this classical identity. The paper writes E_s̄ (the conjugate parameter), so the identity is holomorphic in s on both sides. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Trace map Tr^M_N
items.statement: For N | M: Tr^M_N: M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(M)) → M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), g ↦ Σ_{γ ∈ Γ₀(M)\Γ₀(N)} g|_{2k}γ.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/NormTrace.lean:55: `protected def SlashInvariantForm.trace [𝒢.IsFiniteRelIndex ℋ] : SlashInvariantForm ℋ k`. It is `∑ q : ℋ ⧸ 𝒢.subgroupOf ℋ, quotientFunc f q`, with `quotientFunc f ⟦h⟧ = f ∣[k] h⁻¹` (:43), i.e. the sum over the right cosets (𝒢 ⊓ ℋ)\ℋ of f|γ. It is defined for any 𝒢-slash-invariant function, holomorphic or not, which is what GZ need here with 𝒢 = Γ₀(M), ℋ = Γ₀(N). `ModularForm.trace` (:82) is the holomorphic version. Same construction. The library does not prove that the trace preserves the moderate-growth condition of M̃, because M̃ itself is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/175).

items.name: Trace adjointness for the Petersson product
items.statement: For N | M, f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) and g ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(M)): (f, g)_{Γ₀(M)} = (f, Tr^M_N g)_{Γ₀(N)}. Consequently (4π)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)L_𝒜(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Tr^M_N(θ_𝒜 E_s̄))_{Γ₀(N)} for Re(s) large, with M = N|D|.
items.note: The Petersson integral exists (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/180) and so does the trace (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/182), but no lemma relates them: searched 'trace' in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/*.lean and Norm/Trace.lean, with no hit. The proof is the fundamental-domain decomposition 𝓕_M = ∪_{γ ∈ Γ₀(M)\Γ₀(N)} γ𝓕_N together with the invariance of the integrand, which is TauCeti `UpperHalfPlane.petersson_smul_of_mem` (Petersson/Basic.lean). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-3-the-petersson-inner-product-adjoints-oldforms-and-newforms plans the Petersson product and Hecke adjoints, not trace adjointness. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Möbius decomposition of E_s and discarding the lower-level terms
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. With M = N|D| and E^{(1)}_s as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/185: E_s(z) = ½ Σ_{e|N} μ(e) Σ_{c,d∈ℤ, M|c, e|d} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s|cz+d|^{−2s} = Σ_{e|N} μ(e)ε(e) e^{−(2s+2k−1)} (N/e)^{−s} E^{(1)}_s(Nz/e). Only e squarefree and prime to D contribute. For e > 1 the term Tr^M_N(θ_𝒜(z)E^{(1)}_s(Nz/e)) has level N/e < N: any system of representatives of Γ₀(M)\Γ₀(N) is one of Γ₀(M/e)\Γ₀(N/e), because (e, D) = 1. Hence, for f ∈ S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), those terms are orthogonal to f. For non-holomorphic terms this uses §5: the product of f with a non-holomorphic form equals its product with a holomorphic form of the same level.
items.note: Checked the substitution c = N c″, d = e d″ (the paper's 'replacing c, d by c/N, d/e'). The coset claim follows because Γ₀(N) ∩ Γ₀(M/e) = Γ₀(lcm(N, N|D|/e)) = Γ₀(M) and both indices equal ψ(|D|). The coset claim has no library support; the index is known in Tau Ceti only for prime powers (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0_prime_index, Gamma0_prime_power_index in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups/Basic.lean). Orthogonality of S^new to level-raised forms is the definition tauceti:TauCeti.cuspFormsNew (Newforms/Basic.lean:200, the Petersson-orthogonal complement of cuspFormsOld), but only for holomorphic cusp forms. The non-holomorphic case needs holomorphic projection (§5, not in this chunk; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans 'holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection' adelically). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Level-|D| Eisenstein series E^{(1)}_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. E^{(1)}_s(z) = ½ Σ_{c,d∈ℤ, D|c} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s |cz+d|^{−2s} (Re(s) large): the non-holomorphic Eisenstein series of level |D|, weight 2k−1 and Nebentypus ε. It is E_s with N replaced by 1, and the case D₁ = 1 of (2.1) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/192).
items.note: Same search and nearest items as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/179: Mathlib eisensteinSeries is holomorphic with no character; the plan EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series is weight 0. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The Rankin kernel Φ̃_s = Φ̃_{s,𝒜}
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Φ̃_s(z) = Φ̃_{s,𝒜}(z) = Tr^{ND}_N(θ_𝒜(z) E^{(1)}_s(Nz)) ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), where Tr^{ND}_N means Tr^{N|D|}_N (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/182). Its Fourier expansion in x is Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} A_m(s, y) e(mx) (1.3).
items.note: Not in the libraries: its ingredients θ_𝒜 and E^{(1)}_s are missing, although the trace exists (mathlib:SlashInvariantForm.trace). Nearest plan: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6, 'Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms, holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection', which is the adelic YZZ analogue on quaternionic Shimura curves. No stage plans the classical kernel on X₀(N) or its specialisation from the YZZ kernel. GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)' specialises the final height identity, not the analytic kernel. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (1.2): L_𝒜(f, s) as the Petersson product of f with the Rankin kernel
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Let D be a fundamental discriminant, N ≥ 1 prime to D, and define Φ̃_s = Φ̃_{s,𝒜} ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) by Φ̃_s(z) = Tr^{ND}_N(θ_𝒜(z) E^{(1)}_s(Nz)), where θ_𝒜 is the theta series (1.1) and E^{(1)}_s(z) = ½ Σ_{c,d∈ℤ, D|c} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s|cz+d|^{−2s}. Then for every f ∈ S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)): (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_𝒜(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s̄), first for Re(s) large, with the Petersson product (f, g) = ∬_{Γ₀(N)\ℌ} f ḡ y^{2k} dxdy/y².
items.note: Checked: PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/181 + PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/183 + PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/184. The e = 1 term of E_s̄ is N^{−s̄}E^{(1)}_s̄(Nz), and antilinearity turns it into N^{−s}, which gives the factor N^s. The printed statement has Φ̃_s̄, with the bar; the 722 px page image img/p272.png hides it, the 1400 px crop shows it. No library or atlas coverage (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/181, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/186). The nearest plan is GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 (adelic analytic kernel), which does not plan this classical identity. Route: the classical GZ Chapter IV analytic side is unplanned, so a GZ Part II or a source route into GZ.6 is needed. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Remark after (1.2): only the Fourier coefficients of Φ̃_s with index prime to N matter
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Write Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} A_m(s, y)e(mx) (1.3). The proof of (1.2) used only the orthogonality of f with forms of level strictly dividing N. f ∈ S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) is also orthogonal to g(dz) for d > 1 and g of level dividing N/d, so in (1.2) only the A_m(s, y) with (m, N) = 1 are relevant. If Φ̃, Φ̃′ ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (with the growth of §5) have A_m = A′_m for all m prime to N, then (f, Φ̃) = (f, Φ̃′). In particular, the functional equation (0.2) and the formulas for L_𝒜(f, k) and L′_𝒜(f, k) reduce to identities for A_m(s, y), (m, N) = 1.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §1, Remark after (1.2) and (1.3), p. 272
items.note: The holomorphic core is in the library (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/189): a holomorphic form whose coefficients vanish at all indices prime to N is old. Applying it to Φ̃ − Φ̃′ needs holomorphic projection (§5), which is missing: no Sturm holomorphic projection in the libraries, while GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans it adelically. The paper asserts the remark without proof; it follows from Atkin–Lehner theory plus §5, so it is not recorded as a gap. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner Main Lemma (used implicitly in the Remark after (1.2))
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, k ∈ ℤ, χ a character of (ℤ/N)ˣ. If g ∈ S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) has Fourier coefficients a_n(g) = 0 for every n prime to N, then g lies in the old subspace; hence g is Petersson-orthogonal to S_k^new(Γ₁(N)). GZ use it with χ trivial: S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) is orthogonal to the forms g(dz), d > 1, with g of level dividing N/d.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §1, Remark after (1.2), p. 272 (not stated explicitly; Atkin–Lehner, Math. Ann. 185 (1970), Lemma 6)
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/MainLemma.lean:178: `theorem mem_cuspFormsOld_of_forall_coprime_qExpansion_coeff_eq_zero {χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ} {f : CuspForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k} (hf : f ∈ cuspFormCharSpace k χ) (hvan : ∀ n, Nat.Coprime n N → (qExpansion 1 f).coeff n = 0) : f ∈ cuspFormsOld N k` (Miyake Lemma 4.6.8). `cuspFormsNew N k` (Newforms/Basic.lean:200) is the Petersson-orthogonal complement of `cuspFormsOld N k` (:103, spanned by the level raises V_d from proper divisor levels). Same statement for holomorphic cusp forms. The GZ remark applies it to the holomorphic projection of a non-holomorphic form, which is not covered (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/188).

items.name: Cusps of Γ₀(D) correspond to the positive divisors of D
items.statement: In general a cusp of Γ₀(n) is specified by a divisor n′ of n and an element of (ℤ/(n′, n/n′)ℤ)ˣ. If 16 ∤ n and p² ∤ n for every odd prime p (e.g. n = |D|, D a fundamental discriminant), the cusps of Γ₀(n) are in bijection with the positive divisors of n. In §2 a cusp is labelled by δ₁ | δ, with δ₂ = δ/δ₁ = (c, D) for a matrix (a b; c d) sending ∞ to it.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean defines the cusps of a subgroup of GL(2,ℝ) (fixed points of parabolic elements) but does not classify the cusps of Γ₀(n). TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Basic.lean has cusp widths only (TauCeti.Subgroup.integerCuspWidth). Searched for Γ₀ cusp counts, 'totient.*gcd' and 'card.*cusp', with no hit. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#layer-10-compactified-coarse-curves-over-ℤ1n-cusps-and-the-shimura-covering counts cusps only for Γ₁(N)-quotients of prime level N ≥ 5, not Γ₀(n). Only the |D| squarefree odd case is used after the restriction to odd D. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Decomposition data D = D₁·D₂ (δ_i, ε_i, 𝔡_i, 𝒟₁, κ, c*) and the restriction to odd D
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Write δ = |D|, δ₁ | δ a positive divisor, δ₂ = δ/δ₁. δ_i = N(𝔡_i) for unique integral ideals 𝔡_i of K that are products of ramified primes. If (δ₁, δ₂) = 1 there are unique fundamental discriminants D₁, D₂ (1 allowed) with δ_i = |D_i| and D₁D₂ = D; then ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character of §0, 𝒟₁ is the class of 𝔡₁ (𝔡₁² = (D₁)), and κ(D₁) = 1 if D₁ > 0, i if D₁ < 0. For odd D, (δ₁, δ₂) = 1 always; for even D, (δ₁, δ₂) = 2 can occur. The paper assumes from here on that D is odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4). For c prime to D₁, c* denotes an inverse of c modulo D₁; in (2.2) it is also chosen ≡ 0 (mod D₂).
items.note: The integer-level genus characters are in Tau Ceti: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFun (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:212, a product of prime-discriminant characters), with the factorisation of a fundamental discriminant into prime discriminants (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsFundamentalDiscriminant.exists_finset_primeDiscriminant, FundamentalDiscriminant/Factorization.lean:131). The ideal-class character χ_{D₁·D₂}: Cl_K → {±1} is 'deliberately not yet packaged as a character of the narrow class group' (GenusCharacter/Narrow.lean docstring), and the genus character itself is §0's item. The package (𝔡_i, 𝒟₁, κ, c*) is bookkeeping with no library counterpart. Conrad (2004, §1) notes that GZ's analytic results are proved only for odd D, and that the main results would extend to even D 'provided the analytic results in [GZ] are proven for even discriminants'. This is the restriction made here. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Eisenstein series E^{(D₁)}_s attached to a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ (2.1)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. E^{(D₁)}_s(z) = ½ Σ_{m,n∈ℤ, D₂|m} ε₁(m)ε₂(n) (mz+n)^{−(2k−1)} y^s |mz+n|^{−2s} (Re(s) large). For D₁ = 1 this is E^{(1)}_s, and E^{(D₁)}_s ∈ M̃_{2k−1}(Γ₀(D), ε) ('as is easily checked': under (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(D), ε₁(ma+nc)ε₂(mb+nd) = ε₁(a)ε₂(d)ε₁(m)ε₂(n) = ε(d)ε₁(m)ε₂(n)).
items.note: Same search as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/179: no non-holomorphic Eisenstein series with a pair of characters in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. The nearest plan, EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series, is weight 0 with congruence classes and no character. The Γ₀(D)-invariance claim was checked here by the substitution (m, n) ↦ (m, n)γ. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Transformation of E^{(1)}_s under SL₂(ℤ) (2.2)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with (c, D) = |D₂|, D₁D₂ = D, and c* an inverse of c (mod D₁) with c* ≡ 0 (mod D₂): (E^{(1)}_s|_{2k−1}γ)(z) = ε_{D₁}(c) ε_{D₂}(dδ₁) δ₁^{−s−2k+1} E^{(D₁)}_s((z + c*d)/δ₁), where (F|_{2k−1}γ)(z) = (cz+d)^{−(2k−1)}F(γz).
items.note: Verified: replace (m, n) by γ^{−1}(m, n), and use md ≡ nc (mod D) ⇒ ε(an−bm) = ε₁(c)ε₁(m)ε₂(d)ε₂(n). Then md ≡ nc (mod D) ⇔ D₂ | m and n ≡ c*md (mod D₁); set n = c*md + δ₁n′. No library counterpart, since E^{(D₁)}_s is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/192). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Lemma (2.3): transformation of θ_𝒜 under SL₂(ℤ)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ) (printed 'PSL₂(ℤ)', see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E30) with (c, D) = |D₂|, D₁·D₂ = D, and c* an inverse of c (mod D₁): (θ_𝒜|₁γ)(z) = ε_{D₁}(c/δ₂) ε_{D₂}(d) κ(D₁)^{−1} δ₁^{−1/2} χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}((z + c*d)/δ₁), where κ(D₁) = 1 or i according as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0, and 𝒟₁ is the class of 𝔡₁ with 𝔡₁² = (D₁).
items.note: Proof checked line by line. The reduction to c = δ₂ goes via γ₁ = (∗ ∗; δ₂ x), γ₀ = γγ₁^{−1} ∈ Γ₀(D). Then: split λ modulo 𝔞𝔡₂; 2-dimensional Poisson summation (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/195); substitute ν ↦ ν/δ₂; take the representatives λ₀μ; complete the square with R*; evaluate the quadratic Gauss sum (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/196); and identify ε_{D₂}(R) = ε_{D₂}(d)χ(𝒜). Sanity check: γ = S = (0 −1; 1 0) gives θ_𝒜(−1/z)/z = −iδ^{−1/2}θ_𝒜(z/δ), which also follows from lattice Poisson summation (dual lattice 𝔞𝔡^{−1}). No library support: θ_𝒜 is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/177, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/178). Nearest plan: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5 (adelic theta transformation), with no classical specialisation planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Poisson summation over an ideal lattice of K
items.statement: For any z ∈ ℌ, any fractional ideal 𝔟 of K and any λ ∈ ℂ = K⊗ℝ: Σ_{μ∈𝔟} e(N(λ+μ)z) = (iδ^{−1/2}/(N(𝔟)z)) Σ_{ν ∈ 𝔟^{−1}𝔡^{−1}} e(−N(ν)/z) e(Tr λν), where 𝔡 is the different of K (N(𝔡) = δ), N(x) = |x|² and Tr(x) = x + x̄. (Consider the left side as a periodic function of λ ∈ ℂ/𝔟 and compute its Fourier development.)
items.note: Checked: covol(𝔟) = N(𝔟)√δ/2; the dual of 𝔟 for x·ξ = Re(x ξ̄) is 2𝔟̄^{−1}𝔡^{−1}; the Fourier transform of e(z|x|²) on ℝ² is (i/(2z))e(−|ξ|²/(4z)). Mathlib has only one-dimensional Poisson summation: `Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_of_rpow_decay` (Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/PoissonSummation.lean:205), `SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier` (:219) and `Complex.tsum_exp_neg_quadratic` (Gaussian/PoissonSummation.lean:86). Nothing for lattices in ℝ² or for ideal lattices in Tau Ceti. Nearest plans: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0 ('Prove Fourier inversion … and adelic Poisson summation, with the diagonal lattice and volume from GlobalNumberFields') and MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5. Specialising adelic Poisson summation to this classical identity is not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Evaluation of the quadratic Gauss sum Σ_{n mod δ₂} e_{δ₂}(Rn²)
items.statement: Let D₂ be an odd fundamental discriminant, δ₂ = |D₂| (squarefree), and R an integer prime to δ₂. Then Σ_{μ ∈ O/𝔡₂} e_{δ₂}(R N(μ)) = Σ_{n ∈ ℤ/δ₂ℤ} e_{δ₂}(Rn²) = κ(D₂) δ₂^{1/2} ε_{D₂}(R), with κ(D₂) = 1 if D₂ > 0 and i if D₂ < 0. The first equality holds because δ₂ is squarefree and totally ramified, so ℤ/δ₂ represents O/𝔡₂. The second is 'the usual evaluation of Gauss sums', Gauss's sign determination included.
items.note: Mathlib has the square but not the sign: `gaussSum_sq` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:222) gives τ(χ)² = χ(−1)·#R for a nontrivial quadratic χ and a primitive ψ, so τ = ±√D₂. The sign (τ = +√D₂, i.e. +i√δ₂ when D₂ < 0) is Gauss's theorem and is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Tau Ceti's TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Cyclotomic/GaussSum.lean only extracts a square root of p* in a cyclotomic field. The reduction Σ_n e(Rn²/δ₂) = (R/δ₂)·Σ_n e(n²/δ₂) is also absent for composite squarefree δ₂. Nearest plans: FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.1 ('Construct … Gauss and Jacobi sums and their norm/product identities') and AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1 ('functional equations include conductor, Gauss sum and parity'); neither states the sign determination. Routed (source) to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1.

items.name: Gauss sum of the primitive character ε_{D₂}: Σ_{n mod δ₂} ε₂(n)e(rn/δ₂) = ε₂(r)κ(D₂)δ₂^{1/2}
items.statement: For D₂ a fundamental discriminant (odd here), δ₂ = |D₂| and every r ∈ ℤ: Σ_{n mod δ₂} ε_{D₂}(n) e(rn/δ₂) = ε_{D₂}(r) κ(D₂) δ₂^{1/2}. The right side is 0 when (r, δ₂) > 1.
items.note: Partly in the library. `gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/GaussSum.lean:57): for primitive χ, `gaussSum χ (e.mulShift a) = χ⁻¹ a * gaussSum χ e`. That gives Σ ε₂(n)e(rn/δ₂) = ε₂(r)τ(ε₂) for all r, zero included. The value τ(ε_{D₂}) = √D₂ = κ(D₂)√δ₂ is the missing sign determination of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/196. Routed (source) to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1.

items.name: Reciprocity ε_{D₁}(δ₂) ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1
items.statement: Let D = D₁D₂ < 0 with D₁, D₂ coprime odd fundamental discriminants (one of them may be 1), δ_i = |D_i|. Then ε_{D₁}(δ₂) ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §2, p. 276 ('where we have used ε_{D₁}(δ₂)ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1')
items.note: Proof: for D_i ≡ 1 (mod 4) and n > 0, ε_{D_i}(n) = (n/δ_i) (Jacobi symbol). Since D < 0, exactly one of D₁, D₂ is negative, so one δ_i is ≡ 1 (mod 4). Then Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/JacobiSymbol.lean:431 `jacobiSym.quadratic_reciprocity_one_mod_four {a b : ℕ} (ha : a % 4 = 1) (hb : Odd b) : J(a | b) = J(b | a)` gives (δ₂/δ₁) = (δ₁/δ₂), and the product is (δ₁/δ₂)² = 1. The library has the general law. The identification ε_D(n) = J(n | |D|) for a fundamental discriminant D is not stated in Mathlib. Tau Ceti identifies the genus character of the full prime-discriminant factorisation with the splitting symbol (d/q) at odd primes q (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFun_natCast_eq_legendreSym, GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:308); passing from (D/q) to (q/|D|) is Jacobi reciprocity again.

items.name: Coset representatives of Γ₀(ND)\Γ₀(N)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. [Γ₀(N) : Γ₀(N|D|)] = Σ_{δ₁|δ} δ₁. The cosets Γ₀(N|D|)γ, γ = (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(N), are classified by δ₂ = (c, D) together with the residue class of c*d modulo δ₁ = δ/δ₂. So Tr^{ND}_N F = Σ_{D=D₁D₂} Σ_{j mod δ₁} F|_{2k}γ_{D₁,j}, where γ_{D₁,j} is any representative with (c, D) = δ₂ and c*d ≡ j (mod δ₁).
items.note: It is the P¹(ℤ/δ)-parametrisation of Γ₀(δ)\SL₂(ℤ) transported to level N, using (N, D) = 1. Tau Ceti has only prime-level indices: `CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0_prime_index : (Gamma0 p).index = p + 1` and `Gamma0_prime_power_index` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups/Basic.lean:489, 574). No general coset classification and no multiplicativity in coprime levels. No atlas stage plans it. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The operator U_n on 1-periodic functions
items.statement: For n ∈ ℕ and a function f on ℌ of period 1: (f|U_n)(z) = (1/n) Σ_{j mod n} f((z+j)/n). On Fourier expansions, Σ_{m∈ℤ} A_m(y)e(mx) ↦ Σ_{m∈ℤ} A_{mn}(y/n)e(mx).
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/UpperTri/Sum.lean:70: `noncomputable def heckeSlashUpperTri (f : ℍ → ℂ) : ℍ → ℂ := ∑ b : Fin p, f ∣[k] upperTriRep p b` with upperTriRep p b = !![1, b; 0, p] (HeckeRing/GL2/CosetDecomposition.lean:141, 145). Mathlib's slash gives f∣[k](1 b; 0 p) (τ) = p^{k−1}·p^{−k}·f((τ+b)/p). So heckeSlashUpperTri k p f = (1/p)Σ_b f((τ+b)/p) = f|U_p for every weight k and every function f, holomorphic or not; p is any natural number, not only a prime. This is the same operator. The coefficient rule is in the library only for holomorphic forms: `qExpansion_coeff_heckeSlashUpperTri'` (UpperTri/QExpansion.lean:233) gives a_m(U_p f) = a_{pm}(f). The rule A_m(y) ↦ A_{mn}(y/n) for non-holomorphic 1-periodic functions is not stated (it is immediate from the definition).

items.name: Passing from U_{δ₁} to U_δ via θ_𝒜𝒟₁(δ₂z) and θ_𝒜(z)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For every 1-periodic function f on ℌ: (f(z)θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}(z))|U_{δ₁} = (f(δ₂z)θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}(δ₂z))|U_δ = (f(δ₂z)θ_𝒜(z))|U_δ. The reason is that θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}(δ₂z) and θ_𝒜(z) have the same n-th Fourier coefficient for every n divisible by δ₂: r_{𝒜𝒟₁}(n/δ₂) = r_𝒜(n). This holds because 𝒜𝒟₁ = 𝒜𝒟₂ and every integral ideal of norm n (δ₂ | n) is 𝔡₂ times an integral ideal of norm n/δ₂.
items.note: Checked: (g(δ₂z))|U_δ = g|U_{δ₁} for 1-periodic g. In the Fourier coefficient of index m ≡ 0 (mod δ) of f(δ₂z)h(z), only the coefficients of h at multiples of δ₂ occur. The ideal-counting identity (𝔡₂ divides every ideal whose norm is divisible by δ₂, δ₂ squarefree and totally ramified) is not in the libraries. Its ingredients are: r_𝒜 (not in library), and the ramified prime above p | D being the unique prime above p, which is in Mathlib's Dedekind-domain API. No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The Eisenstein combination ℰ_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. ℰ_s(z) = Σ_{D=D₁·D₂} ε_{D₁}(N) χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) / (κ(D₁)|D₁|^{s+2k−3/2}) · E^{(D₁)}_s(|D₂|z), the sum over all decompositions of D as a product of two fundamental discriminants. ℰ_s depends on N (in fact only on N mod D) and on 𝒜 (in fact only on the genus of 𝒜); the paper suppresses this in the notation.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §2, (2.4) Proposition and the note after it, pp. 276–277
items.note: Not in the libraries: E^{(D₁)}_s and the class-group genus character χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) are missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/192, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/191). No stage plans this classical combination. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans the adelic analytic kernel. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (2.4): the Rankin kernel as U_{|D|} of ℰ_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. Assume (D, 2N) = 1. Then Φ̃_s(z) = Tr^{ND}_N(E^{(1)}_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z)) from Proposition (1.2) equals (ℰ_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z))|U_{|D|}, where ℰ_s(z) = Σ_{D=D₁·D₂} ε_{D₁}(N)χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜)/(κ(D₁)|D₁|^{s+2k−3/2}) E^{(D₁)}_s(|D₂|z), summed over all decompositions of D as a product of two fundamental discriminants D₁, D₂. χ_{D₁·D₂} is the corresponding genus character, κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0, and E^{(D₁)}_s is the Eisenstein series (2.1).
items.note: Checked. For γ ∈ Γ₀(N) with (c, D) = δ₂, (2.2) and (2.3) give E^{(1)}_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z)|_{2k}γ = ε₁(N)κ(D₁)^{−1}δ₁^{−s−2k+1/2}χ(𝒜)E^{(D₁)}_s(N(z+c*d)/δ₁)θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}((z+c*d)/δ₁), using ε_{D₁}(δ₂)ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/198). Then sum over the coset representatives (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/199), convert Σ_j to δ₁·U_{δ₁} (factor δ₁^{−s−2k+3/2}), and apply PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/201. (The page's 'From (2.3) and (2.4)' should read '(2.2) and (2.3)'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E32.) No library or plan (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/186, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/202). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Special case of ℰ_s: k = 1, |D| = p prime, ε(N) = 1
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. If k = 1, |D| = p is prime (so D = −p, p ≡ 3 mod 4) and ε(N) = 1, then ℰ_s(z) = E^{(1)}_s(pz) − i p^{−s−1/2} E^{(D)}_s(z) (printed with superscript (p); see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E33).
items.note: Direct from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/202: the decompositions are (1, D) and (D, 1), with κ(D) = i and χ_{D·1} trivial. It is the simplest instance of the weight-2 (k = 1), ε(N) = 1 setting of the main theorem. No library or plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.
