items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. Write ℰ_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} e_s(n, y) e(nx) (z = x+iy ∈ ℌ). Then Φ̃_{s,𝒜}(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_𝒜(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ), with δ = |D|.
items.note: Immediate from (2.4) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/203). Multiply ℰ_s(Nz) = Σ e_s(n, Ny)e(nNx) by θ_𝒜(z) = Σ_{l≥0} r_𝒜(l)e^{−2πly}e(lx), then apply U_δ, which keeps the indices Nn+l ≡ 0 (mod δ) and replaces y by y/δ (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/200). No library or plan, since the kernel is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/186). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The sign function ε_𝒜(n, d)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For n ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} and d a positive divisor of n: ε(n, d) = ε_𝒜(n, d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1, and ε(n, d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−N n/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) if (d, n/d, D) = 1, where D = D₁D₂ is the decomposition with (d, D) = |D₂|.
items.note: When (d, n/d, D) = 1 the decomposition is determined by d, and the value is in {±1}. It depends on the class-group genus character χ_{D₁·D₂}, which is not packaged in Tau Ceti (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/191). No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The archimedean integral V_s(t)
items.statement: Fix k ≥ 1. For s ∈ ℂ with Re(s) > 1−k and t ∈ ℝ: V_s(t) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞} e^{−2πixt} dx / ((x+i)^{2k−1}(x²+1)^s). This is the Fourier transform of x ↦ (x+i)^{−(2k−1)}(x²+1)^{−s}, which is absolutely integrable exactly when Re(s) > 1−k.
items.note: The paper notes that tables express V_s(t) through Whittaker functions but 'the results found in various tables do not agree', so it proves every property directly (p. 279). Mathlib and Tau Ceti have no Whittaker or K-Bessel functions; searched 'whittaker', 'bessel', 'confluent', and found only Mathlib's OrdinaryHypergeometric/RegularizedHypergeometric (₂F₁). Nearest plan: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 ('normalized local Whittaker terms' of the incoherent Eisenstein kernel). That is the adelic analogue: V_s is the archimedean Whittaker function of the weight-(2k−1) Eisenstein series, but GZ.6 plans neither this classical normalisation nor its properties. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Poisson (Lipschitz-type) identity for Σ_l (z+l)^{−(2k−1)}|z+l|^{−2s}
items.statement: For k ≥ 1, z = x+iy ∈ ℌ and Re(s) > 1−k: Σ_{l∈ℤ} 1/((z+l)^{2k−1}|z+l|^{2s}) = y^{−2s−2k+2} Σ_{r∈ℤ} V_s(ry) e^{2πirx}.
items.note: The general theorem is in Mathlib; the instance is not, because its hypotheses need missing input. `Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_of_rpow_decay` (Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/PoissonSummation.lean:205): `{f : ℝ → ℂ} (hc : Continuous f) {b : ℝ} (hb : 1 < b) (hf : f =O[cocompact ℝ] (|·| ^ (-b))) (hFf : (𝓕 f) =O[cocompact ℝ] (|·| ^ (-b))) (x : ℝ) : ∑' n : ℤ, f (x + n) = ∑' n : ℤ, 𝓕 f n * fourier n (x : UnitAddCircle)`. Apply it to f(u) = (u+iy)^{−(2k−1)}|u+iy|^{−2s}, whose Fourier transform is y^{−2s−2k+2}V_s(ry) (substitute u = yv). The hypothesis on 𝓕f is the decay of V_s(ry) in r, i.e. (3.3b) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/213), which is missing; so the identity is not available as it stands. The holomorphic case s = 0, 2k−1 ≥ 2 is Mathlib's Lipschitz formula `EisensteinSeries.qExpansion_identity` (EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean:174): `∑' n : ℤ, 1 / ((z : ℂ) + n) ^ (k + 1) = ((-2 * π * I) ^ (k + 1) / k !) * ∑' n : ℕ, n ^ k * cexp (2 * π * I * z) ^ n` for 1 ≤ k. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Fourier expansion of E^{(D₁)}_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. Write E^{(D₁)}_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} e^{(D₁)}_s(n, y) e(nx). Then e^{(D₁)}_s(0, y) = L(2s+2k−1, ε) y^s if D₁ = 1, D₂ = D; = V_s(0) L(2s+2k−2, ε) y^{−s−2k+2} if D₁ = D, D₂ = 1; = 0 otherwise. For n ≠ 0, e^{(D₁)}_s(n, y) = ε₁(δ₂)κ(D₂)/δ₂^{2s+2k−3/2} · (Σ_{m|n, m>0} ε₁(m)ε₂(n/m) m^{−(2s+2k−2)}) · y^{−s−2k+2} V_s(ny). Here L(s, ε) = Σ_{n≥1} ε(n)n^{−s}. Valid for Re(s) large, and it gives the meromorphic continuation in s.
items.note: Checked. The m = 0 terms of (2.1) give L(2s+2k−1, ε)y^s only when D₁ = 1 (ε₁(0) = 0 otherwise). Pair ±m, write m ↦ mδ₂ and n = n₀ + δ₂l, apply PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/208 with z replaced by mz + n₀/δ₂, and evaluate Σ_{n₀ mod δ₂} ε₂(n₀)e(rn₀/δ₂) = ε₂(r)κ(D₂)δ₂^{1/2} (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/197). No library counterpart. Mathlib's q-expansions of Eisenstein series (EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean) are level one, even weight and holomorphic. Nearest plan: the node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series (weight-0 Fourier expansion), a different series. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (3.2), n = 0: constant term of ℰ_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. The 0-th Fourier coefficient of ℰ_s(z) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/202) is e_s(0, y) = L(2s+2k−1, ε)(δy)^s + (ε(N)/(i√δ)) V_s(0) L(2s+2k−2, ε) (δy)^{−s−2k+2}.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.2) Proposition (first formula), p. 277; proof pp. 278–279
items.note: Checked from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/209. The D₁ = 1 term gives L(2s+2k−1, ε)(δy)^s. The D₁ = D term gives ε(N)/(κ(D)δ^{s+2k−3/2}) · V_s(0)L(2s+2k−2, ε)y^{−s−2k+2}, with κ(D) = i, which equals (ε(N)/(i√δ))V_s(0)L(2s+2k−2, ε)(δy)^{−s−2k+2}. Dirichlet L-functions are in Mathlib (DirichletCharacter.LFunction), but the Eisenstein coefficients are not. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (3.2), n ≠ 0: non-constant coefficients of ℰ_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For n ≠ 0, the n-th Fourier coefficient of ℰ_s(z) is e_s(n, y) = (ε(N)/(i√δ)) (δy)^{−s−2k+2} V_s(ny) Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_𝒜(n, d) d^{−(2s+2k−2)}, with ε_𝒜(n, d) as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/206.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.2) Proposition (second formula), p. 277; proof p. 279
items.note: Checked. The proof gives e_s(n, y) = iδ^{−s−2k+3/2}(Σ_{D₂|n} ε_{D₁}(−N)χ(𝒜) Σ_{m|n/δ₂} ε_{D₁}(mδ₂)ε_{D₂}(n/mδ₂)(mδ₂)^{−(2s+2k−2)}) y^{−s−2k+2}V_s(ny), using κ(D₂)/κ(D₁) = iε_{D₁}(−1). Put d = mδ₂: the nonzero terms are exactly those with (d, D) = δ₂ and (n/d, δ₂) = 1, i.e. (d, n/d, D) = 1. Matching prefactors needs iε_{D₁}(−N) = (ε(N)/i)ε_{D₂}(−N), which is ε_{D₁}(−1)ε_{D₂}(−1) = ε(−1) = −1. That holds because D < 0. No library or plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (3.3a): the value V_s(0)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1: V_s(0) = (−1)^k π i 2^{−2s−2k+3} Γ(2s+2k−2)/(Γ(s)Γ(s+2k−1)). This holds for Re(s) > 1−k and gives the meromorphic continuation of V_s(0) in s.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition a), p. 277; proofs pp. 279–280
items.note: Two proofs, both checked. (i) Expand (x−i)^{2k−1}, use the Beta integral and the duplication formula, and reduce to the identity Σ_{j=0}^{k−1}(−1/4)^{k−1−j}(2k−1)!/((2j+1)!(k−1−j)!)(s+k−½)…(s+k+j−3/2) = s(s+1)…(s+k−2). The paper leaves that identity to 'a tedious induction'; it was checked here for k = 1, 2, 3. (ii) The Hankel integral for 1/Γ(s) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/218), complete; it contains the misprint PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E35. Numerical spot checks: k = 1, s = 1 gives V_1(0) = −iπ/2; k = 2, s = 1 gives iπ/8; the formula agrees in both. Tools in Mathlib: Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half, Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_eq_betaIntegral (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/220). The formula itself is not in the libraries, since V_s is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/207). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (3.3b): holomorphy of V_s(t) in s and exponential decay in t
items.statement: For t ≠ 0 the function s ↦ V_s(t) continues holomorphically to all s ∈ ℂ and satisfies, locally uniformly in s, V_s(t) = |t|^{O(1)} e^{−2π|t|} as |t| → ∞.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition b), p. 277; proof pp. 280–281
items.note: Proof as printed: first meromorphic continuation, from the u-integral representation of V*_s(t) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/214), which converges for all s. Then holomorphy for t < 0 by deforming the x-path to a contour C around [i, i∞), and similarly for t > 0 around (−i∞, −i]. The estimate comes from the integral representations or the K-Bessel formula (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/217). No library or plan (V_s missing). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (3.3c): V*_s(t) is entire and satisfies V*_s(t) = sign(t) V*_{2−2k−s}(t)
items.statement: For t ≠ 0 set V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1} Γ(s+2k−1) V_s(t). Then V*_s(t) is entire in s and V*_s(t) = sign(t) V*_{2−2k−s}(t). For t > 0 this comes from V*_s(t) = ∫_0^∞ u^{s+k−1} e^{−πt(u+1/u)} ∫_{−∞}^{∞} e^{−πtv²} (v + (u^{1/2}+u^{−1/2})/i)^{2k−1} dv du/u.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition c), p. 278; proof p. 280
items.note: Checked. The integral form comes from Γ(s+2k−1)(πt(x²+1))^{−(s+2k−1)} = ∫_0^∞ u^{s+2k−2}e^{−πt(x²+1)u}du, completing the square, shifting to Im x = −1/u and substituting x = −i/u + v/√u; u ↦ 1/u exchanges s+k−1 ↔ −(s+k−1). For t < 0 the paper says only 'the proof for t < 0 is exactly similar'. Checked here: after shifting to Im x = +1/u the inner factor is (v + i(u^{−1/2} − u^{1/2}))^{2k−1}, which is odd under u ↦ 1/u (with v ↦ −v). This produces the sign −1 = sign(t), consistent with V_{1−k}(t) = 0 for t < 0 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/215). Mathlib has the real-scale Gamma integral `Complex.integral_cpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:372). No library or plan for V*. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (3.3d): V_{−r}(t) for integers 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1
items.statement: Let r ∈ ℤ with 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1. Then V_{−r}(t) = 0 for t < 0 and V_{−r}(t) = 2πi(−1)^{k−r} p_{k,r}(4πt) e^{−2πt} for t > 0, where p_{k,r}(t) = (t/2)^{2k−2−2r} Σ_{j=0}^{r} C(r, j) (−t)^j/(2k−2r−2+j)! (a polynomial). Here V_{−r}(t) = ∫ (x−i)^r (x+i)^{−(2k−1−r)} e^{−2πixt} dx, conditionally convergent for r = k−1.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition d), p. 278; proof p. 281
items.note: Checked by the residue at x = −i: for t < 0 close upward (no pole); for t > 0 close downward. Then V_{−r}(t) = −2πi Res and the binomial expansion of (x−i)^r = ((x+i)−2i)^r gives the printed polynomial. Special case r = 0: V_0(t) = 2πi(−1)^k(2πt)^{2k−2}e^{−2πt}/(2k−2)!. For 2k−1 ≥ 2 this is equivalent to Mathlib's Lipschitz formula `EisensteinSeries.qExpansion_identity` (EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean:174), via PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/208 at s = 0. The general r is not in the libraries. No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (3.3e): ∂_s V_s(t) at the centre s = 1−k for t < 0
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition e), p. 278; proof p. 281
items.note: Checked. Deform the x-path to the contour C circling [i, i∞) counterclockwise and differentiate under the integral sign: ∂_s(x²+1)^{−s} = −log(x²+1)(x²+1)^{−s}, and at s = 1−k the kernel is (x−i)^{k−1}/(x+i)^k (misprinted 's = i−k', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E36). log(x²+1) jumps by 2πi across the cut (right side minus left side), which gives −2πi∫_i^{i∞}. Substituting x = 2ix′ − i gives q_{k−1}(4π|t|)e^{−2πt}. This is the input for the derivative L′_𝒜(f, k) in §4. q_{k−1} is a finite combination of generalised exponential integrals E_j; Mathlib and Tau Ceti have none (searched 'expIntegral', 'incompleteGamma'). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistributions#layer-2-incomplete-special-functions-and-closed-form-cdfs plans incomplete special functions for distributions; it does not plan these. No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: K-Bessel expression for V*_s(t), t > 0
items.statement: For t > 0: V*_s(t) = i Σ_{a,b,c≥0, 2a+b+c=2k−1} (−1)^{k−a}(2k−1)!/((2a)! b! c!) · Γ(a+½)/(πt)^{a+½} · ∫_0^∞ u^{s+k+(b−c)/2−2} e^{−πt(u+1/u)} du = (2(−1)^k i/t^{1/2}) Σ_{a,b,c≥0, 2a+b+c=2k−1} (2k−1)!/(a! b! c!) · (−1/(4πt))^a · K_{s+k−1+(b−c)/2}(2πt). For k = 1: V*_s(t) = (−2i/√t)(K_{1/2+s}(2πt) + K_{1/2−s}(2πt)). The functional equation (3.3c) for t > 0 follows from K_ν = K_{−ν} by interchanging b and c.
items.note: Checked: trinomial expansion; ∫v^{2a}e^{−πtv²}dv = Γ(a+½)(πt)^{−a−½}; (−i)^{2k−1−2a} = i(−1)^{k−a}; Γ(a+½)/(2a)! = √π/(4^a a!); and ∫_0^∞ u^{ν−1}e^{−πt(u+1/u)}du = 2K_ν(2πt). Not used later in this chunk beyond the estimate (3.3b). No K-Bessel functions in Mathlib or Tau Ceti; the atlas plans only other Bessel functions (QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.2 for Rademacher's I-Bessel series). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Hankel's integral formula for 1/Γ(s) (quoted)
items.statement: For Re(s) > 0 and c > 0: 1/Γ(s) = (1/2πi) ∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{w} w^{−s} dw (principal branch of w^{−s}). Equivalently, for u > 0: ∫_{1−i∞}^{1+i∞} z^{−s} e^{uz} dz = 2πi u^{s−1}/Γ(s).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, proof of (3.3a), pp. 279–280 ('uses the Hankel integral formula for 1/Γ(s)')
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for 'Hankel'; the only hits are Hankel matrices. Mathlib has Γ as an integral, its reflection and duplication formulas, and 1/Γ entire (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Beta.lean), but no contour-integral formula for 1/Γ. No atlas stage mentions it. tauceti:Completed/ContourIntegration supplies contour machinery but not this formula. (The paper's use contains the misprint e^{−uz} for e^{uz}, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E35.) Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Integral representation of K_ν and K_ν = K_{−ν} (quoted)
items.statement: For t > 0 and ν ∈ ℂ: ∫_0^∞ u^{ν−1} e^{−πt(u+1/u)} du = 2K_ν(2πt), where K_ν is the modified Bessel function of the second kind; K_ν = K_{−ν}.
items.note: No K-Bessel function in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched 'bessel' and 'besselK'). The paper needs K_ν only to rewrite V*_s (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/217) and for the estimate in (3.3b), which also follows from the u-integral directly (as the paper says). No atlas stage plans K_ν: 'K-Bessel' has 0 hits, and the Bessel mentions are Rademacher I-Bessel (QM.2) and Bessel-potential spaces (PDE). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Legendre duplication formula and the Euler Beta integral (tools for (3.3a))
items.statement: Γ(s)Γ(s+½) = 2^{1−2s}√π Γ(2s); and for Re a, Re b > 0: ∫_0^∞ x^{2a−1}(x²+1)^{−(a+b)} dx = ½ Γ(a)Γ(b)/Γ(a+b), used in the form ∫_0^∞ x^{2k−2j−2}(x²+1)^{−(s+2k−1)} dx = ½ Γ(k−j−½)Γ(s+k+j−½)/Γ(s+2k−1).
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Beta.lean:559: `theorem Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half (s : ℂ) : Gamma s * Gamma (s + 1 / 2) = Gamma (2 * s) * (2 : ℂ) ^ (1 - 2 * s) * ↑(√π)` (namespace Complex); this is the same statement. :124 `Gamma_mul_Gamma_eq_betaIntegral {s t : ℂ} (hs : 0 < re s) (ht : 0 < re t) : Gamma s * Gamma t = Gamma (s + t) * betaIntegral s t`, with `betaIntegral u v = ∫ x in 0..1, x^(u-1)(1-x)^(v-1)` (:60). The (0, ∞) form used by GZ is the substitution x² = y/(1−y), which is not stated separately in Mathlib.

items.name: Corollary (3.4): the Fourier expansion of Φ̃_{−r} for 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For r ∈ ℤ, 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1 (Φ̃ continued in s through its Fourier coefficients): Φ̃_{−r}(z) = Σ_{m=0}^{∞} ( Σ_{0≤n≤mδ/N} e_{n,r}(y) r_𝒜(mδ − nN) ) e^{2πimz}, where e_{n,r}(y) := e_{−r}(n, Ny/δ) e^{2πNny/δ} is given by e_{0,r}(y) = L(2k−2r−1, ε)(Ny)^{−r} if r < k−1, and e_{0,k−1}(y) = [L(1, ε) − ε(N)(π/√δ) L(0, ε)] (Ny)^{1−k}; e_{n,r}(y) = (−1)^{k−r} ε(N) (2π/√δ) (Ny)^{r−2k+2} p_{k,r}(4πNny/δ) Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_𝒜(n, d) d^{2r−2k+2} for n > 0, with p_{k,r} as in (3.3d) and ε_𝒜(n, d) as in (3.2). The coefficients are polynomials in 1/y of degree r.
items.note: Checked from (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3d). The terms with n < 0 vanish because V_{−r}(t) = 0 for t < 0. V_{−r}(0) = 0 for r < k−1 since 1/Γ(−r) = 0 while Γ(2k−2−2r) is finite; V_{1−k}(0) = −πi from the limit Γ(2h)/Γ(1−k+h) → (−1)^{k−1}(k−1)!/2. The factor e^{−2πNny/δ} of V_{−r} cancels against e^{2πNny/δ}. For r = k−1 the bracket equals (1 − ε(N))L(1, ε), by L(1, ε) = πL(0, ε)/√δ; §4 uses this, but it is not stated here. This finite formula at s = 0 (r = 0) and s = 1−k (r = k−1) feeds Propositions (4.4) ff. No library or plan (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/186). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Φ̃_{0,𝒜} is a holomorphic modular form
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. At s = 0, Φ̃_{0,𝒜} ∈ M_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (holomorphic, not in general cuspidal). This is the case r = 0 of (3.4); a priori it holds because ℰ_s(z) is holomorphic in z at s = 0.
items.note: With r = 0, p_{k,0}(T) = (T/2)^{2k−2}/(2k−2)!, so every e_{n,0} is constant in y. The a-priori argument is literal only for k ≥ 2, where the weight-(2k−1) series converges absolutely at s = 0. For k = 1 holomorphy at s = 0 follows from the Fourier expansion: V_0(0) = −πi and the exponent of y is 0. The paper postpones the k = 1 modifications to §6, so this is not recorded as a gap. No library or plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (4.1) Functional equation of the kernel coefficients e*_s(n, y)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let n ∈ ℤ satisfy (4.2): Nn + l ≡ 0 (mod D) for some l = N(𝔞), 𝔞 an integral ideal in A, and y > 0. Put e*_s(n,y) := π^{−s} δ^s Γ(s+2k−1) e_s(n,y). Then e*_s(n,y) = −ε(N) e*_{2−2k−s}(n,y) for all s. Explicitly: e*_s(0,y) = (s+k)(s+k+1)⋯(s+2k−2)[π^{−s}δ^sΓ(s+k)L(2s+2k−1,ε)](δy)^s − ε(N)(2−k−s)(3−k−s)⋯(−s)[π^{1/2−s}δ^{s−1/2}Γ(s+k−1/2)L(2s+2k−2,ε)](δy)^{2−2k−s}, the two brackets being interchanged by s ↦ 2−2k−s by the functional equation of L(s,ε); and for n ≠ 0, e*_s(n,y) = −iε(N)|n|^k π^{2k−1} δ^{−2k+3/2} y V*_s(ny) Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_A(n,d)(|n|/d²)^{s+k−1}, so that (4.1) for n ≠ 0 follows from V*_s(t) = sgn(t)V*_{2−2k−s}(t) (Prop. 3.3c) and (4.3).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, (4.1)–(4.2) and the two displays after (4.2), p. 282
items.note: Checked by hand on the page image: the n = 0 formula follows from Prop. (3.2) and (3.3a) with the duplication formula (2^{−2s−2k+3}Γ(2s+2k−2) = π^{−1/2}Γ(s+k−1)Γ(s+k−1/2)); writing both brackets as (δ/π)^{1/2−k}Λ(σ) with Λ(σ) = (δ/π)^{(σ+1)/2}Γ((σ+1)/2)L(σ,ε), σ = 2s+2k−1 resp. 2s+2k−2, they are swapped by s ↦ 2−2k−s exactly when Λ(σ) = Λ(1−σ) (root number +1, item PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/226). The n ≠ 0 display follows from (3.2) and the definition of V*_s. No library statement: neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has the Rankin kernel Φ̃_s, the Eisenstein combination 𝓔_s, its coefficients e_s(n,y) or V_s(t) (searched: Rankin, Poincaré, nonholomorphic/real-analytic Eisenstein; the only real-analytic Eisenstein series in the atlas is the packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series, a different series). Nearest plan: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 ‘Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives … Prove the functional-equation vanishing that permits differentiation’ — the same method for YZZ's adelic weight-2 kernel, not this classical weight-2k coefficient identity, whose specialisation is not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (4.3) Symmetry of the genus signs: ε_A(n, |n|/d) = −ε(N) sgn(n) ε_A(n, d)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let n ≠ 0 satisfy (4.2): Nn + l ≡ 0 (mod D) for some l = N(𝔞), 𝔞 an integral ideal in A and let d be a positive divisor of n. Then ε_A(n, |n|/d) = −ε(N)·sgn(n)·ε_A(n, d). (Both sides vanish unless (d, n/d, D) = 1. If (d, n/d, D) = 1 write D = D₀D′D″ with D₀, D′, D″ discriminants, |D′| = (d, D), |D″| = (n/d, D), D₀ prime to n; then the product ε_A(n,d)ε_A(n,|n|/d) equals ε_{D₀}(|n|) ε_{D′D″}(−N sgn n) χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A), and (4.2) gives χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A) = ε_{D₀}(l) = ε_{D₀}(−Nn), whence the product is ε_D(−N sgn n) = −ε(N)sgn(n).) In particular, if ε(N) = +1 and n > 0 satisfies (4.2), then Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_A(n,d) = 0.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, (4.3) and its proof, pp. 282–283
items.note: Checked on the page images (p. 283): the three-way splitting and the product formula are correct; ε_D(−N sgn n) = ε(−1)ε(N)ε(sgn n) = −ε(N)sgn(n) since ε is odd. Hypothesis (4.2) is essential (it is what makes χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A) = ε_{D₀}(−Nn)); see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E37. Library: Tau Ceti has genus characters of a fundamental discriminant (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/Basic.lean, genusCharFun, and CoprimeIdeal.lean, genusCharFunCoprimeIdealHom) but no ε_A(n,d) and no statement of this symmetry. No stage plans this computation (searched atlas stage descriptions and packets for ‘genus character’, ‘Rankin’, ‘Gross–Zagier’). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

(3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). items.name: Functional equation of L(s, ε) with root number +1 (quoted input)
items.statement: Let ε = (D/·) with D < 0 a fundamental discriminant, δ = |D|. Then Λ(s, ε) := (δ/π)^{(s+1)/2} Γ((s+1)/2) L(s, ε) extends to an entire function and Λ(1−s, ε) = Λ(s, ε). (Used in §4 to swap the two brackets of e*_s(0,y) under s ↦ 2−2k−s, and in §5 to rewrite the n = 0 term of b_{m,r}: ‘We have used the functional equation of L(s, ε)’, p. 290.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, p. 282 (‘by the functional equation of L(s, ε)’) and §5, p. 290 (after (5.4))
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:284: theorem DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (s : ℂ) : completedLFunction χ (1 − s) = N ^ (s − 1/2) * rootNumber χ * completedLFunction χ⁻¹ s, with rootNumber χ = gaussSum χ stdAddChar / I^(0 or 1) / N^(1/2) (line 272). For ε real, χ⁻¹ = χ, so this is the needed equation up to the root number; the evaluation rootNumber ε = 1 (Gauss's sign τ(ε) = i√δ) is in neither library (Mathlib only has rootNumber_modOne; Tau Ceti's Multiquadratic/Cyclotomic/GaussSum.lean only proves τ² = p*) and no stage or packet plans it (searched ‘Gauss sum sign’, ‘quadratic Gauss sum’, ‘rootNumber’). Hence status missing although the general functional equation is in Mathlib. GZ's use needs the sign exactly: with root number −1 the two brackets in e*_s(0,y) would not be interchanged. Routed (source) to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1.

items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). For an integer n ≠ 0: σ_A(n) := Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_A(n,d). For n > 0: σ′_A(n) := Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_A(n,d) log(n/d²). p_{k−1}(t) := Σ_{j=0}^{k−1} C(k−1, j)(−t)^j/j! (= p_{k,k−1}(t) of Prop. (3.3d)). items.note: No library or planned object: ε_A(n,d) itself is not defined anywhere (Tau Ceti has the genus characters genusCharFun but not these twisted divisor sums). The sign-dependence remark is mine and is the source of issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38. p_{k−1} is elementary (a Laguerre-type polynomial, p_{k−1}(t) = L_{k−1}(t) the Laguerre polynomial); not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched ‘Laguerre’: no hits in either tree). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

(3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Suppose ε(N) = −1. Then L_A(f,k) = 2^{2k+1} π^{k+1} / ((k−1)! √δ) · (f, Φ̃), where Φ̃ ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) has the Fourier expansion Φ̃(z) = Σ_{m=0}^∞ ( Σ_{0<n≤mδ/N} σ_A(n) r_A(mδ − Nn) p_{k−1}(4πNny/δ) + (h/u) r_A(m) ) y^{1−k} e^{2πimz}. (3.4) with r = k−1.)
items.note: Re-derived: Cor. (3.4) with r = k−1 gives e_{n,k−1}(y) = (2π/√δ)(Ny)^{1−k}p_{k−1}(4πNny/δ)σ_A(n) for n > 0 when ε(N) = −1, and e_{0,k−1}(y) = [L(1,ε)+(π/√δ)L(0,ε)](Ny)^{1−k} = (2πh/(u√δ))(Ny)^{1−k} by the class number formula (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/229); the n = 0 term carries r_A(mδ) = r_A(m) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/230). Then (4π)^{−k}N^{1−k}(k−1)!L_A(f,k) = (f, Φ̃_{1−k}) gives the constant. items.name: Analytic class number formula for K: L(1, ε) = πh/(u√δ), L(0, ε) = h/u (implicit input)
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D < 0 (δ = |D|, h = h_K, w = 2u = #O_K^×) and ε = (D/·): L(1, ε) = 2πh/(w√δ) = πh/(u√δ), and (by the functional equation PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/226) L(0, ε) = 2h/w = h/u. Used implicitly: the n = 0 coefficient L(1,ε) − ε(N)(π/√δ)L(0,ε) of e_{0,k−1} becomes (2πh/(u√δ)) when ε(N) = −1, giving the term (h/u)r_A(m) of Prop. (4.4); and in Prop. (4.5) the m-th coefficient of the n = 0 term, (N^{k−1}√δ/2π)·2L(1,ε)(Ny)^{1−k}[…]·r_A(mδ), becomes (h/u)r_A(m)y^{1−k}[…]; the same factor h/u then appears in Theorems (5.6) and (5.8).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, Propositions (4.4) and (4.5), pp. 283–284 (used without comment)
items.note: Not stated on these pages but required to pass from Cor. (3.4) and the derivative of e_s(0,y) to the printed (h/u)r_A(m) terms; I verified the resulting constants numerically (L(1,χ₋₇) = 1.18741… = π/√7). Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:77 has the residue of ζ_K at s = 1 (tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT, residue 2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂}Reg·h/(w√|d_K|)), but not the factorisation ζ_K = ζ·L(s, ε_D) needed to get L(1, ε); no Tau Ceti statement (grep for files combining classNumber with LFunction/LSeries: only DedekindZeta.lean). DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 plans generalized Bernoulli numbers and ‘Compare the algebraic values with the complex analytic L-functions’ (so L(0,ε) = −B_{1,ε}) but not B_{1,ε} = −2h/w or L(1,ε) = πh/(u√δ); status missing. Routed (source) to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4.

items.name: r_A(mδ) = r_A(m) (implicit step)
items.statement: With the standing notation (D odd, so D squarefree), for every m ≥ 0 and every class A: r_A(m|D|) = r_A(m). (The different 𝔡 = (√D) is principal and every integral ideal of norm m|D| is divisible by every ramified prime, hence equals 𝔡·𝔟 with N(𝔟) = m; for m = 0 both sides are 1/w.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, used in (4.4) and (4.5) (the n = 0 term of Cor. (3.4), r_A(mδ − 0·N), is printed as r_A(m)), pp. 283–284; Theorems (5.6), (5.8) use both forms
items.note: Implicit identification, needed to match Cor. (3.4) (whose n = 0 term has r_A(mδ)) with the (h/u)r_A(m) of Props. (4.4)/(4.5). Checked: for squarefree odd D every ideal of norm divisible by p | D is divisible by the unique prime above p, and 𝔡 = (√D). Theorem (5.6) keeps r_A(m|D|) while (5.8) uses r_A(m); consistent by this identity. No library statement (Tau Ceti has ideal-count bounds in NumberTheory/EffectiveBounds/IdealCount but no class-restricted ideal counts r_A); not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

(3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Genus notation (p. 284–285): {𝔫} is the genus of any integral ideal 𝔫 of K with N(𝔫) ≡ ε(N)N (mod D) (independent of the choice); {A𝔫} its product with the genus of A; R_{A𝔫}(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in the genus {A𝔫} (for n = 0 the sum of r_B(0) over the classes B of that genus); δ(n) = 2^s, s = number of prime factors of (n, D) (δ(0) = 2^t, t = number of prime factors of D). For a prime p with ε(p) ≠ 1, {𝔠} denotes the genus of any integral ideal 𝔠 with N(𝔠) ≡ −p (mod D): for ε(p) = −1 this is the genus attached to −p ∈ {x ∈ (ℤ/Dℤ)^× : ε(x) = 1}; for ε(p) = 0 it is the genus whose genus characters at the primes p′ | D, p′ ≠ p, are (−p/p′) (the character at p being fixed by the product formula); explicitly 𝔠 = 𝔮 with N(𝔮) ≡ −p (mod D) if ε(p) = −1, and 𝔠 = 𝔮𝔭 with 𝔭² = (p) and N(𝔮) ≡ −1 (mod D/p) if ε(p) = 0.

items.name: Genus theory: {genera of K} ↔ {x ∈ (ℤ/Dℤ)^× : ε(x) = 1}/(ℤ/Dℤ)^{×2}; each genus has h/2^{t−1} classes (quoted input)
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic with odd fundamental discriminant D having t prime factors. The map sending an ideal class to the residue mod D of the norm of any integral ideal in it prime to D (modulo squares) induces a bijection {genera of K} = Cl_K/Cl_K² ≅ {x ∈ (ℤ/Dℤ)^× : ε(x) = 1}/(ℤ/Dℤ)^{×2}; equivalently the t genus characters χ_p (p | D) separate genera and take exactly the sign vectors of product 1. Hence there are 2^{t−1} genera, each containing h/2^{t−1} ideal classes.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, Remark 1 after (4.6), p. 285 (‘the usual correspondence’); §5, p. 291 (‘each genus contains h/2^{t−1} ideal classes’)
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/PrincipalGenus.lean:79 (a sign vector v indexed by the prime discriminants s of D is in the range of the genus-character family on Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)² iff Σ v = 0, i.e. product of signs 1), :112 (the family is injective on Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²), :150 (principal genus theorem: a narrow class is a square iff all genus characters are 1); hypotheses: K = ℚ(θ), minpoly θ = X² − d, d squarefree, ∏_{P∈s} P = fundamentalDiscriminant d. This is the same statement in sign-vector form (via CRT, (ℤ/Dℤ)^×/squares ≅ {±1}^t by Legendre symbols, ε(x) = 1 being the product-one condition) and for Cl⁺(K), which equals Cl_K for imaginary K; the (ℤ/Dℤ)^× phrasing and the count h/2^{t−1} are immediate corollaries not stated as such.

items.name: Proposition (5.1): holomorphic projection lemma (Sturm, GZ's version)
items.statement: Let k ≥ 2 (weight 2k > 2) and N ≥ 1. Let Φ̃ ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) (p. 270: a function Φ̃ : 𝔥 → ℂ, not necessarily holomorphic, with Φ̃|_{2k}γ = Φ̃ for all γ ∈ Γ₀(N) and (Φ̃|_{2k}γ)(z) = O(y^C) as y → ∞ for all γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ) and some C > 0) with Fourier expansion Φ̃(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} a_m(y) e^{2πimz}, and suppose (Φ̃|_{2k}α)(z) = O(y^{−ε}) as y = Im z → ∞, for some ε > 0 and every α ∈ SL₂(ℤ). For m > 0 put a_m := (4πm)^{2k−1}/(2k−2)! · ∫_0^∞ a_m(y) e^{−4πmy} y^{2k−2} dy. Then Φ(z) := Σ_{m≥1} a_m e^{2πimz} is a holomorphic cusp form of weight 2k and level N, and (f, Φ) = (f, Φ̃) for all f ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)). (Proof: unfold (Φ̃, P_m) against the Poincaré series P_m (item on P_m), using P*_m(z) = O(y^{1−2k}) uniformly under SL₂(ℤ); represent f ↦ (Φ̃, f) by some Φ ∈ S_2k (Riesz) and compare (Φ, P_m) = (2k−2)!(4πm)^{1−2k}b_m.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, (5.1) Proposition and proof, pp. 288–289; source: Sturm [33] (‘since our hypotheses are slightly different from Sturm's, prove’)
items.note: Proof checked (one misprint in the unfolding display, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E41; the first estimate uses |e^{2πiz}| where the c = 0 term is |e^{2πimz}| ≤ |e^{2πiz}|, which is correct as an inequality). Library: no holomorphic projection and no Poincaré series in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched ‘holomorphic proj’, ‘Poincaré series’, ‘Sturm’ — the Sturm hits are the Sturm bound, TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/SturmBound.lean, a different theorem). The Petersson product of cusp forms exists (tauceti:CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets, Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:94; the pairing of a cusp form with an arbitrary function over a set D is tauceti:UpperHalfPlane.peterssonInner, Petersson/Basic.lean:107; both conjugate-linear in the FIRST argument, opposite to GZ). Planned: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 ‘Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms, holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection’. Caveat: GZ.6's holomorphic projection is for YZZ's (parallel) weight-2 adelic kernel, where it needs regularisation (as in GZ §6 for k = 1); the classical weight-2k > 2 lemma here is the unregularised special case and is not a separate node. The Poincaré-series input is planned separately (QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series).

items.name: Holomorphic Poincaré series P_m and the unfolding identity
items.statement: For k ≥ 2, N ≥ 1, m ≥ 1: P_m(z) := Σ_{γ∈Γ_∞\Γ₀(N)} (e^{2πimz})|_{2k}γ = Σ_{(a b; c d)∈Γ_∞\Γ₀(N)} (cz+d)^{−2k} e^{2πim(az+b)/(cz+d)}, Γ_∞ = {±(1 n; 0 1)}. The series converges absolutely (k > 1) and P_m ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)). Its majorant P*_m (absolute values of the terms) satisfies P*_m(z) ≤ e^{−2πy} + y^{−k}(E(z,k) − y^k) = O(y^{1−2k}) as y → ∞, and the same bound holds for P*_m|_{2k}α, α ∈ SL₂(ℤ). Unfolding: for Φ̃ as in (5.1), (Φ̃, P_m) = ∫_0^∞ e^{−4πmy} a_m(y) y^{2k−2} dy; in particular for Φ = Σ b_n q^n ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)), (Φ, P_m) = (2k−2)!/(4πm)^{2k−1} · b_m.
items.note: Checked (the Γ₀(N)-invariance of P*_m(z)|Φ̃(z)|y^{2k} and its O(y^{1−ε}) bound justify the interchange). Packet node QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series: ‘For N ≥ 1, an even integer k ≥ 4 and m ∈ ℤ: P(m, k, N; τ) := Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (e(mτ)|_kA)(τ) … The series converges absolutely and locally uniformly for k ≥ 3 when m ≥ 0’ — the same series with their k = GZ's 2k ≥ 4; stage QM.3 ‘construct Poincare series and pairing/exact-sequence interfaces’. The unfolding identity (Petersson coefficient formula) is covered only by that stage sentence, not by a node, and the majorant estimate is not planned explicitly. No library object (no Poincaré series in Mathlib or Tau Ceti).

items.name: Growth of the SL₂(ℤ) Eisenstein series: E(z,s) = y^s + O(y^{1−s}) (quoted input)
items.statement: For real s > 1 let E(z,s) = Σ_{γ∈Γ_∞\SL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s = Σ_{(c,d)=1, mod ±} y^s/|cz+d|^{2s}. Then E(z,s) = y^s + O(y^{1−s}) as y → ∞ (uniformly in x).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, proof of (5.1), p. 289 (‘since for any s > 1 the Eisenstein series E(z,s) for SL₂(ℤ) satisfies E(z,s) = y^s + O(y^{1−s})’)
items.note: Used with s = k to bound the Poincaré majorant. No non-holomorphic Eisenstein series in Mathlib (NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/* are the holomorphic ones; Summable.lean gives summability of Σ|cz+d|^{−k}, not the asymptotic) or Tau Ceti (grep ‘nonholomorphic’, ‘real-analytic Eisenstein’: none). Planned in general form by AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.1 ‘Prove absolute convergence of the Eisenstein sum over P(F)\G(F) in a specified positive chamber, locally uniform convergence with differentiated growth estimates and automorphy. Derive its constant term’ (for GL₂/ℚ the constant term y^s + φ(s)y^{1−s} plus exponential decay of the rest gives the estimate); the classical level-one specialisation is not a separate node. A different real-analytic Eisenstein series (level N, congruence classes) is the packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series.

items.name: Riesz representation on S_2k(Γ₀(N)) (quoted input)
items.statement: S_2k(Γ₀(N)) with the Petersson product is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space; hence every antilinear functional f ↦ (Φ̃, f) on it is of the form f ↦ (Φ, f) for a unique Φ ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, proof of (5.1), p. 289 (‘the map f ↦ (Φ̃, f) is an antilinear map … so is represented by (Φ, ·) for some holomorphic cusp form Φ’)
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Dual.lean:137: InnerProductSpace.toDual : E ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 E for a complete inner product space (Fréchet–Riesz). Tau Ceti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:296: CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosetsCore : InnerProductSpace.Core ℂ (CuspForm (Γ.map (mapGL ℝ)) k) for finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) (positive definite, Hermitian). Caveat: Tau Ceti deliberately does not derive the InnerProductSpace instance from the core (docstring at :285–296), so the composite statement for cusp forms is one instance-construction away; completeness follows from finite-dimensionality (used in Petersson/Orthogonal.lean, isCompl_peterssonOrthogonal :201). Tau Ceti's pairing is conjugate-linear in the first argument, GZ's in the second.

items.name: Holomorphic projection of forms with polynomial-in-1/y coefficients (special case of (5.1))
items.statement: Let k ≥ 2 and Φ̃ ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) be small at the cusps ((Φ̃|α)(x+iy) = O(y^{−ε}) for all α ∈ SL₂(ℤ)), with Fourier coefficients that are polynomials of degree ≤ 2k−2 in 1/y. Then the holomorphic form obtained from Φ̃ by dropping the terms y^{−j} (the constant term) and replacing each term y^{−j}e^{2πimz} (m > 0, 0 ≤ j ≤ 2k−2) by ((2k−2−j)!/(2k−2)!)(4πm)^j e^{2πimz} has the same Petersson product as Φ̃ with every f ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, paragraph after the proof of (5.1), p. 289
items.note: Checked: (4πm)^{2k−1}/(2k−2)!·∫_0^∞ y^{−j}e^{−4πmy}y^{2k−2}dy = (2k−2−j)!(4πm)^j/(2k−2)!. Gamma integral in Mathlib: Real.integral_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:465). Plan as for (5.1) (GZ.6 ‘holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection’, adelic weight 2); this explicit classical rule is not a node.

items.name: Holomorphic projection of Φ̃_{−r} (0 ≤ r ≤ k−1) and the relation a_{m,r} = C_r b_{m,r}
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1. Φ̃_{−r} (Cor. (3.4)) is holomorphic for r = 0; for r ≥ 1 (so k > 1) it is small at all cusps (at ∞ its constant term is a multiple of y^{−r} and the other terms are O(e^{−2πy}); at the other cusps by the trace-of-theta-times-Eisenstein description), so its holomorphic projection is Φ_{−r} = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,r}q^m with a_{m,r} = (4πm)^{2k−1}/(2k−2)! · Σ_{n=0}^{[mδ/N]} r_A(mδ − nN) ∫_0^∞ e_{n,r}(y)e^{−4πmy}y^{2k−2}dy = (−1)^{k−r} 2^{2k−1} ε(N) r! π^{2k−1−r} / ((2k−2)! N^r |D|^{2k−r−3/2}) · b_{m,r}, with b_{m,r} as in (5.2)–(5.4) (for r ≤ k−2; for r = k−1 the n = 0 term of b_{m,r} is doubled).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, pp. 289–290 (paragraph before (5.2) and the display defining a_{m,r})
items.note: The a_{m,r} ↔ b_{m,r} constant re-derived: for n > 0 the integral gives r!·(4π/δ)^r·P_{k,r}(Nn, mδ)·(2π/δ)^{2k−2−2r}(2π/√δ)N^{−r}σ_{2k−2r−2,A}(n)/(2k−2)!; for n = 0 the functional equation of L(s,ε) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/226) turns (4πm)^r(2k−2−r)!N^{−r}L(2k−2r−1,ε)/(2k−2)! into the same constant times P_{k,r}(0,mδ)σ_{2k−2r−2,A}(0). Numerically: for N = 1, k = 6, D = −7 and r = 1,…,4, Σ_m b_{m,r}q^m is exactly b_{1,r}·Δ (ratios −24, 252, −1472), and for r = 0 it is a modular form with the expected Eisenstein part. Nothing planned for this classical computation. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (5.2)–(5.4): b_{m,r}, P_{k,r}(x,y) and σ_{2l,A}(n)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). For 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1, m ≥ 0: b_{m,r} := Σ_{0≤n≤m|D|/N} r_A(m|D| − nN)·P_{k,r}(Nn, m|D|)·σ_{2k−2r−2,A}(n) (5.2), where P_{k,r}(x, y) := Σ_{j=0}^{r} C(r, j)·C(2k−2+j−r, r)·(−x)^j y^{r−j} (5.3) and, for l ≥ 0, σ_{2l,A}(0) := −½ ε(N) L(−2l, ε), σ_{2l,A}(n) := Σ_{d|n} ε_A(n,d)(n/d)^{2l} for n > 0 (5.4).
items.note: Checked on the zoomed page image. Note σ_{0,A}(n) = σ_A(n) for n > 0. P_{k,r} is a homogenised Jacobi polynomial (item PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/248). L(−2l, ε) = −B_{2l+1,ε}/(2l+1) is planned by DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 (‘Construct generalized Bernoulli numbers … Compare the algebraic values with the complex analytic L-functions’), but b_{m,r} itself is not defined or planned anywhere. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Theorem (5.5): L_A(f, 2k−1−r) for 0 ≤ r < k−1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let 0 ≤ r < k−1 and define b_{m,r} (m ≥ 0) by (5.2)–(5.4). Then Σ_{m≥0} b_{m,r}q^m is a modular form of weight 2k and level N (a cusp form if r ≠ 0), and L_A(f, 2k−1−r) = (−1)^{k−r}(2π)^{2(2k−1−r)}/(2k−2−r)! · 2^{2k−1}/(2k−2)! · ε(N) r!/|D|^{2k−r−3/2} · (f, Σ_m b_{m,r}q^m) for every f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2k and level N. CORRECTED: the paper prints (2k−2−2r)! in the first denominator; the correct factor is (2k−2−r)! = Γ(2k−1−r) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E42). The two agree only for r = 0.
items.note: Derivation: Prop. (1.2) at s = −r gives (4π)^{r−2k+1}N^{−r}Γ(2k−1−r)L_A(f,2k−1−r) = (f, Φ_{−r}), and a_{m,r} = C_r b_{m,r} with C_r as in the preceding item; hence the stated constant with Γ(2k−1−r) = (2k−2−r)!. Numerical confirmation (N = 1, f = Δ, k = 6, D = −7, h = 1, so L_A(Δ,s) = L(Δ,s)L(Δ⊗χ₋₇,s), computed by the approximate functional equation and cross-checked against the Dirichlet series at s = 11): with (2k−2−r)! the implied Petersson norm (Δ,Δ) is 1.03536205680432·10⁻⁶ for r = 0,1,2,3,4 (the known value), while the printed (2k−2−2r)! gives 1.15·10⁻⁷, 1.85·10⁻⁸, 4.93·10⁻⁹, 2.88·10⁻⁹ for r = 1,…,4. Also checked at N = 3, k = 3, D = −7, f = (η(z)η(3z))⁶, r = 1: consistent with Theorem (5.6) (corrected) at the same f. No library object; not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Rationality and near-integrality of b_{m,r} (remark after (5.5))
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). The b_{m,r} of (5.2) are rational; every summand of (5.2) other than the end terms n = 0 and n = m|D|/N is an integer; r_A(0) = 1/(2u) = ½ for D < −4, and σ_{2l,A}(0) = −½ε(N)L(−2l,ε) ∈ ℤ for D < −4l−3 (l ≥ 1).
items.note: Checked the integrality claim σ_{2l,A}(0) ∈ ℤ, i.e. ½L(−2l,ε) = −B_{2l+1,ε}/(2(2l+1)) ∈ ℤ, for all odd fundamental D with −399 ≤ D ≤ −3 and l = 1,…,5: the only failures are at D ≥ −4l−3 (l = 1: D = −3, −7; l = 2: −3, −11; l = 3: −3; l = 4: −3, −7, −19; l = 5: −3, −23), so the bound is correct and sharp in this range (for l = 0, i.e. r = k−1, it fails, but that case is excluded from (5.5)). Generalized Bernoulli numbers are planned (DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0) but not this integrality statement. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: P_{k,k−1} is a Legendre polynomial and P_{k,r} a Jacobi polynomial
items.statement: For the polynomials of (5.3): P_{k,k−1}(x, y) = y^{k−1} P_{k−1}(1 − 2x/y), with P_{k−1} the (k−1)st Legendre polynomial; and in general P_{k,r}(x, y) = y^r P_r^{(2k−2−2r, 0)}(1 − 2x/y), with P_n^{(α,β)} the Jacobi polynomials.
items.note: Checked: P_{k,k−1}(x,y) = Σ_j C(k−1,j)C(k−1+j,j)(−x)^j y^{k−1−j}, and P_n(z) = Σ_j C(n,j)C(n+j,j)((z−1)/2)^j; the Jacobi case from P_n^{(α,0)}(z) = Σ_m C(n,m)C(n+α+m, n)((z−1)/2)^m with α = 2k−2−2r. Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/ShiftedLegendre.lean:37: Polynomial.shiftedLegendre n = Σ_{k≤n} (−1)^k C(n,k)C(n+k,n) X^k ∈ ℤ[X], which is exactly x ↦ P_n(1 − 2x); so the Legendre half is the homogenisation of a library polynomial (y^{k−1}·shiftedLegendre(k−1)(x/y)), but the identity itself is not stated. Jacobi polynomials are in neither library (grep ‘Jacobi polynomial’, ‘gegenbauer’: none) and not planned; status missing for the item as a whole. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Legendre polynomials P_n (quoted standard object)
items.statement: P_n(z) = 2^{−n} Σ_{0≤j≤n/2} (−1)^j C(n, j) C(2n−2j, n) z^{n−2j}; equivalently P_n(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{n} C(n,j)C(n+j,j)((z−1)/2)^j, so that P_n(1 − 2x) = Σ_j (−1)^j C(n,j)C(n+j,j) x^j.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, p. 291 and Theorem (5.8), p. 294 (explicit formula for P_{k−1})
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/ShiftedLegendre.lean:37: noncomputable def Polynomial.shiftedLegendre (n : ℕ) : ℤ[X] := Σ_{k∈range(n+1)} C((−1)^k·n.choose k·(n+k).choose n)·X^k, with Rodrigues' formula factorial_mul_shiftedLegendre_eq (:43). This is the same polynomial after the affine change z = 1 − 2x (the only form in which GZ evaluate it: P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|))); the z-variable expansion printed in (5.8) is not in Mathlib. Checked that the (5.8) formula is the standard one.

items.name: Jacobi polynomials P_n^{(α,β)} (quoted standard object)
items.statement: P_n^{(α,β)}(z) = Γ(α+n+1)/(n!Γ(α+β+n+1)) Σ_{m=0}^{n} C(n,m) Γ(α+β+n+m+1)/Γ(α+m+1) ((z−1)/2)^m; used only for the remark P_{k,r}(x,y) = y^r P_r^{(2k−2−2r,0)}(1−2x/y).
items.note: Only a remark (‘these are much less familiar functions’); nothing depends on it. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti; not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Theorem (5.6): the central value L_A(f,k) when ε(N) = −1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Suppose ε(N) = −1 and k ≥ 1. For m ≥ 0 define b_{m,A} = (m|D|)^{k−1}[ r_A(m|D|)·h/u + Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} δ(n) R_{A𝔫}(n) r_A(m|D| − nN) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)) ], with δ(n), R_{A𝔫}(n) as in (4.6) and P_{k−1} the Legendre polynomial. Then Σ_{m≥0} b_{m,A}q^m is a modular form of weight 2k and level N (a cusp form if k ≠ 1), and L_A(f,k) = (2π)^{2k} 2^{2k−1}/((2k−2)! |D|^{k−1/2}) · (f, Σ_m b_{m,A}q^m) for every f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2k and level N. CORRECTED: the paper prints the constant (2π)^{2k}2^{2k−1}(k−1)!/((2k−2)!|D|^{k−1/2}); the factor (k−1)! must be deleted (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E43). The two agree for k = 1, 2.
items.note: Derivation from Prop. (4.4): holomorphic projection of y^{1−k}·p_{k−1}(4πNny/δ) gives (4πm)^{k−1}(k−1)!/(2k−2)!·P_{k−1}(1−2nN/(mδ)) (and (h/u)r_A(m) gives (4πm)^{k−1}(k−1)!/(2k−2)!·(h/u)r_A(m)), so a_m = (4π)^{k−1}(k−1)!/((2k−2)!δ^{k−1})·b_{m,A} (using σ_A(n) = δ(n)R_{A𝔫}(n) from (4.6a) and r_A(mδ) = r_A(m)); multiplying by the constant 2^{2k+1}π^{k+1}/((k−1)!√δ) of (4.4), the (k−1)! cancels: L_A(f,k) = 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!δ^{k−1/2})·(f, Σ b_{m,A}q^m). This is exactly parallel to the printed constant of Theorem (5.8), which does not carry (k−1)!. Numerically: N = 3, k = 3, D = −7, f = (η(z)η(3z))⁶: Σ b_{m,A}q^m = 6·f (checked to q⁵), and L_A(f,3) = L(f,3)L(f⊗χ₋₇,3) = 0.2183120582… gives (f,f) = 5.74981176452619·10⁻⁵ with the corrected constant — the same value as from Theorem (5.5) at r = 1 (corrected) — and half of it with the printed one. For k = 1 the formula is the analytic side of Gross's definite-quaternion formula (Ch. V §3); GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 plans the Waldspurger formula with ‘definite-quaternionic specializations’, but not this Fourier-coefficient statement, so status missing. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Simplified form of b_{m,A} (remark after (5.6))

(3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). items.name: Example: N = 5, k = 2, D = −p (sum over classes) and the table of b₁
items.statement: Let p ≡ 3 (mod 4) be prime with (5/p) = −1, D = −p, N = 5, k = 2, ε = (·/p), and f = q − 4q² + 2q³ + 8q⁴ − ⋯ the unique normalised newform spanning S₄(Γ₀(5)). Summing Theorem (5.6) over all classes A (Σ_A L_A(f,s) = L(f,s)L_ε(f,s), P₁(x) = x): p^{3/2}/(64π⁴) · L(f,2)L_ε(f,2)/(f,f) = Σ_A b_{1,A} = p·h(−p) + Σ_{1≤n<p/5} (p − 10n) R(n) R(p − 5n), with R(n) = Σ_{d|n}(d/p) and h(−p) replaced by 1/3 for p = 3. The values for p = 3, 7, 23, 43, 47, 67, 83, 103, 107, 127, 163, 167, 223, 227, 263, 283 are 1, 1, 1, 49, 25, 121, 361, 25, 289, 25, 169, 81, 121, 2025, 1, 121 — all squares, in accordance with Waldspurger's theorem.
items.note: Recomputed the right-hand side exactly (class numbers from reduced forms): all 16 printed values are correct and the printed list of p is complete up to 283; the next values are 4489 (p = 307), 225 (347), 1 (367), 441 (383), all squares. Checked the eigenform (η(z)η(5z))⁴ = q − 4q² + 2q³ + 8q⁴ − 5q⁵ − ⋯. The constant 64π⁴/p^{3/2} agrees with both the printed and the corrected constant of (5.6) because (k−1)! = 1 for k = 2. The step Σ_A L_A = L(f,s)L_ε(f,s) is (0.3)/(0.4) (chunk covering pp. 267–269). Not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Waldspurger's theorem (quoted, for the squareness of the example values)
items.statement: (As invoked:) the central values L(f,k)L(f⊗ε,k), suitably normalised, are squares — more precisely, Waldspurger's theorem expresses L(f,k)L(f⊗ε_D,k) (or the product of the central values of a form and its twist) as the square of a toric period / Fourier coefficient of a half-integral-weight form, times explicit factors, so the rational numbers Σ_A b_{1,A} of the example are squares.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, p. 292 (‘in accordance with Waldspurger's theorem, they are all squares’)
items.note: Quoted without statement or reference number on this page; nothing in the proof depends on it. Planned: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 ‘Establish the Waldspurger period formula for the stated GL₂/quaternionic toric data. Give the actual pairing identity including adjoint L-value, zeta/eta factors and normalized local toric forms … Export the explicit split, ramified and definite-quaternionic specializations’. The squareness of the specific example (definite quaternion algebra ramified at 5 and ∞, weight 4) is a specialisation that GZ.5 exports only in general terms. No library statement.

If ε(N) = −1 (so N(𝔫) ≡ −N mod D) and l = m|D| − nN > 0, the genus conditions at the primes p | D with p ∤ n are automatic (l ≡ N(𝔫)n mod p), and δ(n) Σ_A R_{A𝔫}(n) r_A(m|D| − nN) = R(n) R(m|D| − nN) ∏_{p|(n,D)} (1 + ε̂_p((nN − m|D|)/(nN))), where ε̂_p : ℚ^× → {±1} is the homomorphism with ε̂_p(q) = (q/p) for primes q ≠ p, ε̂_p(−1) = (−1/p), and ε̂_p(p) = ((|D|/p)/p).
