items.name: Growth of Φ̃ of Prop. (4.5) at the cusps (k > 1)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Suppose ε(N) = +1 and k > 1, and let Φ̃ be as in Prop. (4.5) with coefficients a_m(y) (of e^{2πimz}). Using p_{k−1}(t) = O(t^{k−1}), q_{k−1}(t) = O(t^{k−1}e^{−t}) (t → ∞), σ′_A(n), r_A(n) = O(n^ε): a_m(y) = O(m^{k+ε}) (m > 0), O(y^{1−k} log y) (m = 0), O(|m|^{k+ε}e^{−4π|m|y}) (m < 0), uniformly for y ≥ 1; hence Φ̃(z) = O(y^{1−k} log y), and the same holds at every cusp (by the theta × Eisenstein description). So Φ̃ satisfies the hypotheses of Prop. (5.1).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, p. 292 (last paragraph) – p. 293 (first line)
items.note: Checked at ∞ (for m < 0 only n ≥ |m|δ/N contribute and q_{k−1}(4πnNy/δ) ≤ e^{−4π|m|y}·(…)); the estimate q_{k−1}(t) = O(t^{k−1}e^{−t}) is meant for t → ∞ (as t → 0, q_{k−1}(t) grows like log(1/t)), which is the regime used since n ≥ 1 and y → ∞. The other cusps are asserted, not computed (‘as we can see by going back to the definition’). No library/plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The four integrals in the holomorphic projection of Prop. (4.5)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1, m, n, N, δ > 0 and z = 1 + 2nN/(mδ): (i) ∫_0^∞ p_{k−1}(4πnNy/δ) y^{k−1}e^{−4πmy} dy = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k · P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(mδ)); (ii) ∫_0^∞ y^{k−1} log y · e^{−4πmy} dy = ∂/∂s(Γ(s)/(4πm)^s)|_{s=k} = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k (Γ′/Γ(k) − log 4πm); (iii) ∫_0^∞ y^{k−1}e^{−4πmy}dy = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k; (iv) ∫_0^∞ q_{k−1}(4πnNy/δ) y^{k−1}e^{−4πmy} dy = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}dx/(x^k(1 + nNx/(mδ))^k) = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k · 2Q_{k−1}(z), the last step by the substitution x = 1 + √((z+1)/(z−1))·e^t, which gives ∫_{−∞}^{∞} dt/(z + √(z²−1) cosh t)^k [printed substitution x = 1 + √((z−1)/(z+1))e^t; issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E45].
items.note: All four checked by hand; (i) is the same computation as in (5.6). Library: only (iii) is in Mathlib (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:465, Real.integral_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi {a r : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hr : 0 < r) : ∫ t in Ioi 0, t^(a−1)·exp(−(r·t)) = (1/r)^a·Gamma a); (ii) needs differentiation under the integral; (i), (iv) and Legendre functions of the second kind are absent. Not planned. Status missing for the item as a whole. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (5.7) Legendre function of the second kind Q_{k−1} and its integral representation (quoted)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1, Q_{k−1} is the function on z > 1 characterised by Q_{k−1}(z) = ½P_{k−1}(z) log((z+1)/(z−1)) + (polynomial in z) and Q_{k−1}(z) = O(z^{−k}) as z → ∞ (5.7); Q₀(z) = ½log((z+1)/(z−1)), Q₁(z) = ½z log((z+1)/(z−1)) − 1. It has the integral representation 2Q_{k−1}(z) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞} dt/(z + √(z²−1) cosh t)^k (Heine).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, (5.7) and the preceding sentence, p. 294 (‘Legendre function of the second kind as in Chap. II’)
items.note: Checked the characterisation, the two first values and the integral representation (numerically as well, e.g. Q₀(3) = ½log 2 and Q₁(3) = (3/2)log 2 − 1 against the hypergeometric formula). Also used in Chapter II (Green's function G_{N,s} with Q_{s−1}). Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has Legendre functions of the second kind (grep ‘second kind’, ‘legendreQ’: only Chebyshev/Stirling hits); no stage or packet plans them (the Legendre hits in packets are the Legendre elliptic curve and the Legendre symbol). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Theorem (5.8): the central derivative L′_A(f,k) for k > 1, ε(N) = +1
items.statement: Suppose k > 1, N ≥ 1, and A an ideal class of the imaginary quadratic field K of (odd) discriminant D with ε(N) = +1 (ε = (D/·)). For m > 0 put a_{m,A} = m^{k−1}[ −Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} σ′_A(n) r_A(m|D| − Nn) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)) + (h/u) r_A(m)(2Γ′/Γ(k) − 2 log 2π + log(N|D|/m) + 2L′/L(1, ε)) − 2 Σ_{n=1}^∞ σ_A(−n) r_A(m|D| + nN) Q_{k−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) ], with σ_A, σ′_A as in (4.4)–(4.6) (so σ_A(−n) = δ(n)R_{A𝔫}(n) by (4.6a)), P_{k−1} the Legendre polynomial and Q_{k−1} the Legendre function of the second kind (5.7). Then Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,A}q^m is a cusp form of weight 2k and level N, and L_A(f,k) = 0, L′_A(f,k) = 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!√|D|) · (f, Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,A}q^m) for all f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2k and level N. CORRECTED: (a) the paper prints σ_A(n) in the last sum; it must be σ_A(−n) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38); (b) the paper writes Σ_{m≥0} in the final formula although a_{m,A} is defined only for m > 0 (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E46).
items.note: Derived from (4.5) + (5.1) + the four integrals: (2k−2)!/(4πm)^{2k−1}·a_m = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k·[…], and −log 4πm + log(Nδ/π) = −2log 2π + log(Nδ/m); renormalising a_m = (4π)^{k−1}(k−1)!/(2k−2)!·a_{m,A} gives the constant 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!√δ) (checked). Numerical confirmation (N = 1, f = Δ, k = 6, D = −7): with σ_A(−n), a_{2,A}/a_{1,A} = −24.0000000000 and a_{3,A}/a_{1,A} = 252.000000000, and L′_A(Δ,6) = L(Δ,6)·L′(Δ⊗χ₋₇,6) = 1.46317630872233 = 2^{23}π^{12}/(10!√7)·a_{1,A}·(Δ,Δ) with (Δ,Δ) = 1.03536205680432·10⁻⁶ (the known Petersson norm); with the printed σ_A(n) the coefficients are not proportional to Δ. Second check at level N = 3 (f = (η(z)η(3z))⁶, k = 3, D = −11, ε(3) = +1): a_{2,A}/a_{1,A} = −5.9999967, a_{4,A}/a_{1,A} = 4.00011 (tail truncated at n = 2000; exact values −6, 4 = a(2), a(4)), and L′_A(f,3) = L(f,3)L′(f⊗χ₋₁₁,3) = 3.92350251067 matches 2^{11}π⁶/(4!√11)·a_{1,A}·(f,f) to 6·10⁻⁸ with (f,f) = 5.74981176452619·10⁻⁵ obtained independently from the corrected (5.5)/(5.6) — which also confirms PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E43 against the paper's own (5.8) constant. Nearest plans: GZ.6/GZ.8 (YZZ's weight-2 analytic kernel and its specialisation to X₀(N)); nothing plans the weight-2k (k > 1) formula, whose arithmetic interpretation (Ch. V §4, heights of Heegner cycles) is also not planned (GeneralizedHeegnerCycles GH.0–GH.8 concern p-adic Abel–Jacobi images, not heights). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Logarithmic growth condition (6.1) at the cusps
items.statement: Let Φ̃ ∈ M̃₂(Γ₀(N)), i.e. a smooth function on ℌ with Φ̃|₂γ = Φ̃ for all γ ∈ Γ₀(N) (Chap. IV §5). For a cusp ξ ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞} choose α ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with α(∞) = ξ. Φ̃ satisfies (6.1) at ξ if there are constants A_ξ, B_ξ and ε > 0 with (Φ̃|₂α)(z) = A_ξ log y + B_ξ + O(y^{−ε}) as y = Im z → ∞. Motivation stated on p. 295: for k = 1 the kernel Φ̃ of Prop. (4.5) has m = 0 Fourier term (A log y + B)y^{1−k} + O(e^{−cy}), all other terms exponentially small, so it grows like A log y + B instead of the decay O(y^{−ε}) required by Prop. (5.1); a priori there are 2H constants A_ξ, B_ξ (H = number of cusps).
items.note: No carrier for a non-holomorphic weight-2 Γ₀(N)-invariant function with prescribed log-growth at every cusp exists in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Nearest: Tau Ceti cusp-vanishing/boundedness of slashed functions, tauceti:IsZeroAt/IsBoundedAt lemmas in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Rat/Slash.lean:55-77 (isZeroAt_rat_slash, isBoundedAt_rat_slash: holomorphic-type conditions, not log growth). The growth-condition bookkeeping is part of holomorphic projection, whose adelic version GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans ("Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels ..., holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection"), but no stage names this classical condition. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Cusps of Γ₀(N): number and invariants (quoted standard fact)
items.statement: The number H of cusps of Γ₀(N) is Σ_{N₁ | N, N₁ > 0} φ(gcd(N₁, N/N₁)) (φ = Euler's function). A cusp ξ = a/c with (a, c) = 1 is determined by the pair of invariants N₁ = (c, N) and the class of (c/N₁)^{−1}·a modulo (N₁, N/N₁).
items.note: Planned by the Tau Ceti ModularForms roadmap, Layer 10A: "For congruence subgroups, prove cofiniteness, identify its cusp-orbit subtype with Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ), and compute the cusp count ε∞". The explicit Γ₀(N) formula and the (N₁, class) invariants are not named there. Library: Mathlib has only the surjection from cosets to cusp orbits (mathlib:cosetToCuspOrbit, Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean:174; surjective_cosetToCuspOrbit :195) and widths (strictWidthInfty_Gamma0 :448); Tau Ceti has cusp widths (tauceti:Subgroup.integerCuspWidth, TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Basic.lean:143). No count formula found (grep for totient in both ModularForms trees: none).

items.name: Hecke's-trick Poincaré series P_{m,s} of weight 2 and the unfolding identity
items.statement: For N ≥ 1, m ≥ 1 and Re(s) > 0 put P_{m,s}(z) = Σ_{Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} y^s e^{2πimz}|₂γ = Σ_{(a b; c d) ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (cz+d)^{−2}|cz+d|^{−2s} y^s e^{2πim(az+b)/(cz+d)} (absolutely convergent). The majorant P*_{m,σ} (σ = Re s, termwise absolute values) is O(y^{−1−σ}) at every cusp with O-constant O(σ^{−1}) as σ → 0. If Φ̃ = Σ a_m(y)e^{2πimx} ∈ M̃₂(Γ₀(N)) is O(y^{−ε}) at each cusp and 0 < σ < ε, then (Φ̃, P_{m,s̄}) = ∫₀^∞ e^{−4πmy} a_m(y) y^s dy, and for a holomorphic Φ = Σ a_m q^m, (Φ, P_{m,s̄}) = Γ(1+s)(4πm)^{−1−s} a_m. P_m = lim_{s→0} P_{m,s} is a holomorphic cusp form of weight 2 on Γ₀(N) ("known", proved by computing the Fourier coefficients of P_{m,s} as functions of s). Consequently the holomorphic projection Φ of Φ̃ has a_m = 4πm lim_{s→0, Re s>0} ∫₀^∞ e^{−4πmy} a_m(y) y^s dy (the case A = B = 0 of (6.2)).
items.note: No Poincaré series for Γ₀(N) in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep 'Poincare' in TauCeti/NumberTheory: no file). QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3 plans Poincaré series for harmonic Maass forms ("construct Poincare series and pairing/exact-sequence interfaces"), a different object; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans adelic holomorphic projection. Neither plans the weight-2 Hecke-trick continuation to s = 0. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (6.2) Proposition: holomorphic projection of a weight-2 form with logarithmic growth at the cusps
items.statement: Let Φ̃(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} a_m(y)e^{2πimx} ∈ M̃₂(Γ₀(N)) satisfy the growth condition (6.1) at all cusps ξ, and suppose A_ξ = A(N₁), B_ξ = B(N₁) depend only on N₁ = gcd(N, denominator of ξ). Let {α(M), β(M) : M | N} be the solution of the non-singular linear system (6.3) Σ_{M|N} ((M,N₁)²/M²) α(M) = A(N₁) (N₁ | N), (6.4) Σ_{M|N} ((M,N₁)²/M²) {β(M) + α(M) log((M,N₁)²/M)} = B(N₁) (N₁ | N). Then there is a holomorphic cusp form Φ = Σ_{m≥1} a_m e^{2πimz} ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) with (Φ, f) = (Φ̃, f) for all f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) and, for (m, N) = 1, (6.5) a_m = lim_{s→0} [4πm ∫₀^∞ a_m(y) e^{−4πmy} y^s dy + 24α(1)σ₁(m)s^{−1}] + 24β(1)σ₁(m) + 48α(1)[σ′₁(m) − σ₁(m)(log 2m + 1/2 + ζ′/ζ(2))], where σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d, σ′₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d log d. (Proof: subtract Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)}, which is orthogonal to cusp forms and has expansion A(N₁) log y + B(N₁) + O(y^{−1} log y) at ξ, then apply the case A = B = 0.)
items.note: The method (holomorphic projection of a non-holomorphic kernel of moderate growth, with Eisenstein corrections) is planned in its adelic Yuan–Zhang–Zhang form by GZ.6: "Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms, holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection ... Compare the arithmetic height kernel with the analytic derivative modulo the explicitly identified constant/Eisenstein/old components". This explicit classical form (log growth, the system (6.3)-(6.4), formula (6.5)) is not named in any stage; if the atlas wants this paper's route, it is a new target. I re-derived (6.5) from the p. 298 asymptotics (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/267); consistent.

items.name: Weight-2 non-holomorphic Eisenstein series E_{2,s} on SL₂(ℤ) and the functions E = E_{2,s}|_{s=0}, F = ∂_s E_{2,s}|_{s=0}
items.statement: E_{2,s}(z) = Σ_{γ∈Γ∞\SL₂(ℤ)} y^s|₂γ = ½ Σ_{(c,d)=1} (cz+d)^{−2}|cz+d|^{−2s} y^s, absolutely convergent for Re(s) > 0 (printed: Re(s) > 2, see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E51), a non-holomorphic modular function of weight 2 on SL₂(ℤ), orthogonal to holomorphic cusp forms (it is P_{m,s} for N = 1, m = 0), of the form y^s + c(s)y^{−1−s} + O(e^{−y}) with c(s) and the O-coefficients holomorphic near s = 0. E(z) := E_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0}, F(z) := ∂/∂s E_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0} (holomorphic continuation, or limit s ↘ 0) lie in M̃₂(SL₂(ℤ)), are orthogonal to cusp forms, and E(z) = 1 + O(1/y), F(z) = log y + O(y^{−1} log y) as y → ∞. Consequently, if Φ̃ ∈ M̃₂(SL₂(ℤ)) has Φ̃ = A log y + B + O(y^{−ε}), then Φ̃ − AF − BE has the same scalar products with holomorphic forms and is O(y^{−ε}).
items.note: Mathlib has only the holomorphic quasimodular E₂: mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2 (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/E2/Defs.lean:60), its q-expansion mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_eq_tsum_cexp (E2/Summable.lean:102, E2 z = 1 − 24 Σ σ₁(n) qⁿ) and transformation law mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_slash_action (E2/Transform.lean:229, E2|γ = E2 − (1/(2ζ(2)))·D2 γ). GZ's E equals E₂ − 3/(πy) (my check: c(0) = −3/π), which is not defined in either library; F (the s-derivative) has no counterpart. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.2 plans adelic Eisenstein series continuation ("Prove meromorphic continuation of operators and Eisenstein series"), not this classical weight-2 family. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Fourier expansion of the weight-0 Eisenstein series and of E_{2,s} (quoted 'well-known')
items.statement: For E(z,s) = Σ_{Γ∞\SL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s (weight 0): E(z,s) = y^s + π^{1/2}Γ(s−½)ζ(2s−1)/(Γ(s)ζ(2s)) · y^{1−s} + (2π^s y^{1/2}/(Γ(s)ζ(2s))) Σ_{m≠0} |m|^{1/2−s} σ_{2s−1}(m) K_{s−1/2}(2π|m|y) e^{2πimx}, σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν, K_ν = K-Bessel function. The identity (cz+d)^{−2}|cz+d|^{−2s} y^s = (2i/(s+1)) ∂/∂z (y^{s+1}/|cz+d|^{2s+2}) (printed with (cz+d)^{−1}, see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E47) gives E_{2,s}(z) = (2i/(s+1)) ∂/∂z E(z, s+1), hence E_{2,s}(z) = y^s − π^{1/2} s Γ(s+½)ζ(2s+1)/(Γ(s+2)ζ(2s+2)) · y^{−1−s} + Σ_{m≠0} e_{2,s}(m,y)e^{2πimz} with e_{2,s}(m,y) = (2π^{s+1}|m|^{−s−1/2}/(Γ(s+2)ζ(2s+2))) σ_{2s+1}(m) e^{2πmy} (∂/∂y − 2πm)(√y K_{s+1/2}(2π|m|y)).
items.note: Checked: the ∂_z identity (with the square), the constant term (−s/(s+1))·φ(s+1), and e_{2,s} by differentiating the m-th term of E(z,s+1). No real-analytic Eisenstein series or K-Bessel function in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep besselK/BesselK: only unrelated hits; grep nonholomorphic/realAnalytic: none). AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.2 plans adelic Eisenstein series and their continuation, not the explicit classical Fourier expansion. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Tabulated K-Bessel integral
items.statement: For m ≥ 1 and 0 < t < Re(s): ∫₀^∞ y^{s−1/2} K_{t+1/2}(2πmy) e^{−2πmy} dy = Γ(s+t+1)Γ(s−t)π^{1/2} / (Γ(s+1)(4πm)^{s+1/2}). With the integration by parts ∫₀^∞ e_{2,t}(m,y) e^{−4πmy} y^s dy = −(2π^{1+t} m^{−1/2−t}/(Γ(2+t)ζ(2+2t))) σ_{1+2t}(m) · s · ∫₀^∞ y^{s−1/2} K_{1/2+t}(2πmy) e^{−2πmy} dy.
items.note: Checked against the standard formula ∫₀^∞ x^{μ−1}e^{−αx}K_ν(αx)dx = √π Γ(μ+ν)Γ(μ−ν)/((2α)^μ Γ(μ+½)) with μ = s+½, α = 2πm, ν = t+½: agrees. No K-Bessel function in either library; no stage plans it. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Mellin asymptotics of the Fourier coefficients of E and F
items.statement: Write E(z) = Σ_m e(m,y)e^{2πimz}, F(z) = Σ_m f(m,y)e^{2πimz}. For m > 0: e(m,y) = −24σ₁(m), and as s → 0 (Re s > 0): ∫₀^∞ e(m,y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = −(6/(πm))σ₁(m) + o(1); ∫₀^∞ f(m,y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = ∂/∂t[−2π^{3/2+t}m^{−1/2−t}Γ(s+t+1)Γ(s−t)σ_{1+2t}(m)/((4πm)^{s+1/2}Γ(2+t)Γ(s)ζ(2+2t))]_{t=0} = −24 Γ(s+1)/(4πm)^{s+1} · [2σ′₁(m) + σ₁(m)(log(π/m) + γ − 1 − 2ζ′/ζ(2) + 1/s)] = −(6/(πm))σ₁(m)s^{−1} − (12/(πm))σ′₁(m) + (12/(πm))σ₁(m)(log 2m + ½ + ζ′/ζ(2)) + o(1), γ = Euler's constant. For (m, N) = 1 the m-th coefficient of Φ̃* = Φ̃ − Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} is a*_m(y) = a_m(y) − α(1)f(m,y) − β(1)e(m,y); these give (6.5).
items.note: Verified the Laurent expansion by hand (ψ(s+1) − ψ(s) = 1/s, ψ(2) = 1 − γ, ζ(2) = π²/6) and that it yields (6.5). Library: the statement e(m,y) = −24σ₁(m) for m > 0 is the non-constant part of the q-expansion mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_eq_tsum_cexp (E2/Summable.lean:102) since E = E₂ − 3/(πy); the Mellin statements have no library or stage counterpart. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Behaviour of E(Mz) and F(Mz) at the cusps of Γ₀(N)
items.statement: Let M | N and ξ = a/c with (a,c) = 1, (c, N) = N₁; α = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ). Put a′ = (M/(M,N₁))a, c′ = c/(M,N₁) ((a′,c′) = 1), complete to α′ = (a′ b′; c′ d′) ∈ SL₂(ℤ), and relate z, z′ by c′z′ + d′ = ((M,N₁)/M)(cz+d); then (a′z′+b′)/(c′z′+d′) = M(az+b)/(cz+d), y′ = ((M,N₁)²/M)y, and E_{2,s}(Mz)|₂α = ((M,N₁)^{2+2s}/M^{2+s}) y^s + O(y^{−1−s}); hence E(Mz)|₂α = (M,N₁)²/M² + O(1/y), F(Mz)|₂α = ((M,N₁)²/M²)(log y + log((M,N₁)²/M)) + O(y^{−1} log y). Therefore Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} has expansion A(N₁) log y + B(N₁) + O(y^{−1} log y) at ξ iff (6.3), (6.4) hold.
items.note: Checked (M, c) = (M, N₁) since M | N, and the scaling of y′. No library or stage counterpart (depends on PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/264). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Invertibility of the matrix C_N and the tridiagonal inverse (6.6)
items.statement: Let C_N = (C_N(N₁, M))_{N₁, M | N}, C_N(N₁, M) = (M, N₁)²/M² (a σ₀(N) × σ₀(N) matrix). The entries are multiplicative, C_{∏p^{ν_p}}(∏p^{λ_p}, ∏p^{μ_p}) = ∏ C_{p^{ν_p}}(p^{λ_p}, p^{μ_p}), so C_N is the Kronecker product of the C_{p^ν} (N = ∏ p^ν). For N = p^ν, C_{p^ν}(p^λ, p^μ) = p^{2 min(λ,μ) − 2μ} (rows λ = 0..ν: (1, p^{−2}, …, p^{−2ν}), (1, 1, p^{−2}, …, p^{−2ν+2}), …, (1, …, 1)), and (6.6) C_{p^ν}^{−1} = (p² − 1)^{−1} × the tridiagonal matrix with diagonal (p², p²+1, …, p²+1, p²), superdiagonal −1, subdiagonal −p². In particular C_N is invertible and (6.3)-(6.4) have a unique solution.
items.note: Verified C·C^{−1} = I for ν = 1, 2 by hand. Generic Kronecker-product facts exist in Mathlib (Matrix.kroneckerMap), but not these matrices; no stage plans them. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (6.7) Proposition: explicit α(1), β(1)
items.statement: In the setting of (6.2): α(1) = ρ^{−1} Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²) A(N₁), β(1) = ρ^{−1} Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²)(B(N₁) − 2A(N₁) log N₁) − 2α(1) Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1), where μ is the Möbius function and ρ = ∏_{p|N}(1 − p^{−2}) = Σ_{N₁|N} μ(N₁)/N₁². (Proof: C_N^{−1}(1, N₁) = ρ^{−1}μ(N₁)/N₁², and Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²) s_p(N₁) = −2 Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²) A(N₁)(v_p(N₁) + 1/(p²−1)) with s_p(N₁) = Σ_{M|N} C_N(N₁,M)α(M)(v_p(M) − 2 min{v_p(N₁), v_p(M)}).)
items.note: Proof re-checked (bracket μC(1,p^μ) − p^{−2}(μ−2)C(p,p^μ) = 2p^{−2μ}; Σ_{μ≥1} p^{−2μ}C^{−1}(p^μ,p^κ) = −μ(p^κ)p^{−2κ}(κ + 1/(p²−1))). One misprint in the proof (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E48). Mathlib has the Möbius function (ArithmeticFunction.moebius) but nothing specific; no stage. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (6.8) Proposition: the constants A(N₁), B(N₁) of the weight-2 kernel Φ̃
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. Let Φ̃ be the function of Prop. (4.5) for k = 1, i.e. Φ̃ = (√δ/2π)·∂/∂s Φ̃_s|_{s=0} with Φ̃_s = Tr^{ND}_N(θ_𝒜(z)E_s^{(1)}(Nz)) (Prop. (1.2)). Then Φ̃ satisfies the hypotheses of (6.2) with A(N₁) = (h/(2u²)) ε(N₁)N₁/N, B(N₁) = A(N₁)(log(N₁²δ/(Nπ)) − γ + 2(L′/L)(1, ε)) (N₁ | N), γ = Euler's constant. (Proof: at a cusp with invariant N₁, (Φ̃_s|₂α)(z) = (1/(2u))(ε(N₁)/N₂)[L(2s+1,ε)(N₁y/N₂)^s − (iV_s(0)/|D|^{1/2}) L(2s,ε)(N₁y/N₂)^{−s}] + … with N₂ = N/N₁, V_s(0) = −π^{1/2}Γ(s+½)i/Γ(s+1), using Lemma (2.3) and (2.2) of Chap. IV and the count of cosets of Γ₀(ND)\Γ₀(N)α with D | c (one) and (c, D) = 1 (|D| of them).)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §6, (6.8) Proposition and proof, pp. 301-303
items.note: I re-derived A, B from the displayed cusp expansion using L(0,ε) = (√δ/π)L(1,ε) and the functional equation (log-derivative of L at 0), and checked the per-coset factor δ^{−3/2} (printed δ^{−3/2}, confirmed on the high-resolution page p. 303). The case N₁ = N reproduces the constant term of Prop. (4.5). No library or stage counterpart. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: α(1), β(1) for the kernel Φ̃ (Props. (6.7) + (6.8))
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. For Φ̃ as in (6.8): α(1) = (h/(2u²)) N^{−1} ρ^{−1} Σ_{N₁|N} μ(N₁)ε(N₁)/N₁ = (h/(2u²)) N^{−1} ∏_{p|N}(1 + ε(p)/p)^{−1}, β(1) = α(1)(log(δ/(Nπ)) − γ + 2(L′/L)(1, ε) − 2 Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1)).
items.note: Checked: ρ^{−1}∏(1 − ε(p)/p) = ∏(1 + ε(p)/p)^{−1} since ε(p)² = 1 for p | N. Note 24α(1) = −hκ/u² with κ of (6.9). No library/stage counterpart. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Mellin integral of the coefficients of Φ̃ (k = 1) and the Legendre-function asymptotics
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. For m > 0, a_m(y) = A_m log y + B_m + Σ_{n≥1} C_{mn} q₀(4πnNy/δ) (from Prop. (4.5); q₀(t) = ∫₁^∞ e^{−tx}dx/x), with A_m = (h/u)r_𝒜(m), B_m = A_m(log(Nδ/π) − γ + 2(L′/L)(1,ε)) − Σ_{1≤n≤mδ/N} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(mδ − Nn), C_{mn} = −σ_𝒜(−n) r_𝒜(mδ + Nn) (σ_𝒜, σ′_𝒜 as in Prop. (4.6)). Then ∫₀^∞ a_m(y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = Γ(s+1)(4πm)^{−s−1}(A_m (Γ′/Γ)(s+1) − A_m log 4πm + B_m) + Σ_n C_{mn} ∫₀^∞ q₀(4πnNy/δ)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy, and ∫₀^∞ q₀(4πnNy/δ)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = 2Γ(2s+2)/((4πm)^{s+1}Γ(s+2)) · Q_s(1 + 2nN/(mδ)) + ε_n(s), ε_n(s) = O(n^{−s−2}) (uniformly near s = 0), ε_n(0) = 0, using Q₀(1+2t) = ½ log(1 + 1/t) and Q_s(1+2t) = (Γ(s+1)²/(2Γ(2s+2)))[t^{−s−1} + O(t^{−s−2})] (t → ∞). Since C_{mn} = O(n^c) for all c > 0, 4πm ∫₀^∞ a_m(y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = B_m − A_m(γ + log 4πm) + (2Γ(2s+2)/((4πm)^sΓ(s+2))) Σ_n C_{mn} Q_s(1 + 2nN/(mδ)) + o(1) (s → 0).
items.note: Checked the s = 0 and n → ∞ matching and the Legendre asymptotic (from Q_ν(z) ~ √πΓ(ν+1)/(Γ(ν+3/2)(2z)^{ν+1}) and duplication). No Legendre function of the second kind in either library (Mathlib has only Polynomial.shiftedLegendre); no stage. Corrected at integration: the third (archimedean) term carries σ_𝒜(−n), not the printed σ_𝒜(n) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38, which covers this page too). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (6.9) Theorem (i): the weight-2 cusp form Φ_𝒜 representing L′_𝒜(f,1)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. There exists a holomorphic cusp form Φ_𝒜(z) = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,𝒜} e^{2πimz} of weight 2 and level N such that L_𝒜(f, 1) = 0 and L′_𝒜(f, 1) = (8π²/√δ)(f, Φ_𝒜) for every cusp form f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2 and level N. (δ = |D|; the constant equals 8π²/√|D|, consistent with Chap. I (6.2).)
items.note: The analytic half of Gross–Zagier (derivative of the Rankin kernel, holomorphic projection) is planned in adelic form by GZ.6 ("Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, ... holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection. Prove the functional-equation vanishing that permits differentiation") and specialised by GZ.8 ("Specialize to X₀(N) ..."); L_𝒜(f,1) = 0 is the sign −1 statement (GZ.8: "For matching local signs deduce the global sign −1"). Existence of some Φ_𝒜 with this property is formal (Riesz representation on the newspace); the content is (ii). Printed issue on this line: duplicated word (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E49). Coordinator lead 'constant should be √|D|' checked: not a mistake, δ := |D| is Chap. IV notation (p. 273).

items.name: (6.9) Theorem (ii): the Fourier coefficients a_{m,𝒜} of Φ_𝒜 for (m, N) = 1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. For m prime to N, a_{m,𝒜} = − Σ_{1≤n≤m|D|/N} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) + (h/u) r_𝒜(m)[log(N|D|/(4π²m)) − 2γ + 2(L′/L)(1, ε)] + lim_{s→0}[−2 Σ_{n≥1} σ_𝒜(−n) r_𝒜(m|D| + nN) Q_s(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) − (hκ/u²) σ₁(m) s^{−1}] + (hκ/u²)[σ₁(m)(log(N/|D|) + 2 Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1) + 2 + 2(ζ′/ζ)(2) − 2(L′/L)(1, ε)) + Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²)], where σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d, κ = −12/(N ∏_{p|N}(1 + ε(p)/p)), σ_𝒜, σ′_𝒜 as in Prop. (4.6), Q_s = Legendre function of the second kind, γ = Euler's constant.
items.note: Re-derived from (6.5), (6.7), (6.8) and the Mellin integral (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/273): B_m − A_m(γ + log 4πm) gives the first two lines, 24α(1) = −hκ/u², and the remaining terms combine using σ₁(m) log m − 2σ′₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²). Agrees with print. No stage plans the explicit Fourier coefficients of the holomorphic projection (GZ.6/GZ.8 plan YZZ's kernel, whose explicit X₀(N) coefficients are not a named target). Nearest: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8. Corrected at integration: the third (archimedean) term carries σ_𝒜(−n), not the printed σ_𝒜(n) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38, which covers this page too). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Endomorphisms act faithfully on the cotangent space; the Hecke algebra embeds in End_ℚ(S) (quoted)
items.statement: If J is an abelian variety over ℚ and S its cotangent space at the origin, End_ℚ(J) acts faithfully on S. For J = J₀(N), S is identified with the space of cusp forms of weight 2 and level N with rational Fourier coefficients; hence 𝕋 → End_ℚ(S) is injective and dim_ℚ 𝕋 ≤ d², d = dim_ℚ S = dim_ℂ S₂(Γ₀(N)).
items.note: Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (no Jacobian of X₀(N) as an abelian variety). Nearest plans: ModularCurvesPartII:R14.5 ("construct its Hecke ideal and the quotient A_f of ... J₀(N) ..., identify the differential eigenspaces"); the Tau Ceti ModularForms roadmap Layer 8 declares the algebraic q-expansion route (S_k ≅ H⁰(X, ω^k) over ℚ) out of scope. Neither states faithfulness on the cotangent space or the rational structure of S. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.3.

items.name: Perfect pairing between the Hecke algebra and cusp forms; Hom(𝕋, ℂ) ↔ cusp forms
items.statement: With S = S₂(Γ₀(N)) ∩ ℚ[[q]] and a_m : S → ℚ the m-th Fourier coefficient, the pairing β : 𝕋 × S → ℚ, β(T, f) = a₁(Tf), is perfect (so dim_ℚ 𝕋 = d), using a₁(T_m f) = a_m(f). Consequently every ℚ-linear α : 𝕋 → ℂ is β(·, f) for a unique f ∈ S ⊗ ℂ, and Σ_{m≥1} α(T_m) q^m = f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)).
items.note: Ingredient in library: tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.qExpansion_coeff_one_heckeRingHomCharSpace_heckeTCompositeGamma0 (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/Nebentypus/Composite.lean:123): for n ≠ 0 and F in the character space modFormCharSpace k χ of Γ₁(N), (qExpansion 1 (T_n F)).coeff 1 = (qExpansion 1 F).coeff n — the relation a₁(T_n f) = a_n(f), on the complex space. The perfect pairing itself and the rational structure are absent. Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8G plans only the newspace version ("after ⊗ℂ its characters — equivalently its eigenlines — are exactly the normalized newforms"), not this duality. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.3.

items.name: Generating series of Hecke-translated heights is a cusp form; g_𝒜 is a cusp form (first assertion of Chap. I, Theorem (6.1))
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. For any y, z ∈ J₀(N)(H), Σ_{m≥1} <y, T_m z> q^m is a cusp form of weight 2 and level N (with complex coefficients), since T ↦ <y, Tz> is ℚ-linear on 𝕋. In particular g_𝒜(z) = Σ_{m≥1} <c, T_m c^σ> e^{2πimz} ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) ⊗ ℂ. This has nothing to do with Heegner points.
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, p. 306 (proof of the first assertion of Theorem (6.1) of Chap. I)
items.note: The adelic analogue (modularity of the Hecke-correspondence generating series) is planned in GZ.6: "Establish modularity of the curve-level Chow-valued series through the relevant product formula and theta construction"; pairing with the height pairing gives this statement. The paper's elementary route (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/276, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/277: faithfulness + perfect pairing) is not planned. Partial coverage.

items.name: Manin–Drinfeld theorem (quoted): the cuspidal class (0) − (∞) is torsion
items.statement: The divisor class of (0) − (∞) on X₀(N) has finite order in J₀(N)(ℚ). Hence c = (x) − (∞) and d = (x) − (0) give the same class in J(H) ⊗ ℚ, and <c, T_m c^σ> = <c, T_m d^σ>.
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, p. 306 (cited as '[4], Cor. 3.6', intended [41] = Manin, Cor. 3.6; issue G/E4); also Chap. I §9, p. 232
items.note: ER.7: "Construct modular units, their divisors at cusps, the relevant Manin–Drinfeld relation and the modular-curve K₂ classes". That plans the relation for its own regulator application; the general statement for the cusps 0, ∞ of X₀(N) is the same Manin–Drinfeld argument. Not in the libraries (no J₀(N)).

items.name: Local decomposition of <c, T_m d^σ> and the archimedean contribution
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. For (m, N) = 1, <c, T_m d^σ> = Σ_v <c, T_m d^σ>_v over places v of H (Néron local symbols; when |c| ∩ |T_m d^σ| ≠ ∅, i.e. r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0, defined as in Chap. II §5). By Chap. II Props. (4.2), (5.8) and Chap. IV Prop. (4.6)(a): Σ_{v|∞} <c, T_m d^σ>_v = lim_{s→1}[−2u² Σ_{n≥1} σ_𝒜(−n) r_𝒜(m|D| + nN) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) − hκσ₁(m)/(s − 1)] + hκ[σ₁(m)(log(N/|D|) + 2Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1) + 2 + 2(ζ′/ζ)(2) − 2(L′/L)(1, ε)) + Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²)] + hu r_𝒜(m)[2(L′/L)(1, ε) − 2γ − 2 log 2π + log|D|], with σ_𝒜(n) = Σ_{d|n} ε_𝒜(n, d) (ε_𝒜(n,d) ∈ {0, 1, −1} as in Chap. IV Prop. (3.2)), κ = κ_N = −12/(N ∏_{p|N}(1 + 1/p)), σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d.
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, pp. 306-307 (first display on p. 307)
items.note: Method planned: GZ.2 ("Export local height decomposition ..."; archimedean Green kernels) and GZ.7 ("Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization"). The explicit X₀(N) resolvent-kernel formula is not a named target. Here κ has ε(p) = 1 for all p | N (Heegner hypothesis), matching (6.9). Corrected at integration: the third (archimedean) term carries σ_𝒜(−n), not the printed σ_𝒜(n) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38, which covers this page too).

items.name: Sum of the non-archimedean local symbols
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. Combining Chap. III Props. (9.2), (9.7), (9.11) over all p and Chap. IV Prop. (4.6)(b): for (m, N) = 1, <c, T_m d^σ>_finite = −u² Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) + hu r_𝒜(m) log(N/m), where σ′_𝒜(n) = Σ_{d|n} ε_𝒜(n, d) log(n/d²).
items.note: Method planned in GZ.7: "Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions ... Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory". The explicit X₀(N) sum is not a named target.

items.name: The coefficient identity <c, T_m c^σ> = u² a_{m,𝒜} for (m, N) = 1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. For (m, N) = 1, <c, T_m c^σ> = u² a_{m,𝒜}, where a_{m,𝒜} is the m-th Fourier coefficient of the cusp form Φ_𝒜 of Theorem (6.9) of Chap. IV. Consequently g_𝒜 − u² Φ_𝒜 is an old form in S₂(Γ₀(N)).
items.note: Checked: archimedean + finite sums (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/280, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/281) add up to u² times (6.9)(ii) (the hu r_𝒜(m) terms combine to hu r_𝒜(m)[log(N|D|/(4π²m)) − 2γ + 2L′/L(1,ε)]). The passage 'coefficients agree for (m,N)=1 ⇒ difference is old' uses Atkin–Lehner/strong multiplicity one (Tau Ceti has strong multiplicity one: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/StrongMultiplicityOne.lean). The explicit coefficient identity is not a named atlas target (GZ.8 plans the resulting L′ formula, see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/26 and PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/28). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: Dependence of g_𝒜 on the Heegner point x
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. g_𝒜 is not quite independent of the choice of the Heegner point x (as erroneously asserted in the announcement [17]), but it is independent up to the addition of an old form. For (m, N) = 1, <c, T_m c^σ> is independent of x, because any two choices of x are related by an element of G × W and this action commutes with T_m for (m, N) = 1.
items.note: HE.1: "Construct a compatible family of points P_c and show its dependence on choices is given by the specified Galois/Hecke actions and torsion translation." The height-invariance under W is not separately named. The correction of [17] is the paper's own and is not recorded as an issue (brief).

items.name: The χ-component c_χ, the f-isotypical component c_{χ,f}, and L(f, χ, s)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. For a character χ of G (≅ Cl_K): c_χ = Σ_{σ∈G} χ^{−1}(σ) c^σ ∈ J(H) ⊗ ℂ (h times the standard eigencomponent). By G-invariance of <,>, <c_χ, T_m c_χ> = h Σ_{σ∈G} χ(σ) <c, T_m c^σ>. For a normalized newform f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)), c_{χ,f} = projection of c_χ to the f-isotypical component of J(H) ⊗ ℂ under 𝕋. L(f, χ, s) = Σ_𝒜 χ(𝒜) L_𝒜(f, s) (Chap. I (5.4)); hence Σ_𝒜 χ(𝒜) g_𝒜 = h^{−1} Σ_{m≥1} <c_χ, T_m c_χ> q^m.
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, p. 308; Chapter I, §6, p. 230
items.note: GZ.8: "Identify the L-linear pairing of the χ- and χ⁻¹-Heegner points with the central derivative"; GZ.0 packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/trace-versus-average ("The trace Tr(P) = Σ_{σ ∈ Gal(H/K)} σP lies in E(K) ... ĥ_ℚ(Av(P)) = ĥ(Tr P)/h²") fixes the trace/average normalisation.

items.name: (1.1) Corollary: non-negativity of L′(f, χ, 1)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. Let f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) be any (normalized) newform and χ any character of Gal(H/K). Then L′(f, χ, 1) ≥ 0. (Immediate from Theorem (6.3): the Petersson product and the global height pairing are positive definite.)
items.note: Not stated in any stage. Ingredients planned: GZ.8 (the formula) and GZ.1 ("Prove positivity for ample symmetric bundles and characterize the zero locus as torsion"); library ingredient for elliptic curves: tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight_nonneg (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean:266). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: (1.2) Corollary: Galois conjugates of L(f, χ, s) vanish to the same order ≤ 1 or all to order ≥ 3
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. Let f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) be any newform and χ any character of Gal(H/K). Then either all conjugates L(f^α, χ^α, s) (α ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)) have a simple zero at s = 1 or else all have a zero of order ≥ 3. (Each has odd order by the functional equation; L′(f^α, χ^α, 1) = 0 iff c_{χ^α, f^α} = c^α_{χ,f} = 0 in J(H) ⊗ ℂ.)
items.note: No stage plans Galois-invariance of the order of vanishing. Nearest: Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8G (conjugate newforms f^σ, a_n(f^σ) = σ(a_n(f))) and GZ.8. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: (1.3) Corollary: Galois invariance of ord_{s=1} L(f, s) in low orders
items.statement: Let f be any newform of weight 2 (level N) and f^α (α ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)) any conjugate. Then ord_{s=1} L(f,s) = 0 ⇔ ord_{s=1} L(f^α,s) = 0; = 1 ⇔ = 1; ≥ 2 ⇔ ≥ 2; ≥ 3 ⇔ ≥ 3. (Proof: L(f,1) = (non-vanishing period)·(algebraic number conjugated by α); same parity by the functional equations; if L(f,1) = 0 ≠ L′(f,1) the sign is −1, choose K as in the paper with L_ε(f,1) ≠ 0 by Waldspurger, then L′(f,1)L_ε(f,1) = L′(f,1_K,1) and Corollary (1.2).)
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, (1.3) Corollary and proof, p. 309
items.note: No stage plans it. Inputs planned elsewhere: twist nonvanishing (RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.2, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/288), period algebraicity (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/289), the GZ formula (GZ.8). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: Waldspurger's nonvanishing theorem, as used (quoted: [36] Th. 2.3, [37] Th. 4)
items.statement: If f is a weight-2 newform of level N whose L-function has sign −1 (f|w_N = f), there is an imaginary quadratic field K = ℚ(√D) as in this paper (D odd fundamental, (D, N) = 1, every p | N split in K) with L_ε(f, 1) ≠ 0, where L_ε(f, s) = Σ ε(n) a(n) n^{−s}, ε = (D/·).
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, proof of (1.3), p. 309; §2, p. 312
items.note: BSD.2: "Prove the quadratic-twist nonvanishing theorem needed to choose a Heegner field, including finitely many prescribed splitting/local character conditions compatible with the functional equation. For a weight-two newform, construct twists with nonzero central value in the sign + branch" (route via Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, not Waldspurger; same statement). BSD.2 also asks D ≠ −3, −4 and infinitely many K.

items.name: Algebraicity of L(f, 1) up to a period, compatible with Galois conjugation (quoted 'known')
items.statement: For a weight-2 newform f, L(f, 1) = Ω·a with Ω a non-vanishing period and a an algebraic number such that the corresponding number for f^α is a^α; in particular L(f,1) = 0 ⇔ L(f^α,1) = 0, and similarly for L_ε(f,1).
items.note: L1: "For a fixed normalized newform construct its coefficient field and the plus/minus eigenspaces over that field. Define period lines first ... Prove algebraicity of the period-normalized values". Galois equivariance of the period-normalized value under conjugation of f is not stated explicitly; partial.

items.name: Factorization L(f, 1_K, s) = L(f, s)·L_ε(f, s); for f ↔ E, L(E/K, s) = L(E, s)·L(E′, s)
items.statement: Let f be a weight-2 newform of level N and K as above (ε(N) = 1 with all p | N split). For χ = 1 (trivial character), L(f, 1, s) = Σ_𝒜 L_𝒜(f, s) = L(f, s)·L_ε(f, s), with functional equation of sign −1; L_ε(f, s) has sign equal to −(sign of L(f,s)). If L(E, s) = L(f, s), then L(f, 1, s) = L(E/K, s) and L_ε(f, s) = L(E′, s), E′ the twist of E by K (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/300).
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, proof of (1.3), p. 309; §2, pp. 310, 312
items.note: BSD.0: "For a quadratic character construct the existing quadratic twist and prove every local Euler-factor comparison, including bad primes, then the factorization L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^K,s)". Only the elliptic-curve case is planned; the case of f with non-rational coefficients (used in (1.3)) is not. Checked the Euler factors at p | N (split): (1 − a_p p^{−s})^{−2} on both sides.

items.name: Strong Weil curve and modular parametrization (quoted: [25], Faltings)
items.statement: (a) If E/ℚ has L(E, s) = L(f, s) for a modular form f, then f is a Hecke eigenform of weight 2 with coefficients in ℤ (verifiable by a finite computation for given E). (b) Conversely, for such f the periods of ω_f = 2πif(z)dz = Σ_{n≥1} a_n q^n dq/q define an elliptic curve E₀/ℚ (the strong Weil curve) with L(E₀, s) = L(f, s) [25]. (c) By Faltings' isogeny theorem every E/ℚ with L(E, s) = L(f, s) is isogenous to E₀ and admits a covering π: X₀(N) → E over ℚ (N = level of f) with π(∞) = 0.
items.note: R29.5: "Apply the weight-two, trivial-nebentypus quotient theorem ModularCurvesPartII R14.5 to the primitive newform ..., obtaining A_f as a quotient of J₀(N_E) ... Use R19's Tate-module identification and R28's isogeny theorem to obtain an isogeny A_f→E over Q. Compose the rational-cusp-normalised Abel–Jacobi map, the quotient map and this isogeny"; R28.4: "Establish the isogeny criterion when the rational Tate modules are isomorphic". (c) is exactly this route.

items.name: Manin constant c of the parametrization π
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. Let ω be a Néron differential on E (unique up to sign). Then π*(ω) = c·ω_f for a non-zero integer c; the sign of ω is chosen so that c > 0. (Quoted conjecture, not assumed: c divides the index of π_*H₁(X₀(N), ℤ) in H₁(E, ℤ) [25]; for the strong Weil parametrization this is Manin's conjecture c₀ = 1.)
items.note: GZ.3: "Construct differential pullbacks and Manin constants as comparison quantities with exact isogeny functoriality; never assume the Manin constant is universally one"; GZ.8 keeps "Manin constants" in the explicit formulas. That c is an integer is itself a theorem (not proved in the paper); no stage names the integrality.

items.name: The Heegner point P_K ∈ E(K) and its height
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. For a Heegner point x of discriminant D on X₀(N): P_K = Σ_{σ∈Gal(H/K)} π(x^σ) = Σ_σ π(x)^σ ∈ E(K) (sum in E(H)). It is independent of the choice of x up to sign and addition of a rational torsion point (printed: 'up to sign'; issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E58), and ĥ(P_K) = ĥ(c_{1,f})·deg(π), canonical heights on E and J₀(N) over K.
items.note: HE.1: "Map CM points to degree-zero Jacobian classes using a cusp ..., then to A or E through the existing modular quotient. Track denominators of ξ and the degree of the parametrization integrally ... Preserve the distinction between a trace to K and a point over its ring class field"; GZ.1: "Construct the bilinear height ... with adjunction under homomorphisms" (gives ĥ(π_* c_f) = deg π·ĥ(c_f)); GZ.0 packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/trace-versus-average.

items.name: Period comparison ‖ω‖² = c²‖ω_f‖²/deg(π)
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. With ‖ω‖² := ∬_{E(ℂ)} |ω ∧ ω̄| and ‖ω_f‖² = ∬_{X₀(N)(ℂ)} |ω_f ∧ ω̄_f| = 8π²(f, f): ‖ω‖² = c²‖ω_f‖²/deg(π).
items.note: GZ.3: "In dimension one identify the composition with the degree of the parametrization. Construct differential pullbacks and Manin constants"; GZ.0: "Construct explicit comparison maps for the choices of volume, differential ...". Checked: π*ω = cω_f and ∫_X |π*ω ∧ π*ω̄| = deg π ∫_E |ω ∧ ω̄|.

items.name: (2.1) Theorem: L′(E/K, 1) = ‖ω‖² ĥ(P_K)/(c² u_K² |D|^{1/2})
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. Then L′(E/K, 1) = ‖ω‖²·ĥ(P_K)/(c²·u_K²·|D|^{1/2}), ĥ the canonical height on E over K, c the Manin constant, ‖ω‖² = ∬_{E(ℂ)}|ω ∧ ω̄| for a Néron differential ω.
items.note: GZ.8: "Specialize to X₀(N), a rational elliptic modular quotient ... keeping unit-group factors, discriminants, degrees and Manin constants. Compare trace-normalized and averaged Heegner points and the existing elliptic height"; BSD.5: "use ... the Gross–Zagier/period/index comparison at rank one". Checked the constant: Chap. I (6.3) with χ = 1 has ĥ over H; ĥ_H = h·ĥ_K (Chap. I (6.4)) cancels the 1/h. Height normalisation hazards (Tau Ceti canonicalHeight = ½ x-height) are recorded in GZ.0 packet nodes GZ.0/x-height-canonical-height and GZ.0/bsd-height-pairing.

items.name: BSD prediction for E over K (quoted conjecture, [35])
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. Assume P_K has infinite order (so L′(E/K,1) ≠ 0). BSD predicts rank E(K) = 1 and L′(E/K, 1) = ‖ω‖²·m²·ĥ(P_K)·|Ш_K| / (|D|^{1/2}·[E(K) : ℤP_K]²), where for a place 𝔭 | N of K, m_𝔭 = order of the group of connected components of the Néron model of E over O_𝔭; as p = 𝔭𝔭̄ is split, m_𝔭 = m_𝔭̄ =: m_p and m_𝔭m_𝔭̄ = m_p²; m = ∏_{p|N} m_p; Ш_K = Ш(E/K), conjecturally finite, and then of square order [35].
items.note: Arithmetic side planned in Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7 (stretch): "assuming Ш(E/K) finite the arithmetic side of BSD is definable: the BSD quotient Ω(E)·Reg(E/K)·#Ш(E/K)·∏_p c_p/#E(K)_tors²"; BSD.5: "Define the rational BSD defect as the analytic leading term divided by the arithmetic expression" (over ℚ); BSD.1 relates invariants under quadratic base change. Note: m_p must be read as the Tamagawa number c_p = #Φ(𝔽_p) (for p split, E over K_𝔭 = ℚ_p); Reg/|tors|² = ĥ(P_K)/[E(K):ℤP_K]². 'Ш is a square' (Cassels) is not separately planned.

items.name: (2.2) Conjecture: the Heegner index formula
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. If P_K has infinite order in E(K), then it generates a subgroup of finite index and [E(K) : ℤP_K] = c·m·u_K·|Ш_K|^{1/2}. (Given Theorem (2.1) this is equivalent to the BSD formula over K in rank 1. It is independent of the parametrization: for another π′, n′_E∘π′ = n_E∘π with integers n, n′ ≥ 1, so n′c′ = nc and n′P′_K = nP_K; henceforth π is taken of minimal degree, which minimizes the index of ℤP_K.)
items.note: BSD.5 ("Rational leading-term quotient and Heegner index formula"): "Relate the height of a non-torsion Heegner point to the squared index of its class in the rank-one lattice, with torsion and rational-versus-quadratic regulator factors"; HE.6: "prove the length bound by the index of the bottom class". Planned is the equivalence with BSD and one-sided bounds; the conjecture itself is open in general (p-parts under hypotheses in RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6).

items.name: (2.3) Conjecture and the divisibility of the index by t = |E(ℚ)_tors|
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. The index of ℤP_K in E(K) is divisible by t = |E(ℚ)_tors| (when P_K has infinite order), so (2.2) implies: (2.3) if E(K) has rank 1, then c·m·u_K·|Ш_K|^{1/2} is divisible by t. (Meaningful without finiteness of Ш_K: for divisibility by n one may replace Ш_K by its n-torsion, which is finite.)
items.note: No stage. (Implicitly (2.3) also needs P_K of infinite order, i.e. rank 1 together with L′(E/K,1) ≠ 0; the paper's phrasing relies on BSD for that step.) Routed (source) to RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5.

items.name: Examples N = 11 and N = 65; Kramer's 2-Selmer bound (quoted [22])
items.statement: Values (E; c, m, t): N = 11: (E₀ = J₀(11); 1, 5, 5), (E₀/μ₅ = J₁(11); 5, 1, 5), (E₀/(ℤ/5ℤ); 1, 1, 1). N = 65 = 5·13: (E₀ = J₀(65)/<w₅, w₁₃>; 1, 1, 2), (E₀/(ℤ/2ℤ); 1, 4, 2). For E = E₀ of level 65, (2.3) predicts: if K is imaginary quadratic with 5 and 13 split then (a) K = ℚ(i) (u_K = 2), or (b) Ш(E/K)₂ ≠ 0, or (c) rank E(K) > 1. Using Kramer [22] one shows that for K ≠ ℚ(i) the 2-Selmer group of E over K has ℤ/2ℤ-rank ≥ 4, so (b) or (c) holds.
items.note: Checked against LMFDB: 65a1 (optimal, [1,0,0,−1,0]) has c₅ = c₁₃ = 1, torsion ℤ/2, Manin constant 1; 65a2 has Tamagawa product 4 = 2·2, torsion ℤ/2. N = 11 values agree with the known data (11a1: c₁₁ = 5, torsion 5; 11a3 = X₁(11): c₁₁ = 1, torsion 5; 11a2: trivial torsion). Note K = ℚ(i) (D = −4) is outside the paper's standing D odd, so (a) is only meaningful for the conjecture. The Kramer computation is not reproduced. No stage. Routed (source) to RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5.

items.name: The quadratic twist E′ of E by K
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. E′ is the twist of E by K: if y² = x³ + ax + b is a Weierstrass equation for E, E′ is Dy² = x³ + ax + b.
items.note: tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwist (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/QuadraticTwist.lean:451): quadraticTwist (E : WeierstrassCurve K) (L) [Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] : WeierstrassCurve K, the twist by the trace and norm of a generator of L/K; different generators give isomorphic models (exists_smul_quadraticTwist_eq, :488), so for L = ℚ(√D) it is ℚ-isomorphic to Dy² = x³ + ax + b. Also tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistPointEquiv (:809) identifies points of the twist with the (−1)-eigenspace. The L-function identity L_ε(f,s) = L(E′,s) is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/290 (planned, BSD.0).

items.name: Rationality of L(E′, 1)/Ω′ by modular symbols (quoted [25])
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. L(E′, 1) = α′·Ω′, where Ω′ is the fundamental real period of the Néron differential ω′ = ω/√|D| on E′ and α′ ∈ ℚ (non-zero by the choice of K).
items.note: BSD.5: "use modular-symbol rationality at rank zero"; L1: "Prove algebraicity of the period-normalized values". (Whether ω/√|D| is exactly the Néron differential of E′ at 2 and at primes dividing D is glossed; only rational factors are affected.)

items.name: Period identity ‖ω‖²/|D|^{1/2} = [E(ℝ) : E(ℝ)⁰]·Ω·Ω′
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. With Ω the fundamental real period of ω on E and Ω′ that of ω′ on E′: ‖ω‖²/|D|^{1/2} = [E(ℝ) : E(ℝ)⁰]·Ω·Ω′.
items.note: BSD.1: "Relate component groups, minimal differentials and periods under quadratic base change and twist"; GZ.0 packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/real-period-components (Ω⁰ least positive real period, c∞ = #π₀(E(ℝ))). Checked for both lattice shapes (Δ > 0 rectangular: ‖ω‖² = 2ω₁|ω₂|, Ω′ = |ω₂|/√|D|, index 2; Δ < 0: ‖ω‖² = ω₁|ω₂|, index 1).

items.name: Modular abelian variety A_f and (2.4) L(A/ℚ, s) = ∏ L(f^α, s)
items.statement: Let f = Σ a_n q^n be a Hecke eigenform of weight 2 and level N whose coefficients generate a totally real field M_f of degree m (f lies in an m-dimensional irreducible representation of the Hecke algebra over ℚ). One associates to f an m-dimensional abelian variety A₀/ℚ, a quotient of J₀(N); for A₀ or any A isogenous to A₀ over ℚ, (2.4) L(A/ℚ, s) = ∏_{α: M_f ↪ ℝ} L(f^α, s).
items.note: R14.5: "For a normalised cuspidal newform f of weight exactly two ... construct its Hecke ideal and the quotient A_f of J₁(N), or J₀(N) for trivial character, as an abelian variety over Q. Prove its dimension equals the degree of the coefficient field"; the L-identity needs the Galois representation of A_f (R14.5 defers it: "Proving that comparison belongs to AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1/R19.6"). The equality of L-functions itself is not named; partial.

items.name: Consequences for A_f: order of vanishing m or ≥ 3m, rank ≥ m, BSD up to ℚ^×
items.statement: In the setting of (2.4) assume f|w_N = f (sign −1). Then ord_{s=1} L(A/ℚ, s) is m or ≥ 3m according as L′(f, 1) ≠ 0 or = 0 (Cor. (1.3)); if it is m, then L^{(m)}(A/ℚ, 1) = m!·∏_α L′(f^α, 1) (printed without m! and with s for 1; issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E52). Imitating m = 1: ord_{s=1} L(A/ℚ, s) = m implies rk A(ℚ) ≥ m (A(ℚ) ⊗ ℝ contains the m-dimensional span of the c_{1,f^α}), and if equality holds the BSD formula for L^{(m)}(A/ℚ, 1) is true up to a non-zero rational multiple.
items.note: Only sketched in the paper ("We now imitate the argument"). Not planned: GZ.8 plans heights for strict GL₂-type A ("A totally real extension concerns the precise parametrized strict-GL₂-type abelian variety and coefficient-character component") and HE.7 the Kolyvagin–Logachev RM extension, but no stage states the rank ≥ m / BSD-up-to-ℚ^× conclusion for A_f over ℚ. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: Generalized setting: the set S, the quaternion algebra B, the order R and the embedding ι: K → B
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; k = 1. Let S = {p prime : ord_p(N) odd, ε(p) = −1}; then (−1)^{|S|} = ε(N). If |S| is even (L_𝒜(f,s) has an odd-order zero at s = 1), B is the indefinite quaternion algebra over ℚ ramified exactly at S; if |S| is odd, B is the definite quaternion algebra ramified at S ∪ {∞}. Every prime ramified in B is inert in K, so there is an embedding ι: K → B. R is an order of B containing ι(O_K) with reduced discriminant N; such orders exist [15]; they are unique up to conjugacy in the indefinite case and fall into finitely many conjugacy classes in the definite case. Γ = R^×/{±1} is a discrete subgroup of G = (B ⊗ ℝ)^×/ℝ^×.
items.note: HE.1: "For quaternionic curves construct optimal embeddings of the specified orders and their CM points in the same canonical tower. Prove the local embedding conditions"; R18.1 applies ShimuraData to a quaternion algebra. The non-Eichler orders of reduced discriminant N when ε(p) = −1 (and the existence reference [15]) are not specifically named.

items.name: Shimura curves: canonical model, Hecke correspondences and Heegner points (quoted: Shimura [32])
items.statement: Indefinite case: G ≅ PGL₂(ℝ), Γ⁺ = Γ ∩ PGL₂⁺(ℝ) is a Fuchsian group acting on ℌ; if (3.1) (ε(p) = 1 for all p | N) holds then Γ⁺ ≅ Γ₀(N); Γ⁺\ℌ is an algebraic curve over ℂ, complete iff S ≠ ∅. It has a canonical model X over ℚ, characterized by the fields of rationality of its special points, with a modular description as coarse moduli of polarized abelian surfaces with endomorphisms by R. The Hecke correspondences are rational over ℚ and determine the zeta function. ι|_O gives a Heegner point x of discriminant D on X rational over H; Pic(O) acts freely on the Heegner points of discriminant D, via Gal(H/K) by Shimura's reciprocity law.
items.note: R18.1: "Apply ShimuraData and ShimuraVarieties to a quaternion algebra over a totally real field split at one specified real place, constructing its canonical Shimura curve and complex uniformization"; HE.1: "prove descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication and the canonical-model reciprocity law".

items.name: Generalized main identity, indefinite case (announced; proof in a later paper)
items.statement: With B indefinite (|S| even, ε(N) = 1, k = 1) and X, x as above: the coefficients a_{m,𝒜} of Theorem (6.9) of Chap. IV are a fixed multiple of <x, T_m x^{σ_𝒜}>, <,> the Néron–Tate height pairing on Pic(X). The constant κ = −12 N^{−1} ∏_{p|N}(1 + ε(p)/p)^{−1} of (6.9) arises, as in Chap. II (2.13), as the residue at s = 1 of the resolvent kernel function G_s of X(ℂ).
items.note: GZ.8: "Specialize to X₀(N), a rational elliptic modular quotient, generalized-Heegner quaternionic curves and finite ring-class characters". The residue statement for κ is consistent with vol(Γ⁺\ℌ) (local unit indices N_p(1 + ε(p)/p)), my check; not separately planned.

items.name: Definite case: the curve X = ⊔ Γ_i\Y, Brandt matrices, Heegner points and the height pairing
items.statement: Definite case: G ≅ SO₃(ℝ) ⊂ PGL₂(ℂ) and Γ is finite, acting on ℙ¹(ℂ); Γ\ℙ¹(ℂ) has the canonical model Γ\Y over ℚ, Y the genus-0 curve over ℚ attached to B. For Hecke operators take X = ⊔_{i=1}^n Γ_i\Y, n = class number of R, Γ_i = projective unit group of the right order of the i-th left ideal class (an adelic double coset space). The Hecke algebra acts on Pic(X) ≅ ℤ^n by the Brandt matrices [16]. ι gives a Heegner point x of discriminant D on X, defined over K; Pic(O) acts freely on such points. Height pairing on Pic(X): <x, y> = 0 if x, y lie on different components, and <x, y> = |Γ_i| if both lie on Γ_i\Y.
items.note: R18.3: "Define algebraic automorphic forms on the finite double-coset set with their weight module and integral coefficients. Prove finiteness, the Hecke action, change of level". The Brandt-matrix identification and this particular pairing (Gross's) are not named; partial.

items.name: Definite main identity and the special-value formula for L(f, χ, 1) (announced; N prime, ε(N) = −1 in [16])
items.statement: In the definite case (|S| odd, ε(N) = −1, k = 1): the coefficients b_{m,𝒜} of Theorem (5.6) of Chap. IV are fixed multiples of Σ_{ℬ∈Pic(O)} <x_ℬ, T_m x_{ℬ𝒜}>. An argument as in §1 then relates L(f, χ, 1) and <x_{χ,f}, x_{χ,f}> for a newform f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) and χ: Cl_K → ℂ^×, x_{χ,f} the (χ, f)-eigencomponent.
items.note: GZ.5: "Establish the Waldspurger period formula for the stated GL₂/quaternionic toric data ... Export the explicit split, ramified and definite-quaternionic specializations needed by Euler-system and level-raising consumers". This is the classical form of that specialization (Gross's formula); the explicit Brandt-module form is not named.

items.name: Waldspurger–Vignéras: L(f, 1_K, 1) is proportional to a square in M_f
items.statement: In the definite setting, since x_{1,f} lies in a fixed one-dimensional space as K varies, the theorem of Waldspurger and Vignéras (cf. [36]) that L(f, 1_K, 1) is proportional to the square of an element of M_f (M_f = field of Fourier coefficients of f) follows immediately.
items.note: Not stated in any stage; nearest GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 (Waldspurger formula) and RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.2. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5.

items.name: Closed formula for γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) (Chap. II Prop. (5.8) rewritten with Chap. IV Prop. (4.6a))
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). For s ∈ ℂ and m ∈ ℕ prime to N, γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) = Σ_{τ∈G} G^m_{N,s}(x^τ, x^{τσ}), where x is a Heegner point of discriminant D, σ ∈ G ↔ 𝒜, G^m_{N,s} = G_{N,s}|T_m and G_{N,s} is the resolvent kernel function for Γ₀(N) (when r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0 some terms are infinite and γ^m_{N,s} is modified as in Chap. II §5). Then γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) = −2u² Σ_{n≥1} σ_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) + 2hu r_𝒜(m)((Γ′/Γ)(s) − log 2π + ½ log|D| + (L′/L)(1, ε)).
items.note: No resolvent kernel G_{N,s} in either library. For s = 1 the archimedean local height is covered by method in GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7 (Green functions); higher s = k is not planned anywhere. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: (4.1) Theorem and (4.2): higher-weight analogue of the main identity
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). There is a holomorphic cusp form Φ = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,𝒜} q^m ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (printed 'm ≦ 1', issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E53) with L′_𝒜(f, k) = (2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!·√|D|))·(f, Φ) for all f ∈ S^{new}_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), and for m prime to N: (4.2) a_{m,𝒜} = (m^{k−1}/u²) γ^m_{N,k}(𝒜) + (h/u) r_𝒜(m) m^{k−1} log(N/m) − m^{k−1} Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)), P_{k−1} the (k−1)-st Legendre polynomial. Since P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) ∈ ℚ and σ′_𝒜(n) is a non-negative even integral multiple of the logarithm of a single prime (remark after Chap. IV Prop. (4.6)), (4.2) writes a_{m,𝒜} as a finite sum of values of G^m_{N,k} at Heegner points plus a rational combination of logarithms of primes.
items.note: Checked: substituting the γ^m_{N,k} formula (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/311) into (4.2) reproduces a_{m,𝒜} of Chap. IV Theorem (5.8). No stage plans the higher-weight Gross–Zagier formula (S.-W. Zhang's heights of Heegner cycles); GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.0-GH.8 plan Kuga–Sato and generalized Heegner cycles with étale/p-adic Abel–Jacobi and BDP/Castella–Hsieh p-adic formulas, not complex heights or this identity. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Deligne's Heegner vectors and height pairing (reported, unpublished)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). Deligne defined Heegner vectors s_x in the stalks above Heegner points x of the local coefficient system Sym^{2k−2}(H¹) (H¹ = first cohomology of the universal elliptic curve over X₀(N)) and a height pairing <,> with <s_x, T_m s_{x^σ}> = a_{m,𝒜}; the pairing is defined as a sum of local heights characterized by axioms similar to Chap. I §4, computed by intersection theory at finite places and by values of an eigenfunction of the Laplacian (namely G_{N,k}) at archimedean places. The definitions extend to the curves of §3 (Sym^{2k−2}(H¹) replaced by Γ⁺\ℌ × W or ⊔_i Γ_i\(ℙ¹(ℂ) × W), W the unique (2k−1)-dimensional irreducible representation of B^×/ℚ^×), giving formulas for heights of Heegner vectors in terms of L_𝒜(f, k) or L′_𝒜(f, k). The global meaning of the sum of local heights (e.g. when it vanishes) was not understood.
items.note: Nearest plans: GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.0 ("Construct the relevant desingularized fiber powers of the universal elliptic curve") and GH.1 ("Form generalized Heegner cycles ... Construct the étale Abel–Jacobi map"); neither plans an archimedean/complex height pairing of Heegner cycles. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Relations λ for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)); G_{N,k,λ} and γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). A relation for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) is a sequence λ = {λ_m}_{m≥1} with (i) λ_m ∈ ℤ, λ_m = 0 for all but finitely many m; (ii) Σ_{m≥1} λ_m a_m = 0 for every cusp form Σ a_m q^m ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)); (iii) λ_m = 0 for m not prime to N. Put G_{N,k,λ}(z₁, z₂) = Σ_{m≥1} λ_m m^{k−1} G^m_{N,k}(z₁, z₂) and γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) = Σ_{m≥1} m^{k−1} λ_m γ^m_{N,k}(𝒜) = Σ_{τ∈G} G_{N,k,λ}(x^τ, x^{τσ}). (If S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) = 0 every a_{m,𝒜} vanishes and (4.2) gives γ^m_{N,k}(𝒜) directly.)
items.note: Depends on the resolvent kernel (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/311); no library or stage counterpart. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: (4.3) Corollary: γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) is a rational combination of logarithms of primes
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). Let λ be a relation for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) and 𝒜 an ideal class of K. Then γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) = Σ_{m>0} λ_m m^{k−1} hu r_𝒜(m) log(m/N) + u² Σ_{m,n∈ℤ, m|D| ≥ nN > 0} λ_m m^{k−1} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)). In particular exp((D^{k−1}/u²)·γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜)) is a rational number, and in fact a rational square unless |D| is prime.
items.locator: Chapter V, §4, (4.3) Corollary and proof, pp. 316-317
items.note: Formula checked from (4.2) and Σλ_m a_{m,𝒜} = 0. Integrality step: (m|D|)^{k−1}P_{k−1}(1 − 2t·…) ∈ ℤ because P_n(1 − 2t) has integer coefficients; this polynomial is mathlib:Polynomial.shiftedLegendre n (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/ShiftedLegendre.lean:40, coefficients (−1)^k C(n,k) C(n+k,n) by coeff_shiftedLegendre :84), but Mathlib has no identification with the classical Legendre polynomial. Two misprints in statement/proof: PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E54, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E55. No stage. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Weight 2 (k = 1): G_{N,1,λ} at Heegner points are logarithms of absolute values of algebraic numbers in H
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; (3.1). For k = 1 the terms G_{N,1,λ}(x^τ, x^{στ}) are the archimedean local height pairings of Σ_m λ_m T_m((x) − (∞)) and (x^σ) − (0) (Chap. II). Since the Hecke action on J₀(N) is the same as on S₂(Γ₀(N)), a relation λ for S₂(Γ₀(N)) makes Σ_m λ_m T_m 𝔞 principal for every degree-0 divisor 𝔞; in particular Σ_m λ_m T_m((x) − (∞)) = (φ) with φ a rational function on X₀(N) over H, and the local height axioms give <Σ_{m≥1} λ_m T_m((x) − (∞)), (x^σ) − (0)>_v = log|φ(x^σ)/φ(0)|_v for every place v of H. Hence the G_{N,1,λ}(x^τ, x^{στ}) are logarithms of absolute values of the conjugates of an algebraic number of H.
items.note: The principal-divisor axiom of local heights is part of GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.2 ("Export local height decomposition, base-change and correspondence-adjunction APIs"); the conclusion is not named. Uses Σλ_m T_m = 0 in 𝕋 (perfect pairing, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/277). Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: (4.4) Conjecture: algebraicity of higher Green's functions at Heegner points (and its refined form)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). Let λ be a relation for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), fix a Heegner point x and an embedding H ↪ ℂ. Then there is α ∈ H^× with G_{N,k,λ}(x^τ, x^{στ}) = u² D^{1−k} log|α^τ| for all τ ∈ G = Gal(H/K). Refined form (stated informally): the expression (4.3) for γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) predicts the ideal generated by α, hence α up to a unit, and with (4.4) up to a root of unity.
items.note: Compatible with (4.3): summing over τ gives (u²D^{1−k}/2) log|N_{H/ℚ} α|. No stage plans it (searched atlas for Green function / algebraicity / CM value: only GZ.2/GZ.7 archimedean Green kernels for weight 2). Later literature treats this conjecture (e.g. Viazovska; Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang; Y. Li); not reviewed here. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: (4.5) Fourier expansion of G(z) = G_{1,2}(z, z) (stated; proof deferred)
items.statement: For N = 1, k = 2, with G(z) = G_{1,2}(z, z) defined by the limiting procedure of Chap. II §5: G(x + iy) = −(2π/3) y − (119 ζ(3)/(2π²)) y^{−2} + (8 − 480/(πy) − 240/(π²y²)) e^{−2πy} cos 2πx − (282876 + 283968/(πy) + 70992/(π²y²)) e^{−4πy} cos 4πx + O(e^{−6πy}), with an O-constant of about 10⁸.
items.note: Checked numerically for consistency with the stated values (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/319): residuals 1.1e−3 (D = −7), 1.1e−19 (D = −43), 1.8e−40 (D = −163), each within the stated tail 10⁸·e^{−6πy}. No stage. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Numerical examples of (4.3) and (4.4) (D = −p, N = 1, k = 2, λ = (1, 0, 0, …))
items.statement: D = −p with p > 3 prime, p ≡ 3 (mod 4), 𝒜 = [O], N = 1, k = 2, λ = (1, 0, 0, …) (a relation since S₄(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0): γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) = Σ_z G(z) over the h(−p) points z ∈ ℌ/SL₂(ℤ) satisfying a quadratic equation of discriminant −p. For h(−p) = 1: G((1+i√7)/2) = −log 7 − 2 log 3 − (12/7) log 5; G((1+i√43)/2) = −log 43 + (2/43) log(5⁶·7²⁹/(2¹²⁷·3⁵⁴)); G((1+i√163)/2) = −log 163 + (2/163) log(2²³³·5⁶·7³⁷·19¹²⁵/(3¹⁶³·11³⁵·23⁴²·29¹³⁸·127⁹¹)). For p = 31 (h = 3): G((1+i√31)/2) + G((1+i√31)/4) + G((−1+i√31)/4) = −log 31 − (2/31) log(3¹¹⁶·11⁸·23³⁰·17⁶), and the refined (4.4) predicts G((1+i√31)/2) = −log π₃₁ − (2/31) log(π₃⁵⁴π₉³¹π₁₂₁¹³π₁₇⁶π₂₃³⁰/(π₁₁¹⁸θⁿ)) for some n ∈ ℤ, θ ≈ 1.465571232 the real root of θ³ − θ² − 1 = 0, π₃ = θ + 1, π₉ = 3/π₃, π₁₁ = 3θ − 4, π₁₂₁ = 11/π₁₁, π₁₇ = −θ + 3, π₂₃ = −3θ + 5, π₃₁ = 3θ + 1 in ℚ(θ) = ℚ(j((1+√−31)/2)), the real subfield of the Hilbert class field of ℚ(√−31); this holds numerically to ≥ 15 decimal places with n = 61.
items.note: Verified with mpmath (40 digits) using (4.5): D = −43 agrees to 1.1e−19 and D = −163 to 1.8e−40; D = −7 to 1.1e−3 and the p = 31 sum to 5.3e−5, both within the tail bound for y = √7/2, √31/4. The refined p = 31 prediction holds to 1.2e−15 with n = 61, and the best real n is 60.99999999999995. Norms of the π_q were checked from θ³ − θ² − 1 (N(π_q) = q). Exponents read from 4x zooms of p. 318. No stage. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.
